articles.title: WWE SummerSlam 2022: Brock Lesnar lifts ring with tractor, Logan Paul frog splashes The Miz, more highlights
articles.summary: Roman Reigns retained the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship in an epic match with Brock Lesnar -- but it was just one of the many SummerSlam highlights.
articles.body: Roman Reigns, Brock Lesnar, Logan Paul and Bianca Belair were among the WWE superstars who delivered incredible highlights on Saturday night at SummerSlam. Reigns and Lesnar battled in a last-man-standing match for the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship. While Reigns got the better of Lesnar in the match, the two opponents put together a few moments that would be etched into SummerSlam lore. Lesnar would use the tractor he rode into the arena on to lift up the ring and knock Reigns to the floor. He would then F-5 Reigns’ valet, Paul Heyman, through the announcers' table. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM Theory would then rush down to the ring to try to cash-in his Money in the Bank contract and take advantage of both Lesnar and Reigns being down – but to no avail. Theory hit Reigns with the briefcase but was met by an F-5 from Lesnar. Jey and Jimmy Uso then superkicked Lesnar, knocking him out. Reigns smashed the briefcase onto Theory’s back. Reigns would get the win after burying Lesnar underneath the damaged announcers' table. He would retain the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship. In one of the earlier matches, Paul looked to get one over on The Miz. Paul impressed WWE fans in his match. In one of the highlight-reel moments, Paul went off the top rope and completed a frog splash and put The Miz through one of the announcers' tables. WWE LEGEND KURT ANGLE OPENS UP ABOUT JOURNEY TO SUPERSTARDOM, BATTLE WITH ADDICTION: 'I WANT TO HELP OTHERS' Pat McAfee, former NFL punter-turned-WWE personality, was also thrust into a match against Happy Corbin. The two were teammates at one time on the Indianapolis Colts. McAfee used a low blow and a sunset flip from the middle rope to beat Corbin. Belair and Becky Lynch continued their feud in a match for the RAW Women’s Championship. The two put together another epic battle, which ended with Belair hitting the K.O.D. on Lynch and pinning her to retain the title. But before both competitors left the ring, the WWE Universe got a surprise return from Bayley. The former women’s champion returned to the ring following a torn ACL in 2021. She came out with Dakota Kai and IYO SKY. Cooler heads would prevail, however, as no skirmish was initiated. Edge also returned to the ring at SummerSlam. Weeks after being disposed as the leader of The Judgment Day, Edge returned to the ring to confront his former faction mates during their match against The Mysterios. Rey and Dominik Mysterio took on Finn Balor and Damien Priest in a no disqualification tag-team match. Edge made his return and speared Balor and Priest. The interference allowed the Mysterios to win the match. Edge’s return came after vignettes had played during RAW alluding to his return. CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP SummerSlam results

articles.title: Bloodied Ric Flair wins 'last match' in front of family, WWE legends
articles.summary: Ric Flair headlined one final main event on Sunday in a tag-team match with his son-in-law, and AEW star, Andrade to go against Jeff Jarrett and Jay Lethal.
articles.body: Pro wrestling legend Ric Flair performed Sunday in what was billed as his "last match" in the industry. Flair teamed up with his son-in-law Andrade El Idolo to take on Jay Lethal and Jeff Jarrett in Nashville, Tennessee. The match was a part of a Jim Crockett Promotions event. "The Nature Boy" was busted open during the match, openly bleeding down his face. Jarrett would try to hit Flair with his signature cheat code – a guitar shot – but missed and hit his partner instead. Flair was passed brass knuckles and delivered a shot to Jarrett. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM Flair would put Jarrett in the figure-four leglock. Jarrett would be down the for the three-count. "I had one of my best matches of my career here with Ricky Steamboat," the 73-year-old said afterward, via ESPN. "All my family is here. We made jokes about me being married five times. All the kids are here. One wife, but all my granddaughters. My friends are here. I swear to God, guys. If I didn't have enough pressure on me tonight, f---ing Kid Rock walked into the locker room tonight." Flair last performed in 2011. He was helped out of the ring by Andrade, an AEW star who is married to WWE star Charlotte Flair. Flair blew kisses to the crowd as he walked up the ramp. WWE LEGEND KURT ANGLE OPENS UP ABOUT JOURNEY TO SUPERSTARDOM, BATTLE WITH ADDICTION: 'I WANT TO HELP OTHERS' He was also greeted by Bret Hart, Mick Foley and The Undertaker. All three WWE Hall of Famers were sitting ringside. Jarrett, a standout in the pro wrestling industry and WWE Hall of Famer in his own right, was also emotional after the match. "It's his last one. If anything goes wrong, it's on me. It's on others. I'm so damn happy for Ric, I don't know what to say. ... As a spectator, y'all watched it and went home tonight," Jarrett said. "When you're participating, it's a whole other level of pressure that I've never been under." Flair’s wrestling career spanned about six decades. He was one of the first big stars to crossover and draw mainstream interest with his "Woo!" catchphrase and lavish robes. CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP Flair got started in American Wrestling Association and later competed in WWE, World Championship Wrestling, New Japan Pro Wrestling, Total Non-Stop Action and more. He wraps up his in-ring career as a 16-time world champion and two-time WWE Hall of Famer.

articles.title: Notifications, social media and more with BBC Sport
articles.summary: With latest scores and headlines sent straight to your device, personalisation and much more, ensure you have a great sporting life with BBC Sport.
articles.body:
Want all the biggest sports news, analysis and scores sent direct to your phone or tablet? Then download the BBC Sport app.

The app also comes with all our website content along with a radio player, Chromecast integration, a widget and personalised menu options. It's free and easy to download - simply head to the relevant link below:

Download the BBC Sport app: Apple , external - Android , external - Amazon , external

The BBC Sport app offers two types of notification.

With news notifications you can have the biggest sport stories and the best content right at your fingertips. Stay in the know by picking from our offering of top sport headlines, football news - including the biggest updates, features and analysis on your Premier League, Championship and Scottish Premiership club - and news from nine other major sports, as well as the best from each nation of the United Kingdom. You can also sign up to get alerts to our latest Insight in-depth features.

You can also follow your team from wherever you are with our massive range of event notifications. We offer notifications across five sports - football, cricket, Formula 1, rugby union and rugby league - covering every major moment. Line-ups, kick-offs, and half-time scores, goals, wickets, tries and conversions, results and times on the wave of the chequered flag. We serve more than 400 teams, with more to come.

articles.title: What's the difference between racing Indy 500 and Daytona 500? Drivers explain
articles.summary: What's the difference between racing the Indianapolis 500 and the Daytona 500? Drivers who have tried both explain.
articles.body: They are the signature spectacles in each racing series, the Indianapolis 500 and all its pageantry with more than a century of tradition and milk drinking in open-wheel racing, and the Daytona 500, NASCAR’s season-opener run under the Florida sun at the unofficial home of the "birthplace of speed." Indy and Daytona. Just say the city names to even casual sports fans, and they'll surely know each of them as two of the biggest dates — for sure, two of the biggest parties — in American racing. They are united by four wheels, 500 miles on a 2.5-mile track, and raucous crowds of 100,000-plus fans that spill into Indy's Snake Pit and Daytona's Tent City. And, well, not much else. "They’re two completely different concepts of racing and I think people don’t really understand the differences," said Juan Pablo Montoya, a two-time Indy 500 champion with seven starts in the Daytona 500. Montoya is one of the handful of elite drivers to attempt racing in both the Indianapolis 500 and the Daytona 500. This year's Daytona 500 field is dotted with drivers who have tried both, including seven-time NASCAR champion Jimmie Johnson, AJ Allmendinger, Kyle Larson and even a Daytona 500 rookie in four-time Indy 500 champion Helio Castroneves. While a longshot, the Brazilian star is attempting to match A.J. Foyt and Mario Andretti as the only drivers to win the Indy 500 and the Daytona 500. [Read more: 2025 IndyCar Championship odds: Alex Palou favored] Castroneves will have some help in the draft — the tricky mix of downforce and drag — from three other teammates at Trackhouse Racing. "I think the main difference is, they’re both unique to survive," Montoya said. "The factor with NASCAR that makes it really difficult is that you not only depend on yourself to win the race, you depend on your teammates pushing you, your friends. Having the teammates close to you at the right time makes a bigger difference than anything else." Here's what some of this year's drivers who steeled their nerves over 500 miles in both races have to say about the challenges of them both — and how Castroneves might fare in Sunday's race. Jimmie Johnson "The race itself and the ways the cars behave in the draft are so different. I’m very curious to see what Helio thinks as he gets more experience on the track. In IndyCar, the tow is just mind-blowing how much it helps cars pick up speed. A tow in the stock car is minimal. All the energy comes from behind the push. Really just different dynamics." Johnson is a two-time Daytona 500 winner and the 2022 rookie of the year at the Indianapolis 500. Kyle Larson On the crowd: "Both atmospheres are really good, for sure. I don’t know. They’re still, like, very different. Like, it’s hard to answer that because they’re both the peak of the sport. They just have their differences. "The infield at Indy has the Snake Pit, but the infield here has all the campers, and that’s really cool. Driver intros [are] sort of similar. The crowd feels closer to you at Indy, at least the grandstand crowd. The frontstretch at Indy is swarmed with people. But pit road is also similar to that here. But it’s more race fans. I don’t know. I feel like maybe Indy just has like a little bit more of the kind of history feel to it than the 500, Daytona 500. Other than that, I mean, they’re both great. The atmospheres at both of them were great." [Read more: FOX Sports announces inaugural broadcast crew for IndyCar coverage] On the cars: "I think the challenging part potentially is just probably the weaker brakes. You don’t slow down as good as you would in IndyCar for like a green-flag pit cycle. Maximizing time for the green-flag ins-and-outs, that’s where it’s going to be probably a challenge. Too, at Indy, it’s so narrow, y’all just follow each other. Here it’s like you’re trying to pass people, braking and stuff. That’s probably where he’ll get a little bit maybe overwhelmed at times. But he’ll get the hang of it. It’s not a big deal. He’ll be fine." Larson is NASCAR's 2021 Cup Series champion, competed in the Indy 500 last year and will return this May. AJ Allmendinger On the cars: "Where do you start, I guess? I think when it comes to the Daytona 500, just that pack racing, right? You’re constantly side-by-side. The Indy 500, the year I ran it, the way the aero was, you make big runs and stuff, but you’re not side-by-side constantly. I think that to me is the bigger difference of the way you race those races. You have to be pinpoint accurate in either car. The consequences are really high in both cars if you make a mistake. I think the stress of not having to be side-by-side at the Indy 500 constantly is a little bit easier. But you’re also running 50 miles-per-hour quicker." On the crowd: "We all love motorsports. There [are] a handful of races you can say to somebody that’s not a motorsports person and they know exactly what it is. These two races, you could argue the four biggest races in the world. You could put up Monaco, you could put up Le Mans, maybe. The energy of this race as you build up to it and as you walk out, and they announce you, at least for me, it’s the same emotion for sure." Allmendinger finished third in the 2009 and 2017 Daytona 500s, and was seventh in the 2013 Indy 500 and leading until he was forced to pit because his seat belt became undone. Reporting by The Associated Press. Jimmie Johnson "The race itself and the ways the cars behave in the draft are so different. I’m very curious to see what Helio thinks as he gets more experience on the track. In IndyCar, the tow is just mind-blowing how much it helps cars pick up speed. A tow in the stock car is minimal. All the energy comes from behind the push. Really just different dynamics." Johnson is a two-time Daytona 500 winner and the 2022 rookie of the year at the Indianapolis 500. Kyle Larson On the crowd: "Both atmospheres are really good, for sure. I don’t know. They’re still, like, very different. Like, it’s hard to answer that because they’re both the peak of the sport. They just have their differences. "The infield at Indy has the Snake Pit, but the infield here has all the campers, and that’s really cool. Driver intros [are] sort of similar. The crowd feels closer to you at Indy, at least the grandstand crowd. The frontstretch at Indy is swarmed with people. But pit road is also similar to that here. But it’s more race fans. I don’t know. I feel like maybe Indy just has like a little bit more of the kind of history feel to it than the 500, Daytona 500. Other than that, I mean, they’re both great. The atmospheres at both of them were great." [Read more: FOX Sports announces inaugural broadcast crew for IndyCar coverage] On the cars: "I think the challenging part potentially is just probably the weaker brakes. You don’t slow down as good as you would in IndyCar for like a green-flag pit cycle. Maximizing time for the green-flag ins-and-outs, that’s where it’s going to be probably a challenge. Too, at Indy, it’s so narrow, y’all just follow each other. Here it’s like you’re trying to pass people, braking and stuff. That’s probably where he’ll get a little bit maybe overwhelmed at times. But he’ll get the hang of it. It’s not a big deal. He’ll be fine." Larson is NASCAR's 2021 Cup Series champion, competed in the Indy 500 last year and will return this May. AJ Allmendinger On the cars: "Where do you start, I guess? I think when it comes to the Daytona 500, just that pack racing, right? You’re constantly side-by-side. The Indy 500, the year I ran it, the way the aero was, you make big runs and stuff, but you’re not side-by-side constantly. I think that to me is the bigger difference of the way you race those races. You have to be pinpoint accurate in either car. The consequences are really high in both cars if you make a mistake. I think the stress of not having to be side-by-side at the Indy 500 constantly is a little bit easier. But you’re also running 50 miles-per-hour quicker." On the crowd: "We all love motorsports. There [are] a handful of races you can say to somebody that’s not a motorsports person and they know exactly what it is. These two races, you could argue the four biggest races in the world. You could put up Monaco, you could put up Le Mans, maybe. The energy of this race as you build up to it and as you walk out, and they announce you, at least for me, it’s the same emotion for sure." Allmendinger finished third in the 2009 and 2017 Daytona 500s, and was seventh in the 2013 Indy 500 and leading until he was forced to pit because his seat belt became undone. articles.title: Ranking the 10 best starting pitchers in MLB for 2025
articles.summary: Let's dive into the top 10 starters heading into the 2025 MLB season.
articles.body: Buckle up: Over the next two weeks, we're ranking baseball's best players at every position. Our eight-part series begins with starting pitchers, where a reigning Rookie of the Year looks to build off his success and a former Cy Young winner makes a comeback.  Let's dive into the top 10 starters heading into the 2025 season. 2025 Best MLB Catchers 10. Jacob deGrom, RHP, Texas Rangers 2024: Returned from Tommy John surgery for three September starts (10.2 IP, 1.69 ERA, 14 Ks)2025 ZiPS: 3-1, 51 IP, 3.13 ERA, 69 Ks, 1.4 fWAR There was a lot of back-and-forth about who gets the last spot in our rankings, but a healthy deGrom is not only one of the best pitchers in MLB, he's also a favorite to win the Cy Young award. Of course, the key word for deGrom is always health, and with a lethal triple-digit fastball that he's revamped to top out at 97 mph, this could be deGrom's best shot at winning his third career Cy Young — maybe even solidifying his case for the Hall of Fame in the process. 9. Logan Gilbert, RHP, Seattle Mariners 2024: 9-12, 208 IP, 3.23 ERA, 220 Ks, 4.1 fWAR2025 ZiPS: 12-8, 189 IP, 3.29 ERA, 190 Ks, 3.5 fWAR In an era of way-too-many pitchers being sidelined by major and minor injuries, Gilbert's ability to post is refreshing. He tossed at least 185 innings in each of his last three seasons, featuring an MLB-best 33 starts and a minuscule 4.6% walk rate in 2024. It will be fascinating to see how Gilbert separates himself from the rest of Seattle's Cy Young-caliber arms as he enters his age-28 season. 8. Blake Snell, LHP, Los Angeles Dodgers 2024: 5-3, 104 IP, 3.12 ERA, 145 Ks, 3.1 fWAR2025 ZiPS: 9-5, 133 IP, 3.38 ERA, 176 Ks, 3.1 fWAR It's pretty incredible to think Snell is going for his third career Cy Young award this year — while leading what looks more and more like the best rotation in baseball. Snell's pitchability is never in doubt, but after tossing 150 innings just twice out of his nine years in the big leagues, his durability is. If he can complete his goal of being a workhorse for the Dodgers, then perhaps we can expect Snell to find some consistency as a high-impact starter this year. 7. Logan Webb, RHP, San Francisco Giants 2024: 13-10, 204 IP, 3.47 ERA, 172 Ks, 4.4 fWAR2025 ZiPS: 13-9, 195 IP, 3.22 ERA, 164 Ks, 4.4 fWAR Webb has thrown at least 192 innings and collected Cy Young votes in each of his past three seasons, finally earning his first career All-Star nod last year after recording sub-3.00 ERAs in April and May. The Giants can rely on the 28-year-old to continue limiting home runs and walks — and a .292 BABIP projected by ZiPS would be the best of his career. 6. Chris Sale, LHP, Atlanta Braves 2024: 18-3, 177 IP, 2.38 ERA, 225 Ks, 6.4 fWAR2025 ZiPS: 11-5, 138 IP, 2.98 ERA, 170 Ks, 3.7 fWAR If vintage Sale is here to stay, then there's an argument to be made that he could be ranked even higher on this list. It will be tough for his peers to try and take away his Triple Crown after the renaissance season he put up last year and, even though he's in his age-36 season, there's little reason to believe he won't repeat his electric performance for the Braves. 5. Garrett Crochet, LHP, Boston Red Sox 2024: 6-12, 146 IP, 3.58 ERA, 209 Ks, 4.7 fWAR2025 ZiPS: 12-6, 135 IP, 2.93 ERA, 169 Ks, 4.0 fWAR The pressure is on Crochet to do two things: bring, from Chicago to Boston, the best strikeout rate of last season (35.1%) among pitchers with at least 140 innings pitched, and increase his innings limit. If the southpaw can accomplish that in a full season with the Red Sox, he could threaten Skubal's case to win the AL Cy Young award. 4. Corbin Burnes, RHP, Diamondbacks 2024: 15-9, 194 IP, 2.92 ERA, 181 Ks, 3.7 fWAR2025 ZiPS: 14-7, 181 IP, 2.97 ERA, 179 Ks, 3.8 fWAR The NL got much more challenging for opposing hitters when Burnes decided to take his talents to the desert this winter. Even though his strikeout rate has steadily declined since 2020, Burnes is excellent at making adjustments to his repertoire, including one that led to a 1.29 ERA over his final six starts of 2024. It will be interesting to see how he settles in with the Snakes. 3. Paul Skenes, RHP, Pittsburgh Pirates 2024: 11-3, 133 IP, 1.96 ERA, 170 Ks, 4.3 fWAR2025 ZiPS: 8-6, 151 IP, 3.25 ERA, 181 Ks, 3.7 fWAR After winning the NL Rookie of the Year award and finishing third in Cy Young balloting, what's next for Skenes? Winning the MVP? The 22-year-old could become the first Rookie of the Year pitcher to claim a Cy Young the following season since Dwight Gooden did it in 1985. We're looking forward to Skenes crossing over the 150-innings threshold as he gets ready to pitch a full season in the big leagues this year. 2. Zack Wheeler, RHP, Philadelphia Phillies 2024: 16-7, 200 IP, 2.57 ERA, 224 Ks, 5.4 fWAR2025 ZiPS: 13-7, 175 IP, 3.28 ERA, 184 Ks, 4.2 fWAR Wheeler looked poised to win his first career Cy Young award last season when he recorded personal bests in ERA and WHIP (0.95) before Chris Sale put up a career year of his own. Wheeler leads all major-league pitchers with 24.7 fWAR since 2020, and his experience and durability make him our No. 1 starter in the National League. 1. Tarik Skubal, LHP, Detroit Tigers 2024 stats: 18-4, 192 innings pitched, 2.39 ERA, 228 strikeouts, 5.9 fWAR2025 ZiPS projection: 13-7, 170 IP, 2.74 ERA, 196 Ks, 5.2 fWAR Not only is Skubal the unequivocal leader atop our starting-pitcher rankings, but the 28-year-old ace at the peak of his prime also has a legitimate chance to repeat as the American League Cy Young winner. It will be exciting to watch the southpaw reunite with his 1-2 punch partner in Jack Flaherty as the Tigers hope to make the playoffs in back-to-back seasons for the first time in over a decade. Honorable mentions: Cole Ragans, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dylan Cease, Framber Valdez, Michael King  2025 MLB Positional Rankings Deesha Thosar is a MLB reporter and columnist for FOX Sports. She previously covered the Mets for four years as a beat reporter for the New York Daily News. Follow her on Twitter at @DeeshaThosar.

articles.title: Rugby League Ashes 2025: Fortune favours the brave as England must seize their golden opportunity at Wembley, says Brian Carney
articles.summary: Sky Sports Rugby League's Brian Carney looks ahead to the Ashes; Three Test matches between England and rivals Australia will be held at Wembley Stadium, Everton's new Hill Dickinson Stadium, and Headingley; It marks the return of the Ashes for the first time since 2003
articles.body:
Whenever I think about facing the Kangaroos, I'm drawn to the words of Mark Twain. "It's not the size of the dog in the fight , it's the size of the fight in the dog." And if ever there were a day for England to beat the Kangaroos, it's this one.

Australia arrive at Wembley without James Tedesco, Latrell Mitchell, Tom Trbojevic, Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow, Payne Haas, Zac Lomax or Xavier Coates - all among the best rugby players on the planet.

Through injuries, withdrawals, and shifting allegiances, the Kangaroos are without a number of star names.

  • Rugby League Ashes 2025: All you need to know
  • Mikey Lewis ready to face Hull KR coach Australia's Willie Peters in The Ashes
  • Kai Pearce-Paul focused on representing hometown London in Wembley clash
  • Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract on NOW

By contrast, England - who historically enter the international season down on numbers due to a longer season - are missing only Matty Ashton and Victor Radley. It's a far cry from the 2017 World Cup final when they were missing key players such as Josh Hodgson and Sean O'Loughlin and paid the price in a tense 0-6 battle.

Tomorrow they will enter Wembley strong, in front of a record Test crowd. Of course there are headline Australian stars like Nathan Cleary but the supporting cast should not spook England.

England have made much of a club-like atmosphere in their camp and their time together over the last three years. Shaun Wane has stuck with the players he trusts. If that's the case, then combinations and fluidity should immediately be on show against a side that have had the bare minimum of minutes together. This Australia side is completely different than the one that won the Pacific Championships last year.

England were rightly tipped by many to beat Tonga and Samoa in the last two years. They were superb in justifying their favourites tag and dismantled them with ease at times.

Historically there has been an aura around the Green and Gold that meant that the game was often lost before the players even got on the pitch. I remember that from being part of the Lions team in the 00s. But this is not a settled Kangaroos camp. In the build-up there was talk of disorganised preparation, as Mal Meninga walked away to recruit players for an NRL side that only starts in 2027. In his place comes Kevin Walters, who coached in the Super League fifteen years ago, with little success.

The question everyone in the game is asking is whether this is the unbeatable green and gold machine of old. Or is it a side distracted by the cult of State of Origin, their sacred ground, while the international jersey has gathered dust? The last time these two nations played, England were an ankle tap away from tying a game that may have ended in glory. The tragedy is that because they haven't played each other for eight years, we have no idea how the game will go. But that in itself brings excitement and intrigue.

The brilliant work done by players and administrators down under to push international rugby league back to the top of the pile should be commended. But the only way to kick on now is to see England play their part and win their first series since 1970.

As a member of the 2003 Lions team that could have won 3-0, but ended up losing 3-0, I know that narrow defeats count for nothing. Having played in teams that have sporadically beaten Australia home and away over the years I know a 2-1 series defeat counts for nothing either.

They, like me, will find out that if they don't seize this moment, there is no glory in defeat. It will be an opportunity wasted, and one that the players may never get the chance to rectify.

The stage is theirs. The time is now. This is the best chance England have ever had. Now they have to go and make the most of it. Fortune favours the brave.

Rugby League Ashes 2025

First Test: Saturday October 25, Wembley Stadium, London

Second Test: Saturday November 1, Everton Stadium, Liverpool

Third Test: Saturday November 8, Headingley Stadium, Leeds

articles.title: A last-second goal ends the World Cup honeymoon for Mauricio Pochettino and the USA. Now the real work begins
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino said he was happy. He said it in English, he said it in his native Spanish. He swore he was happy.
articles.body: Mauricio Pochettino said he was happy. He said it in English, he said it in his native Spanish. He swore he was happy. He didn’t sound happy. And really, there wasn’t much of a reason to be. A little more than an hour before his post-match press conference in the bowels of SoFi Stadium, Pochettino watched his USA team give up a last-second goal to Turkey that ensured a 3-2 defeat in this final match of the group stage. A weakened US side – nine changes were made from the team that faced Australia last week in Seattle – had scored quickly, gave up two first-half goals and then equalized in a strong second half. But a goal from Kaan Ayhan, scored with the last kick of the game, handed the US its first defeat after two dominant victories to open the tournament. And with it, he may have ended the honeymoon for this USA team. Pochettino’s surly mood after the game – brushing off questions about momentum, chastising American journalists for not congratulating him for winning Group D – was a marked change from the gregarious figure who sat in the same chair a little more than 24 hours before. The question now is if that mood was indicative of the vibes around this US team changing ahead of the knockout stages now that the bubble of invincibility has been popped. “I think it’s all positive, and I am so positive, and I am happy,” Pochettino said in answer to a question about whether the US may have lost momentum. “Maybe I am not showing (it) because your questions are a little bit weird, but I am so happy, and the players are happy because I think we perform, we compete, and we are first. “I was talking with the Turkish channel now, as I said, ‘Have a good trip back to Turkey,’ and we are going on. But I think now when I arrive here (in the press conference) – maybe I am confused – but maybe the mood is like we go home tonight and Turkey stay.” Pochettino is, of course, right on some very important points. By winning its first two games of this World Cup, the USA locked up the top spot in Group D and has a Round of 32 matchup against Bosnia and Herzegovina set for July 1 in the San Francisco Bay Area. It’s exactly what this team would have hoped for when the tournament started and gives them a favorable path for a deep tournament run. His lineup on Thursday, which consisted of eight players making their first World Cup starts, showed off the depth of his team as key players like Tyler Adams, Folarin Balogun, Chris Richards and Antonee Robinson were able to rest and avoid possible suspension for the game against the Zmajevi. Despite the multitude of changes, the Americans started the game well with an opening goal in the third minute and then fought back to tie the match in the second half after Turkey finally got on the score sheet. And Christian Pulisic returned to action and looked like his game-changing best, coming on in the 58th minute and quickly providing scores of chances as the US took the game to the Turks. A loss is ultimately a harsh result on the Americans after the way they recovered in the second half, looking like the more likely side to score until the game reached the final minutes. “We are much better (now) than before that game because we are players now with 90 minutes in the legs and performing, and I think ready to help if we need from the beginning or after from the bench,” Pochettino said. Still, Pochettino’s tone indicated he was still annoyed to have lost. The way the loss came about should be raising alarm bells inside the US camp. Before the tournament began, it was no secret that the USA’s defending was suspect. While the Stars and Stripes can go forward at opposing goals with flair and intent, the backline has been known to give up goals. The shutout against Australia was the first time they’d kept a clean sheet since a friendly against Japan nearly a year before. With the games now having the kind of stakes that Thursday’s contest lacked, that leaky defense – especially in crunch time toward the end of matches – is the possible Achilles heel for this team. The Turks put the US under pressure for much of the first half and again in those final minutes, playing with the desperation of a team that didn’t want to leave this World Cup without getting at least one result. When the Bosnians take the pitch in Santa Clara in a little less than a week, they’ll likely bring that same verve as they play in their nation’s first World Cup knockout game. At times on Thursday, the US struggled to cope with that pressure. The Americans are used to being the team that brings the game to their opponent, not being the squad that is absorbing and repelling attacks. But when faced with their first real setback of this tournament, the US responded positively. The introduction of Pulisic in the second half will also be a reassuring takeaway from this contest as the AC Milan man looked likely to score from the moment he entered the fray and was the best part of what the US did after Sebastian Berhalter’s strike drew the Americans level. “I think it was important to for him to get the feelings I seen again after not to be able to available for Australia,” Pochettino said. “One of the objectives in that game, not only was to win, (it was) to provide Christian in between 30 and 40 minutes to get the feeling to be ready for the next game, that is important too.” The loss to Turkey doesn’t mean all that much in what the US has to do going forward. The squad knew who its next opponent would be, when it would be playing and where it was going next. Any worries about complacency were wiped away in the third minute when Auston Trusty fired home the opening goal and caused the stands at SoFi Stadium to shake (literally) with the noise and jumping fans. Sure, it was a starting lineup of players who are usually backups or impact subs. Sure, the result has no effect on the Americans’ path toward a deep run in the tournament. Sure, a lot of the mistakes or poor moments in defense can be waved away by recognizing that most of the team’s best defenders were sitting on the bench when the Turks wheeled away in delight with Ayhan’s goal. But results do not happen in a vacuum. American soccer fans had been stunned at the way this US team looked in its opening two games, finding themselves believing that a nation that has won one knockout game in the World Cup in its history could have the squad to make a run far into July. It felt like a new day was dawning in US men’s soccer. And the moment Ayhan’s goal hit the back of the net felt like a reminder of gut-punch defeats past from teams that didn’t quite have what it took. Time will tell if this team is different. The time to prove it comes in five days at Levi’s Stadium.

articles.title: Super League's Final Charge: Leeds Rhinos, Wakefield Trinity, Wigan Warriors, Warrington Wolves, Hull KR, Leigh Leopards and St Helens in contention
articles.summary: A look at the 'Final Charge' and how the last three rounds of the Super League season are shaping up; round 25 of Super League commences from Thursday August 27, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
There are just three rounds of Super League action remaining and, with it, a whole lot of drama as Super League's Final Charge ramps up.

In Super League, the two teams who finish first and second are guaranteed a home semi-final across Friday September 25 and Saturday September 26.

In the week prior to that, the Play-Off Eliminators occur in which the third-place team takes on the team in sixth and fourth plays fifth for the chance to make it into the semis.

  • Super League fixtures & results | Super League table
  • Get Sky Sports or stream contract-free on NOW
  • Choose the Sky Sports notifications you want
  • Listen to The Bench, Sky's rugby league podcast

Then the winners of the semi-finals head to the Grand Final at Old Trafford on Saturday October 3.

Let's take a look at what each team has remaining and what is on the line for them...

1) Leeds Rhinos (38 points)

Leeds Rhinos have been at the summit of Super League for a while now and they will want to hold onto that for their three remaining fixtures.

However, they are now level on points with Wigan, who briefly leapfrogged them with Friday's win over Wakefield, but they have a vastly-superior points difference after Sunday's rout of York.

They last won the League Leaders' Shield way back in 2015 and last won a trophy in 2020 when they took Challenge Cup glory, so finishing top would see a welcome return of some silverware for the Rhinos.

In their last three matches, they face St Helens (A), Wigan Warriors (A) and Hull FC (H).

After the tricky trip to face Saints, they crucially host the Warriors on September 5 so their run-in is far from an easy on, but if they can now remain unbeaten, League Leaders' Shield glory will be theirs and they will be one match from walking out at the 'Theatre of Dreams' once again.

2) Wigan Warriors (38 points)

The team who have been there, done that, and got the T-shirt. Matt Peet, head coach of Wigan, has made no secret of how hard he has been pushing for a top-two finish because he knows how crucial that home semi-final is.

Now, if his team continue on, they could usurp Leeds if they keep the pressure on with their play-off spot confirmed.

Not only that, the Warriors will be hungry to avenge their Grand Final defeat to Hull KR in 2025.

They have the Challenge Cup in their trophy cabinet and will have all eyes on adding a second piece of silverware.

Ahead of the play-offs, they still have to play Hull KR (H), Leeds Rhinos (A) and Catalans Dragons (H).

3) Warrington Wolves (36 points)

Warrington Wolves made it three wins in a jam-packed 10 days by beating Huddersfield Giants to move on to 36 points.

Their 34-24 triumph against Huddersfield on Sunday was a fifth consecutive win, putting them in the right form at the right time for the play-off charge with just three rounds to go, and they could yet even snatch top spot.

In their remaining fixtures, they face Hull FC (A), Wakefield Trinity (A) and Toulouse Olympique (H).

All of those teams are below them in the table - a luxury not afforded to many other teams in the play-off picture.

The game against Wakefield will be the toughest test, with Trinity just four points below them.

4) Wakefield Trinity (32 points)

What a season it has been for Wakefield Trinity.

They are on the hunt for their highest Super League finish, but will now want to bounce back following their heart-breaking two-point defeat to top-of-the-table Leeds and then subsequent defeats to St Helens and Wigan Warriors.

In honesty, with two top teams remaining in their run-in, those results should worry Daryl Powell's side.

They have games against York Knights (H), Warrington Wolves (H) and Leigh Leopards (A) left.

Those are against two teams out of the seven still in the fight.

5) Leigh Leopards (32 points)

The team that has become renowned for coming good when they need to, Leigh Leopards want to shore up their spot in the play-offs once again.

After a disastrous start to the season, Adrian Lam's side have found their groove, made waves and look in real good nick at present.

Indeed, their win over Leeds set down a marker.

However, they have a tough end to the season in which they will know every win will matter.

The Leopards face Huddersfield Giants (A), St Helens (H) and Wakefield Trinity (H).

If Leigh want to make it to the Grand Final for the first time, they need to continue to show their steel now.

6) Hull KR (30 points)

Hull KR are right in the mix and will want it to stay that way but after their loss to Warrington, they are two points off fourth spot with three games left.

The Robins were the team who did it all in 2025, ending the wait for a new team to win the competition, and now they will want to send coach Willie Peters out on a high by going back to back.

Their shock loss to Toulouse did not help their cause, though.

Their remaining matches are against Wigan Warriors (A), Huddersfield Giants (H) and St Helens (A).

7) St Helens (28 points)

St Helens have three matches to try and ensure they do not make some unwanted history.

Saints have never missed out on the play-offs. Most recently they lost 20-12 to Hull KR in the semi-finals in 2025 as the Robins went on to complete the treble.

After their loss to Hull FC, St Helens looked down and out. With triumphant wins over Wakefield and Castleford, the never-say-die attitude has been reinstated once again.

They will now refocus and aim for three wins out of three to be in with a shout. If they win all three they move to 34 points.

Not only that, they face other teams in the play-off hunt and will take on Leeds Rhinos (H), Leigh Leopards (A) and Hull KR (H).

All three their three remaining matches are against teams in the top six - talk about having to take your moment.

Will they do the unthinkable? If they do manage to win their next two, that final-round contest against Hull KR could be extra tasty...

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

After a disastrous start to the season, Adrian Lam's side have found their groove, made waves and look in real good nick at present.

Indeed, their win over Leeds set down a marker.

However, they have a tough end to the season in which they will know every win will matter.

The Leopards face Huddersfield Giants (A), St Helens (H) and Wakefield Trinity (H).

If Leigh want to make it to the Grand Final for the first time, they need to continue to show their steel now.

6) Hull KR (30 points)

Hull KR are right in the mix and will want it to stay that way but after their loss to Warrington, they are two points off fourth spot with three games left.

The Robins were the team who did it all in 2025, ending the wait for a new team to win the competition, and now they will want to send coach Willie Peters out on a high by going back to back.

Their shock loss to Toulouse did not help their cause, though.

Their remaining matches are against Wigan Warriors (A), Huddersfield Giants (H) and St Helens (A).

7) St Helens (28 points)

St Helens have three matches to try and ensure they do not make some unwanted history.

Saints have never missed out on the play-offs. Most recently they lost 20-12 to Hull KR in the semi-finals in 2025 as the Robins went on to complete the treble.

After their loss to Hull FC, St Helens looked down and out. With triumphant wins over Wakefield and Castleford, the never-say-die attitude has been reinstated once again.

They will now refocus and aim for three wins out of three to be in with a shout. If they win all three they move to 34 points.

Not only that, they face other teams in the play-off hunt and will take on Leeds Rhinos (H), Leigh Leopards (A) and Hull KR (H).

All three their three remaining matches are against teams in the top six - talk about having to take your moment.

Will they do the unthinkable? If they do manage to win their next two, that final-round contest against Hull KR could be extra tasty...

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

articles.title: 'Land has been allotted': Tripura CM fulfils promise to CWG medallist Asmita Dey
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: Tripura chief minister Manik Saha has fulfilled a promise made to Commonwealth Games gold medallist Asmita Dey, with the state government a.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Tripura chief minister Manik Saha has fulfilled a promise made to Commonwealth Games gold medallist Asmita Dey, with the state government allotting her a piece of land in Agartala to build a house.The 23-year-old judoka was honoured in Tripura on Wednesday after becoming the first Indian judoka to win a Commonwealth Games gold medal.Dey won the womenâs -48kg title in Glasgow after defeating Canadaâs Heidi Quach in a dramatic golden-score contest. The state government also presented her with a cheque of Rs 10 lakh as part of the felicitation.From a village in Tripura to Commonwealth Games glorySpeaking at the event, Saha highlighted Deyâs difficult journey from a small village in South Tripura to the top of the Commonwealth Games podium. Her father, he noted, worked as a cycle mechanic in Sonaichari.âThe journey from an obscure village in South Tripura to a podium finish at Glasgow was a race against time. Her father was a cycle mechanic at Sonaichari. Against all odds, she stood firm on her mission and achieved phenomenal success for the country,â he said.The chief minister recalled meeting Dey at Tripura Bhavan in New Delhi after her return from the Games. During that meeting, the judoka had expressed her wish to have a house in Agartala.âDuring the meeting, Asmita revealed she desperately wanted a house in Agartala. I promised to fulfil her wish, and today a piece of land has been allotted to her,â he said.CM urges Asmita to target Asian Games successSaha said Deyâs achievement could motivate more young athletes from Tripura to pursue sport at the highest level. He also urged her to remain disciplined as she prepares for the Asian Games, particularly because of the strict anti-doping requirements.âI urge Asmita to remain alert, particularly about food, because she has to pass through a stringent dope test before joining the prestigious Asian Games. We believe she will shine again in the Asian Games by winning a medal for the country,â he said.Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Tinku Roy, Agartala Mayor Dipak Majumder and Arjuna award-winning gymnast Dipa Karmakar were among those who attended the felicitation ceremony.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: The Hundred 2026 awards: Stuart Broad, Nasser Hussain, Lydia Greenway pick best local player, overseas player, newcomer, fielder, captain and more
articles.summary: Nasser Hussain, Stuart Broad, Lydia Greenway pick their best local player, overseas player, newcomer, value for money, fielder, captain for 2026 Hundred season in men and women's competitions
articles.body:
Sky Sports Cricket's Nasser Hussain and Stuart Broad give out their player awards for the 2026 men's Hundred campaign, while Lydia Greenway looks at the women's competition...

Best local player

Stuart Broad:

"Jos Buttler is into the eliminator with Manchester Super Giants. Batting three, he's scored vital runs at vital times.

"He's England's best-ever white-ball batter. He's the icon of that MSG franchise.

"He's a leader in that changing room and he's got a chance of lifting the trophy."

Nasser Hussain:

"Ben Duckett went straight to the final with Trent Rockets and avoided the eliminator. That's how well he's played.

"Top of the order, he plays spin, plays fast bowling, hits it in unusual areas. He's been brilliant in the field.

"Also, at the top of the order, the way he's set the tone for that middle order of the Trent Rockets, it's just nice to see Duckett playing with such confidence and such flair.

I mentioned his fielding as well, which we do have a section on, but he's been excellent. I'm very impressed."

  • Today's cricket scorecards: The Hundred and more
  • The Hundred - latest men's and women's tables for 2026
  • Watch The Hundred and more sport contract-free on NOW

Lydia Greenway:

"I've gone for the leading wicket taker in the tournament, Tilly Corteen-Coleman. I think she's taken 13 wickets.

"The reason I picked her, she's just been really consistent. Not just this season but over the last couple of seasons.

"It's great to see her top of the tree with the wickets."

Best overseas player

Stuart Broad:

"Mitch Marsh has played some really eye-catching innings. He's batting at one of the best batting services in the country at Headingley, and he's been really entertaining.

"He's done exactly what you want an overseas player at the top of the order to do. He's led from the front. He's set the tone. He's guided his teams to win.

"His average is higher when they win than when they lose, which means he's playing a key role in winning games. Look at his strike rate, nearly 170.

"So I think he's been really crucial and a really clever signing."

Nasser Hussain:

"Mitch Marsh. Compare his consistency to someone like Harry Brook. Now, Harry's a very fine player, but a lot of his runs have come at Headingley on that belter of a surface.

"Mitch Marsh knows Headingley well, he's got Test runs there. He loves it, but he's also gone away from home at Trent Bridge, Manchester. He's got runs all around the country.

"I like the way he's a very simple person. He's a very simple player. You pitch it up, he belts it straight back past you. You drop your length back just a fraction and he'll pull you for six.

"I just love the way he keeps it very simple. And for an Aussie, he's a really nice top bloke."

Lydia Greenway:

"Overseas player has to be Phoebe Litchfield. She's obviously the leading run scorer, and the way she's gone out and dominated bowling attacks has been really entertaining to watch.

"She looks as if she's in the form of her life. She's the hardest player to set a field to in the competition.

"She hits straight down the ground, she hits behind square and then she can open up square of the wicket on both sides. She's got that ridiculous switch hit.

"If I was a captain against her, I would literally have no idea where to set the field to. She's absolutely the player in form at the moment."

Best newcomer

Nasser Hussain:

"Mitch Marsh is new to The Hundred. This is the first year he's played in The Hundred. So if he's new and he's come here from Australia, I have him as a newcomer.

"He had never played a Hundred game before this, I'm taking his age away from it."

Stuart Broad:

"I've gone for a young player who's had his first go, not in franchise cricket but in The Hundred, LD Pretorius.

"No one's really seen him in England, not really heard of him. He's not scored Ashes centuries.

"Pretorius, to me, he's playing on a difficult surface at Lord's, he's played some beautiful shots.

"He's got clear strength through the offside. A pick-up over square leg, which is fantastic.

"He's a really stylish player, and he's one of those newcomers the world of cricket will know a lot of in five years' time."

Lydia Greenway:

"I've gone for Charley Phillips. She has come in and really made the most of her opportunity. She's taken some big scalps as well within the seven wickets she's taken.

"And she's bowled in different phases of the game."

Best value for money

Nasser Hussain:

"I've gone Calvin Harrison, because he came in late as a replacement player.

"Around about £31,000 was the replacement figure. And he's bowled beautifully. He's got eight wickets.

"He's fielded really well, we've seen some of his extraordinary catches, but I just think to come in at the last moment and play, he's a real talented cricketer.

"That's someone England should be looking at across formats. He bats very well - he hasn't had much chance with the bat because the Trent Rockets have been so good - but value for money, I'm going Calvin Harrison and what he's done for the Trent Rockets."

Stuart Broad:

"I completely agree with Nasser. Calvin Harrison's been absolutely superb and now it's my time to be honest and say I've got this completely wrong with Adil Rashid, because he's on £250k to play!

"Yes, he's been very successful but as Nasser, I think, got newcomer wrong, I might have got value for money wrong because a quarter of a million pounds is quite a lot of money for eight games.

"He's been fantastic, Adil Rashid, as he was going to be.

"He's one of those players that I think every single team would have been talking about at the start of the auction. You know what you're going to get. He just delivers time after time.

"His leg spin, which is always crucial. We're in a dry spell, so it's going to spin a little bit more.

"He's one of those players that could have gone for a lot more. When you're talking about Harry Brook at £465k, Jofra Archer at £450k at the same franchise, that's where I sneaked in my value for money, because he's virtually half the price of Archer, but he performs.

Lydia Greenway:

"I've gone for Charley Phillips again here. I think she was a bargain at £15k.

"It's brilliant to see a player like her in the form that she's been in.

"And the wickets that I've mentioned, she's got big wickets. She's got Sophie Devine, Georgia Voll has been in there, Phoebe Litchfield as well, Hollie Armitage.

"So she's just been able to go in, has got quite a slingy action and just hits the top of off-stump. So it's been a pleasure to watch."

Love to watch

Nasser Hussain:

"Adil Rashid. Because in an era when spin bowlers have to bowl it quickly, have to bowl it into the surface, I still love the fact that Adil Rashid is brave enough to toss the ball up with all the variations.

"He's right at the top of his game, in an era where spinners sometimes just bowl darts.

"Adil Rashid, love watching him."

Stuart Broad:

"Trent Boult. He's done a few quirky things on the field, celebrations. He particularly upset Jonny Bairstow at Lords, but that was his ball of the tournament for me, the inswinger into the bottom of leg stump.

"I spoke to Jonny and think it was a bit of choice language that sent him off, but that's what Trent does. He's a little bit unusual at times, but he's an incredible bowler.

"I'm just drawn to him. Every time he gets a new ball in his hand, something's going to happen.

"There was a wonderful anti-fist pump that I saw with Mitch Santner. He put it in, Mitch came out, he withdrew it, and it was all a bit awkward, but Trent found that really funny."

Lydia Greenway:

"I've gone Nat Sciver-Brunt. The fact she hasn't always played the games, obviously she has been managing that calf injury, but when she comes in she looks as if she's never been away from the game.

"I was watching her in her last game and she wheeled out a reverse sweep first ball and it just shows the class of her, not to just get a score under her belt, but to do it at a decent strike rate.

"She's a player I always enjoy watching. Strong off the back foot, can play little dink shots, but manages the situation, manages the tempo and offers a huge amount obviously for the Rockets."

Best fielder

Nasser Hussain:

"I'll fix this a little bit, because Chris Jordan, for me, is the best fielder and has been throughout The Hundred every year, but I just could not leave out this catch from Will Jacks.

"It was Pretorius at the crease, and he was batting really well, and the members were sat watching that right in front of them.

"The first bit of the catch was hard, the second bit was remarkable."

Stuart Broad:

"Catches are easier than run-outs, so that's why I chose this from Ben Duckett.

"A brilliant bit of work from Duckett, diving to his left, picking the ball up, throwing it when he's turning, and most importantly, it doesn't matter if you run out Trent Boult but it does matter if you run out Nicky Pooran.

"A brilliant bit of work to hit the stumps when you only have one to aim at. I thought that really changed that game."

Lydia Greenway:

"I've gone for Bess Heath actually. In terms of number of catches, she isn't up there, but I love her approach.

"For any young girl, if you're at a ground and you're watching Heath, you can tell she's got that mentality of wanting the ball to come to her.

"She doesn't shy away from catches. She made one absolutely stunning catch. A lot of players would have sat back, they would have let it bounce once and would have taken the ball and it wouldn't have even been an opportunity.

"She's been a real sort of entertainer and energetic person in the field, which adds so much value to a team when you're out there."

Best captain

Stuart Broad:

"Sam Billings. He's won the last three Hundred titles with Oval Invincibles, he's gone to Trent Rockets, and first of all it was a brilliant signing from Trent Rockets, knowing his leadership capability.

"Once he's been given the role at a ground that he's not captained in a huge amount at before, Trent Bridge, he's got to know what the crowd like, he's got to know the surface very well.

"He leads his players brilliantly, they're top of the table, deserve to be top of the table, straight to the final, which was always the goal for the Trent Rockets, and he's got a hell of a chance to go four from four."

Nasser Hussain:

"Sam Billings. I like his aggression and the fact he's got a point to prove.

"He did an interview after he beat MI London - he was there for three years and unceremoniously sacked by them, let's be honest, after everything he'd done - and he's gone to his next franchise and he's proving a point.

"He loves this tournament. It's almost the latter stages of his career, it's what makes Sam Billings the cricketer he is."

Lydia Greenway:

"I've actually gone for Dani Gibson because if people remember the SunRisers Leeds went on a run of three losing games. They couldn't get a win for love nor money, but she and her team managed to turn it around.

"They're now finding some form at a really good time.

"For someone like Dani Gibson, it's the first time she's captain in a tournament on this sort of stage, so I've loved how she's done it.

"I love how she's spoken to the media and just the energy that she brings on the field.

"Tactically, clearly she'll always be learning. She's obviously got Adrian Birrell, who she's working closely with as a head coach. I've really enjoyed watching her this season."

articles.title: England bolters: The names putting their hand up despite not being in performance squad with Umyla Hanley, Tom Holroyd included
articles.summary: England will head to the Rugby League World Cup in Australia in October; Brian McDermott will be tasked with choosing a squad to go; 38-man performance squad was announced in June
articles.body:
We are just two months out from the Rugby League World Cup and with that in mind, every Super League player will have a place on the plane to Australia in the back of their mind.

Back in June, new England head coach Brian McDermott announced a 38-man performance squad, including 10 uncapped players, with whom he would work over the season to get England as well prepared as they can be for the tournament come October.

Leeds Rhinos star and reigning Man of Steel Jake Connor has not played for his country in seven years and was overlooked by then England coach Shaun Wane for the 3-0 Ashes defeat at home to Australia last autumn. But now, he is back.

articles.title: Super League receive investment offer from Australia's National Rugby League as part of 'recapitalisation project'
articles.summary: Super League have received an investment offer from Australia Rugby League Commission (ARLC) who run the NRL; Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season - including two matches in each round exclusively live
articles.body:
Super League have received an investment offer from the Australia Rugby League Commission (ARLC) which governs the National Rugby League (NRL) in Australia.

Conversations have long been occurring between Australia's governing body and Europe's, with a formal offer now having been received.

In a statement, Super League said: "RL Commercial can confirm that a first offer has been received from the ARLC (Australian Rugby League Commission) as part of the sport's recapitalisation project.

  • Super League fixtures & results | Super League table
  • Get Sky Sports or stream contract-free on NOW
  • Choose the Sky Sports notifications you want
  • Listen to The Bench, Sky's rugby league podcast

"The Super League clubs have been informed this morning.

"Details of the offer remain confidential."

Former NRL chief executive Andrew Abdo spoke to Sky Sports back in April about the NRL's planned involvement in Super League. He was over in the UK for talks about the move.

He said it was a move focused on the "globalisation" of rugby league with a view to ensure that rugby league in the UK and Europe is governed by an independent commission, similar to the set up of the ARLC.

ARLC Chairman Peter V'Landys is now understood to be leading the talks.

"We really believe in the globalisation of rugby league," Abdo told Sky Sports.

"This is a great game and we want to take it to as many people as possible. We want to win as many fans as possible.

"So while the game is growing really well in the southern hemisphere, we also want the game to be strong here in the north.

"This is about a partnership where we can collaborate on how we can grow the game, how we can grow revenues and how can those revenues be pumped back into the game?

"That's pretty nuanced and that's something we have to develop together."

RL Commercial managing director Rhodri Jones added on the talks from April: "They would like to have a heavy influence on the commission and who sits on that commission.

"What they perhaps haven't understood in totality is the make up of our governance structure in this country.

"We have multiple organisations in RFL, Super League and RL Commercial. When it is such a big topic like recapitalisation, it is complex.

"But with hard work, better detail, we can overcome some of these challenges so we can get to the right result that the sport wants."

The talks have now moved into the next negotiation phase.

2026 Super League - key dates and what to look out for

  • Elimination Play-offs: September 19-September 20
  • Play-off semi-finals: September 26-September 27
  • Grand Final: October 3, Old Trafford.

Sky Sports will again show every game of the Super League live this season - including two matches in each round exclusively live, with the remaining five matches each week shown on Sky Sports+

articles.title: Daly Cherry-Evans: Former Kangaroos half-back signs one-year deal with Hull FC for 2027 Super League season
articles.summary: NRL stalwart Daly Cherry-Evans has signed with Hull FC for the 2027 Super League season; He is considered an NRL legend with a nine-year international career for the Kangaroos
articles.body:
NRL legend Daly Cherry-Evans has signed a one-year deal for Hull FC which sees him complete a shock switch to Super League for the 2027 season.

Former Kangaroos half-back Cherry-Evans, widely considered one of the best playmakers in the history of the sport, is no stranger to shock moves, joining Sydney Roosters from Manly Sea Eagles for 2026 after 15 years with the club.

It had been rumoured that Cherry-Evans, who played for Australia across nine years, could be retiring at the end of this season but instead, he will make the move to Super League as he turns 38.

articles.title: Daly Cherry-Evans: NRL legend opens up on Hull FC move: 'It's where the connections felt right'
articles.summary: NRL legend Daly Cherry-Evans will swap Sydney for Hull in 2027 after signing a one-year deal with Hull FC; He will turn 38 as he joins the Super League club; he says it is a move to 'protect his future'
articles.body:
NRL legend Daly Cherry-Evans has opened up on his shock move to sign a one-year deal with Hull FC in the Super League in 2027 and says it is the club with which the "connections felt right".

Cherry-Evans sensationally moved to Sydney Roosters ahead of the 2026 season and scored a try on Thursday in their match against Penrith Panthers to move his side top of the NRL table.

However, as he turns 38 years of age, Cherry-Evans will swap Sydney for the Black and Whites.

  • Daly Cherry-Evans signs one-year deal with Hull FC
  • Super League fixtures & results | Super League table
  • Get Sky Sports or stream contract-free on NOW
  • Choose the Sky Sports notifications you want
  • Listen to The Bench, Sky's rugby league podcast

Former Kangaroos half-back Cherry-Evans is widely considered one of the best playmakers in the history of the sport, playing nine years for Australia and captaining Queensland.

While Cherry-Evans admitted he pondered about continuing to live the NRL "dream", his curiosity about Super League won out in a moment that felt like the "right time" to move across the world.

"That's just where the relationships and the connections felt right. I didn't have to look at too many other places, to be honest. If you're going to do it, you might as well do it properly, and Hull will give us that opportunity," Cherry-Evans said.

"As a person, deep down, I've always had that curiosity about what Super League would be like or what another code would be like in another country. As I've gotten older, I've understood that there's a big wide world out there, so it has become an interest, but I never knew when.

"I never had a timeline. It was just a thought that kept popping over again and again. It felt like coming to the Roosters wasn't just going to benefit me with footy, but also challenge me in other ways, and that's definitely been the case. It'll be another case of that in a different country next year.

"It just feels like the right time. No one can know when someone's right time is. It comes from deep within. The conversations I've had with myself and the people I love and trust - everything just makes sense to make the move now.

"There was definitely that voice in my head that said 'Stay in the NRL. Keep living out that dream.' But there's more to my story than me just playing in the NRL.

"I guess why I play in the NRL has a lot to do with challenging myself at the highest level but also inspiring my family and I feel like our family is ready for something different.

"We've had an amazing experience that's still continuing at the Roosters, but what an amazing opportunity I'm going to have to go and play in the UK with my wife and kids who will be old enough to remember it years down the track."

'It is a move to protect my future'

While all eyes are currently trained on Cherry-Evans' spectacular move, his are solely focused on ensuring that Sydney Roosters win the competition in 2026.

The move, in itself, was more about "protecting" the playmakers' future.

"There's absolutely nothing more important to me right now than winning a Premiership this year, but at some stage you do have to protect your future, and talking to my wife and the people we love and trust within our circle, we were told you will never regret going over to the UK and giving the Super League a go.

"We're really excited about what's ahead for us as a family and also I'm very excited about the challenges that the Super League is going to give to me.

"I am always about challenges and testing myself and Super League is going to give me that opportunity.

"But now that it's all done, it's great and I'm excited about it, but I can just drop the shoulders and just focus on everything inside these four walls for the rest of the year."

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

articles.title: Super League: Coach-less Castleford Tigers claim much-needed victory at Hull FC with Ryan Carr still absent
articles.summary: Liam Hood strikes decisive late try as Castleford Tigers claim much-needed Super League victory at Hull FC on Friday night; win comes with Tigers head coach Ryan Carr still absent for personal reasons; Castleford arrest run of three straight losses in which they conceded 144 points
articles.body:
Castleford Tigers ended a disastrous run in Super League with a late 18-14 win at Hull FC on Friday.

The Tigers had conceded 144 points in successive defeats to Wakefield, Warrington and Hull KR but bounced back at the MKM Stadium thanks to Liam Hood's late try.

Castleford - whose head coach Ryan Carr remains absent for personal reasons - opened the scoring after 10 minutes when Renouf Atoni took a short ball at speed and Tom Weaver added the conversion

  • Super League fixtures & results | Super League table
  • Get Sky Sports or stream contract-free on NOW
  • Choose the Sky Sports notifications you want
  • Listen to The Bench, Sky's rugby league podcast

Mikaele Ravalawa dived over to stretch the lead after Phoenix Laulu-Togagae had lofted a perfectly-weighted pass into the corner.

Weaver kicked a penalty to make it 12-0 but Hull launched a stirring fightback either side of the interval.

Jakob Arthur's grubber kick was collected by Joe Batchelor and Aidan Sezer added the goal.

Hull claimed the lead as Harvey Barron took a high ball to touch down and Sezer sent over Lewis Martin in the corner.

But Hood burst over from dummy-half 12 minutes from time and Weaver enjoyed more kicking success as the Tigers climbed two places to ninth while Hull stay 12th.

Castleford Director of Rugby Chester: It's been turbulent - I don't know what situation is, the board will make call

Castleford Tigers Director of Rugby Chris Chester told Sky Sports:

"I'm not too sure [what the situation with Ryan Carr is]. My focus this week and certainly over the last few days has been getting these guys ready for a tough game against Hull FC.

"It's been a really turbulent week.

"The board will make that decision when it's right. My job has been to prepare these guys the best I possibly could and they showed some real heart out there and played for the badge tonight.

"But I just want to say a few words on Danny Wilson [Castleford chief executive], who is laid up in bed, he hasn't been well. We miss him here at the club.

"That win was for him."

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

articles.title: Super League: St Helens keep slim play-off hopes alive after stirring second half earns 46-16 win over Wakefield Trinity
articles.summary: St Helens have never failed to make play-offs but in battle to reach post-season this year; Saints bounce back from three straight defeats with victory at Wakefield after 34 unanswered points in second half; Wigan beat Bradford, who drop to foot of table after Huddersfield win at Toulouse
articles.body:
St Helens produced a blistering second-half performance to stun Wakefield Trinity with a 46-16 victory and keep their slim Super League play-off hopes alive.

Saints, who have never failed to make the post-season, came into the match on a run of three defeats in a row and five losses in six, leaving them six points off the top six.

The visitors slipped 10-0 down to fourth-placed Wakefield and trailed 16-12 at half-time but then ran in six unanswered tries in the second period.

  • Latest Sky Sports deals or stream rugby league with NOW
  • Betfred Super League table as Leeds Rhinos lead the way
  • Listen to The Bench, Sky Sports' rugby league podcast

Tristan Sailor's brace completed his hat-trick while Lewis Murphy added to his first-half score and Jake Davies touched down twice in the closing stages to move St Helens to within four points of sixth-placed Leigh Leopards with four games remaining.

Wakefield falter after bright start

Wakefield, who lost Josh Rourke and try-scorer Isaiah Vagana to injuries inside the first quarter of an hour, missed the chance to move two points behind table toppers Leeds as they suffered a sixth successive defeat to Saints and slipped to back-to-back home losses after last week's narrow reverse against the Rhinos.

Tyson Smoothy's eighth-minute effort, which was converted by Jack Sinfield, and Vagana's Sinfield-aided score in the 12th put Wakefield on top.

However, Vagana was barged into as he went down and went off with a physio holding his left arm, after Rourke departed following a collision with Murphy.

Sailor and Murphy dragged Saints back into the contest with tries that Jackson Hastings converted, only for Sinfield to exploit a huge gap before kicking his second conversion to leave Wakefield four points to the good at the break.

Lachlan Walmsley had two tries chalked off for Trinity after the resumption, either side of which Murphy put Saints back in front with another fine finish, diving one-handed in the corner before hobbling off with an injury to his left leg.

Once Billy Keeley latched on to a loose ball and went over after 64 minutes, Saints dominated, with Sailor's hat-trick, sealed after a lung-busting run, prompting Wakefield's fans to stream for the exits.

Powell rues Wakefield's lack of 'fight'

Trinity coach Daryl Powell called his side's capitulation "unforgivable", saying: "There was a lack of effort, almost, at the end.

"It's really disappointing. The second half last week and the whole game today, I don't think we're in a great place.

"We didn't perform well. We took a smack on the nose last week and we haven't recovered from that this week. They were desperate and they outplayed us. I don't think our fight was good enough.

"It's hugely disappointing and I've said to the players 'we've got to flip this pretty quick'. We play Wigan next week and it doesn't get any harder than that."

Wigan level on points with Leeds as Bradford slip to bottom spot

Wigan moved level on points with leader Leeds as they scored six tries in a 34-6 victory at lowly Bradford, who now prop up the table following resurgent Huddersfield's victory at Toulouse on Saturday evening.

The visitors crossed three times in each half with Jake Wardle, Adam Keighran and Bevan French touching down before the break.

Wardle went over again in the second period while Kian McDermott and Jake Kerr also registered tries, with the Bulls' sole effort coming from Andy Ackers.

Wigan's 18th win of the season leaves them four points clear of Warrington and Wakefield in third and fourth respectively, while Bradford have been usurped by Huddersfield on points difference after their fellow Yokshiremen's 26-10 win in France.

The Giants have won four games in a row after just two victories across their first 19 matches, with this latest success thanks to two tries from Sam Halsall and one apiece for Joe Greenwood and Conor Wrench.

Huddersfield's revival, which has also included beating York, Hull FC and Catalans, has come at the same time Toulouse have faded, with Sylvain Houles' men on a four-match losing streak following previous disappointing results against Catalans, Leeds and Wigan.

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

articles.title: The Hundred: Tim Seifert propels Manchester Super Giants to title with last-gasp win over Trent Rockets in Lord's final
articles.summary: Tim Seifert produced a sensational 72 off 38 in the men's Hundred final at Lord's; Liam Dawson smashed a six over the rope to win the title with two balls to go; Rockets miss out on a clean sweep of men's and women's titles
articles.body:
Tim Seifert produced an imperious 72 off 38 balls to steer the Manchester Super Giants to The Hundred title after a five-wicket victory over the Trent Rockets in an incredible final at Lord's that went down to the last three balls.

The opener notched the fastest fifty in men's Hundred final history and was aided by cameos from opening partner Paul Walter (22 off 14), captain Jos Buttler (23 off 14) and a crucial knock from Leus Du Plooy (27no off 18) to chase down their opponents' substantial score of 158.

Two late wickets from Mohammed Amir (3-29) gave the Rockets hope, leaving the Super Giants needing three runs off the last five balls, but spinner Liam Dawson resisted the pressure and smashed a six with three balls to go to seal the title for MSG.

  • Scorecard: Manchester Super Giants vs Trent Rockets
  • Latest Sky Sports deals or stream cricket with no contract
  • Listen to latest episode of the Sky Sports Cricket podcast

The victory secured the Super Giants their maiden Hundred title after beating SunRisers Leeds in the eliminator on Friday, preventing the Rockets from becoming the first team to win both the men's and women's Hundred after Trent Rockets women demolished SunRisers Leeds women earlier on Sunday.

Super Giants' batters storm to title-clinching victory

Rockets openers Duckett (31 off 24) and Allen (15 off 13) - who were afflicted by the low-scoring Lord's pitch, which has seen a first-innings average of just 141 during the 2026 Hundred - managed just 33 from the powerplay but seemed to have settled into their innings before Super Giants spinner Noor Ahmad (3-33) dismissed both openers in a game-changing four deliveries that took the Rockets from 48-0 to 52-2.

The batting side, though, rebounded through the impressive innings of Anuerin Donald (38 off 19), before a spell of three wickets in 11 balls - including a comedic run out that saw the captain Sam Billings dismissed - left them reeling at 95-5.

Useful cameos from Lewis Gregory (32 off 16) and Mitch Santner (20no off 16), though, helped the Rockets to a defendable score of 158 after their 100 balls.

Super Giants openers Seifert and Walter (22 off 14) - the latter of whom smashed 80 off 46 balls in the eliminator - gave their side a brilliant start to the run chase, notching their fifty partnership off just 26 balls.

Seifert was spared his blushes after an incredible one-handed diving Finn Allen catch was overruled by the third umpire after his foot brushed the boundary rope, but his partner Walter was sent packing just three deliveries later when he was caught on the boundary by Duckett to end the 66-run opening wicket stand.

Seifert, undeterred, continued his stellar innings and raced to a stunning 24-ball fifty, combining effectively with both Buttler and Du Plooy before his dismissal, but the wickets of Heinrich Klaasen (11 off 9) and Michael Bracewell (0 off 2) in successive balls to Amir set up a tantalising finale, with the Super Giants needing three off Ben Sanderson's last five balls.

Two dots in the first two balls of the last five increased the tension and pressure on tail-ender Dawson, but the England international resisted and smashed the game-winning maximum with the next ball to win the title for his side and cap off the 2026 Hundred.

Buttler: We deserved Hundred title

Manchester Super Giants captain Jos Buttler, speaking to Sky Sports:

"Mixture of emotions - the excitement and euphoria of winning it, a little bit of relief after the last few balls there - but fantastic effort from everyone to lift the trophy. I think we deserve it.

"I enjoyed [captaining]. It's a little bit more stressful, but captaining a great bunch of guys with a bowling attack that's really varied.

"It was crucial that we broke some really important partnerships and that went a long way to winning the game.

"We've had some brilliant performances from everyone. The two boys at the top of the order since Aiden [Markram] hasn't been here have been outstanding - but it's also been the wicket-taking ability,

"We're very well-marshalled off the field by a great coaching team as well. Tom Moody, Justin Langer and everyone have been brilliant - I'm proud of everyone involved."

  • Third Test (Edgbaston) - Wednesday September 9 - Sunday September 13 (first ball 11am)
