articles.title: The Hundred: Trent Rockets thrash SunRisers Leeds at Lord's to win women's title for first time
articles.summary: Defending women's Hundred champions SunRisers Leeds skittled for 91 by Trent Rockets in women's final; Georgia Adams stars with ball and in field for Rockets, before Ash Gardner's side ease to target in just 54 balls; Rockets won eight of their nine games this season, including last seven
articles.body:
Trent Rockets stormed to a first women's Hundred title after demolishing defending champions SunRisers Leeds by eight wickets in a one-sided final at Lord's.

Rockets razed SunRisers for 91 from as many balls after winning the toss before cantering to their target with 46 deliveries to spare as skipper Ash Gardner pounded the winning four through the off-side.

Georgia Adams (2-15 from nine balls), playing in her fifth Hundred final, enjoyed a brilliant afternoon for Rockets.

  • Scorecard: Trent Rockets Women vs Sunrisers Leeds Women
  • Latest Sky Sports deals or stream cricket with no contract
  • Listen to latest episode of the Sky Sports Cricket podcast

The off-spinning all-rounder's wickets included Annabel Sutherland (25) stumped, while she also caught the dangerous Phoebe Litchfield (10) at short fine leg on the scoop and superbly ran out Jess Jonassen (0) from cover.

Rockets made light work of the chase with Sophia Dunkley (41 off 23) and Beth Mooney (31no off 21) pounding 45 in the 25-ball powerplay during an opening stand of 69 from 61 balls - Dunkley looked on course for fourth fifty of the campaign before spooning Dani Gibson to short cover with 23 runs needed.

Sutherland and SunRisers skipper Gibson (22) were the only batters in their side to make it into the 20s, with the team slumping to 24-3 after 19 balls and then losing their final seven wickets for 35 once Deepti Sharma (12) was bowled.

Rockets romp to victory as bowlers set the tone

Rockets, who secured a seventh win in a row and an eighth in nine overall, were clinical with the ball, starting with Kim Garth (2-18) striking twice in as many legal deliveries early on to banish Bryony Smith (2) and birthday girl Lauren Winfield-Hill (0).

Charley Phillips (2-12) and Samantha Bates (2-17) also picked up a brace of wickets for Rockets, with Bates' haul taking her to 13 in the tournament.

Sutherland and Gibson added fleeting impetus for SunRisers - the former clubbing the only six of the innings and the latter latching on to some wayward deliveries from Garth - but there was little else to cheer for the team in orange.

SunRisers' triumph last summer, which came under their previous Northern Superchargers name, saw them upset table toppers Southern Brave in the final.

But they could not repeat that result against this year's winners of the league phase as they lost to Rockets for a second time this season, following a five-run loss at Trent Bridge on August 2.

That was a slender defeat, this was a hammering, with perhaps the only disappointment for Rockets that Nat Sciver-Brunt fell cheaply, pinned lbw by Sutherland for four.

'Adams turns up in big games'

Sky Sports Cricket's Nasser Hussain:

"Georgia Adams is a serial winner, a top signing, she turned the game around.

"It's not just about the wickets and catches, it's about who you get out. Annabel Sutherland, Phoebe Litchfield, Jess Jonassen. That was a serious performance from someone who consistently turns up in the big games."

'We aren't reliant on one or two people'

Rockets captain Ash Gardner:

"Different people stood up at different times. It's been a fantastic campaign to be part of. I've said it all along, we're not reliant on one or two people.

"People played their role, that is all you can ask as a captain. We've been fantastic throughout. We're an experienced group and I've been able to lean on many people so it hasn't just been me."

articles.title: Hull KR 28-34 Warrington Wolves: George Williams stars as Sam Burgess' side move two points off Super League top spot
articles.summary: Warrington Wolves' win puts them two points behind Leeds and Wigan; Mikey Lewis was sent to the sin bin on the return from his four-match ban for dangerous contact with kicker Ewan Irwin; round 24 of Super League continues on Thursday August 20, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Warrington Wolves sent a statement with a 34-28 win over Hull KR in their rearranged Super League round two match at Sewell Group Craven Park.

The match could not take place 22 rounds ago due to the Robins being in Las Vegas but the new allotted time seemed to suit Sam Burgess' side as they romped to a victory which puts them two points off top spot.

For the home side, the stand out point will be that Mikey Lewis returned from a four-game ban, in which they won all four matches, but then was sin-binned in a contest in which they were second best.

  • Super League's Final Charge: Seven teams in contention
  • Super League fixtures & results | Super League table
  • Get Sky Sports or stream contract-free on NOW
  • Choose the Sky Sports notifications you want

The yellow card came for a dangerous contact with kicker Ewan Irwin, which Warrington head coach Sam Burgess described as "dangerous".

"I think the challenge at the back end of the game was a bad challenge. It is a bad challenge. He (Irwin) is very lucky he's come out of that healthy. He's a tough kid," Burgess said.

"I'm not trying to make it worse than it is.," he later added. "You just have to watch it. It's really dangerous.
In the NRL, you're going to be in a bit of trouble."

The Robins did have a 14-10 half-time lead thanks to a Rhyse Martin penalty plus converted Lewis and Karl Lawton tries.

Warrington went over through an unconverted Albert Hopoate effort and a James Bentley try, but were four points adrift.

But a dominant second half saw Toafofa Sipley, Liam Byrne, George Williams and Albert Hopoate all score, ensuring late tries from Dean Hadley and Tevita Pangai Jnr were sheer consolations, while Mikey Lewis was sin-binned on his return from suspension.

Wolves show play-off credentials

Hull KR took an early lead through the boot of Martin after Warrington conceded a penalty for a high shot on Frenchman Arthur Mourgue.

But the Robins started to make errors, twice dropping the ball and then conceding a penalty. Warrington slowly turned the screw and after forcing three repeat sets, they eventually scored the first try of the game as a sweeping move from left to right saw Hopoate squeeze home in the corner on 18 minutes.

Irwin couldn't convert, and it was the Wire who came up with errors for the next period. However, the hosts didn't punish them and when they eventually conceded a penalty for holding down, England captain Williams produced a crisp pass for Bentley to race on to and score from close range, Irwin tagging on the extras this time for a 10-2 lead.

But Rovers were ahead before the break. On his return from a four-match suspension, Lewis got himself on the scoresheet after being the first to react to Jez Litten's threaded kick to the in-goal, and a minute before the break Lawton barged over, with both tries converted by Mourgue.

That put Rovers 14-10 ahead, but Sam Burgess' side were ahead three minutes after the interval as powerhouse prop Sipley crashed over from a few meters out after Danny Walker's smart pass, with Irwin converting once again.

On 50 minutes, Mourgue brought the game level with a penalty goal, leaving the game evenly poised at a crucial period.

The game would soon be injected with further spice as a commotion saw players from both teams come together.

But the Robins lost their composure as Mourgue was penalised for a needless block on Walker while his team were coming away from their own try line. That allowed Irwin to kick a penalty goal to go two points ahead once again.

Immediately after that, Lewis kicked out on the full for the second time in the game and Warrington made the most of it once more, with Byrne smashing through the defensive line to score a converted try that extended the lead to eight points going into the final quarter.

From there, it was one-way traffic. The brilliant Williams got on the inside of Litten to score by the sticks, and he then produced a wonderful kick that was sublimely finished by Hopoate to add emphasis to the scoreline.

Hadley and Pangai Jr got late consolations for Rovers, but it was too little, too late.

Burgess: Scoreline doesn't reflect dominance

Player of the match George Williams told Sky Sports:

"For Mikey Lewis, he's a nice quiet lad, not how he plays. It's a fine line, and at the minute he's getting it wrong. But just put an arm around him.

"He's one of the best players in the comp."

Warrington Wolves head coach Sam Burgess:

"I'm happy and proud of the team. We didn't have it our way for parts of it.

"We'll reassess, but I'm proud of the spirit. This is a tough place to come.

"I'm proud of our effort and physicality.

"The scoreline didn't reflect the game in the first half, and it's fair to say it doesn't in the second half either. We were dominant in a lot of areas.

"Our collective effort, everyone did their jobs. We grew in the disruption."

Peters: Warrington didn't have to work for tries

Hull KR head coach Willie Peters to Sky Sports:

"Yeah it was a tough second half to watch.

"There were a lot of moments to like in that game, but a lot we won't want to watch back again. Just not good enough.

"It's disappointing and I'm disappointed with the tries we let in.

"Warrington are a very good team, I'm not taking anything away from them, but they didn't have to work for coming through the middle of us.

"We're a brave team, because it could have got worse, but obviously the game was gone by the end.

"I need to have a look at the Mikey Lewis incident. I don't know how bad it was."

  • Super League fixtures & results | Super League table
  • Get Sky Sports or stream contract-free on NOW
  • Choose the Sky Sports notifications you want

The yellow card came for a dangerous contact with kicker Ewan Irwin, which Warrington head coach Sam Burgess described as "dangerous".

"I think the challenge at the back end of the game was a bad challenge. It is a bad challenge. He (Irwin) is very lucky he's come out of that healthy. He's a tough kid," Burgess said.

"I'm not trying to make it worse than it is.," he later added. "You just have to watch it. It's really dangerous.
In the NRL, you're going to be in a bit of trouble."

The Robins did have a 14-10 half-time lead thanks to a Rhyse Martin penalty plus converted Lewis and Karl Lawton tries.

Warrington went over through an unconverted Albert Hopoate effort and a James Bentley try, but were four points adrift.

But a dominant second half saw Toafofa Sipley, Liam Byrne, George Williams and Albert Hopoate all score, ensuring late tries from Dean Hadley and Tevita Pangai Jnr were sheer consolations, while Mikey Lewis was sin-binned on his return from suspension.

Wolves show play-off credentials

Hull KR took an early lead through the boot of Martin after Warrington conceded a penalty for a high shot on Frenchman Arthur Mourgue.

But the Robins started to make errors, twice dropping the ball and then conceding a penalty. Warrington slowly turned the screw and after forcing three repeat sets, they eventually scored the first try of the game as a sweeping move from left to right saw Hopoate squeeze home in the corner on 18 minutes.

Irwin couldn't convert, and it was the Wire who came up with errors for the next period. However, the hosts didn't punish them and when they eventually conceded a penalty for holding down, England captain Williams produced a crisp pass for Bentley to race on to and score from close range, Irwin tagging on the extras this time for a 10-2 lead.

But Rovers were ahead before the break. On his return from a four-match suspension, Lewis got himself on the scoresheet after being the first to react to Jez Litten's threaded kick to the in-goal, and a minute before the break Lawton barged over, with both tries converted by Mourgue.

That put Rovers 14-10 ahead, but Sam Burgess' side were ahead three minutes after the interval as powerhouse prop Sipley crashed over from a few meters out after Danny Walker's smart pass, with Irwin converting once again.

On 50 minutes, Mourgue brought the game level with a penalty goal, leaving the game evenly poised at a crucial period.

The game would soon be injected with further spice as a commotion saw players from both teams come together.

But the Robins lost their composure as Mourgue was penalised for a needless block on Walker while his team were coming away from their own try line. That allowed Irwin to kick a penalty goal to go two points ahead once again.

Immediately after that, Lewis kicked out on the full for the second time in the game and Warrington made the most of it once more, with Byrne smashing through the defensive line to score a converted try that extended the lead to eight points going into the final quarter.

From there, it was one-way traffic. The brilliant Williams got on the inside of Litten to score by the sticks, and he then produced a wonderful kick that was sublimely finished by Hopoate to add emphasis to the scoreline.

Hadley and Pangai Jr got late consolations for Rovers, but it was too little, too late.

Burgess: Scoreline doesn't reflect dominance

Player of the match George Williams told Sky Sports:

"For Mikey Lewis, he's a nice quiet lad, not how he plays. It's a fine line, and at the minute he's getting it wrong. But just put an arm around him.

"He's one of the best players in the comp."

Warrington Wolves head coach Sam Burgess:

"I'm happy and proud of the team. We didn't have it our way for parts of it.

"We'll reassess, but I'm proud of the spirit. This is a tough place to come.

"I'm proud of our effort and physicality.

"The scoreline didn't reflect the game in the first half, and it's fair to say it doesn't in the second half either. We were dominant in a lot of areas.

"Our collective effort, everyone did their jobs. We grew in the disruption."

Peters: Warrington didn't have to work for tries

Hull KR head coach Willie Peters to Sky Sports:

"Yeah it was a tough second half to watch.

"There were a lot of moments to like in that game, but a lot we won't want to watch back again. Just not good enough.

"It's disappointing and I'm disappointed with the tries we let in.

"Warrington are a very good team, I'm not taking anything away from them, but they didn't have to work for coming through the middle of us.

"We're a brave team, because it could have got worse, but obviously the game was gone by the end.

"I need to have a look at the Mikey Lewis incident. I don't know how bad it was."

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

articles.title: Lakers’ Jeanie Buss ‘contesting’ family’s vote to sell to Kushner, Iger
articles.summary: The Lakers governor is resisting attempts to sell family’s minority share to new owners Bob Iger and Josh Kushner.
articles.body:
Jeanie Buss is challenging her siblings’ attempt to ‌sell the family’s remaining stake in the famous National Basketball Association (NBA) franchise, the Los Angeles Lakers.

Hours after the Buss family released a statement revealing ⁠its intention to sell its ⁠17.8 percent ownership of the team to new owners Bob Iger and Josh Kushner, CNBC and ESPN reported that Jeanie’s lawyer sought to halt the siblings’ sale on legal grounds.

list 2 of 4 Barcelona reaches deal with Man City to sign Spain skipper Rodri

list 3 of 4 La Liga: The key talking points for Real Madrid before the 2026-27 season

list 4 of 4 Arsenal defend title against revamped challengers as Premier League returns

At issue is ⁠Jeanie’s status as the Lakers’ controlling owner. NBA guidelines require controlling owners or governors to own at least 15 percent of a franchise.

Fourteen months ago, Jeanie spearheaded the sale of the franchise to Mark Walter for $10bn, a then-record for ⁠a US professional sports franchise. The Buss family trust – which comprises Jerry Buss’s six children – voted to sell to Walter, although there was some infighting due to the perception that the process was rushed.

Part of the agreement with Walter provided that Jeanie would remain governor through 2030, but her siblings were terminated from their positions with the organisation following the sale.

Last ‌week, Walter sold the Lakers to Iger and Kushner for the record-breaking price of $12.5bn, a sale yet to be approved by the NBA.

The Buss family – which has been either a primary or minority owner of the Los Angeles Lakers since 1979 – made their move on Monday afternoon, though it was not clear at the time that Jeanie was not on board.

“We have decided as a family to sell the remaining Buss Family Trust shares to the Bob Iger group as part of the ongoing transaction,” the family said in a statement to ESPN. “We ⁠love the Lakers, Laker fans and will continue to support Los Angeles; but it ⁠is time to use this opportunity to move on and exit gracefully while we still can.”

Lawyer Adam Streisand replied on Jeanie’s behalf later on Monday, with a letter obtained by CNBC and ESPN addressed to siblings Jim, Johnny, Janie, Joey and Jesse Buss. He argued that a court ruled ⁠in 2017 that any sale of the Lakers required approval from the cotrustees, Jeanie among them.

“Pursuant to the JAB Trust and the attached Court Order,” Streisand added. “The cotrustees are ⁠bound to vote the Los Angeles Lakers, Inc shares to ensure that ⁠the minimum 15 percent ownership requirement is maintained in order to ensure that Jeanie Buss may remain Controlling Owner.”

“Any attempt by the cotrustees to do otherwise, and any attempt to aid or abet the cotrustees as such, would constitute a breach of trust, breach of fiduciary duty and be in contempt ‌of court.”

Jeanie took over as the governor in 2013 following her father’s death.

Walter, the CEO and chair of diversified holding company TWG Global, owns MLB’s Los Angeles Dodgers and the WNBA’s Los Angeles Sparks. He is ‌under federal ‌investigation for alleged tax fraud involving four of his other business interests.

Should the sale go through, Iger and Kushner will own approximately 83 percent of the Lakers.

The NBA Board of Governors, which must approve this sale, does not meet until September 15-16 in New York.

articles.title: Patrick Kane Throws Out Cubs 1st Pitch in Trending Video After Return to Blackhawks on New Contract
articles.summary: Patrick Kane got a warm welcome back to Chicago after rejoining the Chicago Blackhawks last month.
articles.body:
Patrick Kane got a warm welcome back to Chicago after rejoining the Chicago Blackhawks last month.

The veteran right winger threw out the first pitch at Wrigley Field ahead of Tuesday night's matchup between the Cubs and White Sox.

Kane, 37, agreed to a two-year, $8 million contract with the Blackhawks to set up a reunion between him and the team where he had the best years of his career. He played for Chicago from 2007 to 2023, winning a Hart Trophy and three Stanley Cups

The Blackhawks traded Kane to the Detroit Red Wings at the deadline in 2023 as they began shifting towards a rebuild. He played the last three seasons in Detroit on one-year deals.

When Kane decided to return for a 20th NHL season, rejoining the Blackhawks seemed like a perfect move, and now he's back with the team that drafted him first overall nearly two decades ago.

"What a time! To say I get to be a Blackhawk again is an amazing feeling... the love, passion and energy I've felt from the fans has been unparalleled, even when I was not always wearing the Blackhawks sweater," Kane wrote in a social media post after signing his new deal. "There's nothing like the city of Chicago and home games in the UC."

Kane is coming off a season in which he recorded 57 points (16 goals, 41 assists) in 67 games. He'll look to put together a strong year as the Blackhawks try to get back to the playoffs for the first time since 2020.

Having a franchise legend like Kane should help the young, rebuilding squad progress this year.

articles.title: Sabalenka cruises through as Medvedev falls to Nakashima at Cincinnati Open
articles.summary: Top-ranked Aryna Sabalenka lost just four games to breeze into fourth round while Brandon Nakashima recorded a huge win.
articles.body:
World number one Aryna Sabalenka dominated China’s Wang Xinyu 6-1, 6-3 to cruise into the Cincinnati Masters fourth round, while Daniil Medvedev suffered a shock defeat to Brandon Nakashima.

Sabalenka took only 20 minutes on Tuesday to breeze through the first set against her 36th-ranked opponent and began the second set with a break of serve.

list 1 of 4 Jose Mourinho returns to Real Madrid in closed-door ceremony

list 2 of 4 Barcelona seal deal for World Cup winner Rodri from Manchester City

list 3 of 4 Premier League is back: All to know as the 2026-27 season kicks off

list 4 of 4 Arsenal preview: Five key questions heading into new Premier League season

She kept up the pressure in the second set, with Wang double-faulting on the top seed’s first match point after 54 minutes.

The victory marked the 45th in a row for Sabalenka at the Masters 1000 level.

“I cannot complain. She’s a tough opponent,” Sabalenka said. “To win in straight sets like this in under an hour is insane.

“I’m super happy to be through. I really trusted myself and went for my shots. I wasn’t overthinking. I was able to stay focused and be in every point.”

Sabalenka next plays Czech Sara Bejlek, a 4-6, 6-1, 6-2 winner over Ekaterina Alexandrova.

Fourth seed Coco Gauff needed to battle after a sizzling first set in a 6-1, 7-6 (7/3) victory over fellow American Ann Li.

The 2023 champion had it all her own way in the opening set against her 29th-ranked foe, winning in 30 minutes. The pair exchanged early breaks in the second on the way to a tie-breaker, in which Gauff seized a 4-1 lead and won on her third match point.

“She played better in the second set, and I missed a couple of break opportunities,” Gauff said. “I tried to forget about those.

“It was hard to control the ball for both of us, and it was my first time playing a day match on this centre court, so I had to adjust to that.”

Mirra Andreeva’s French Open reigning champion status counted for little as the fifth seed struggled to close out a 6-1, 7-6 (7/5) victory over Janice Tjen.

The Indonesian challenger, ranked 37, was bowled over in the first set but made Andreeva work to finally advance.

“In the first, I was in command, and she had unforced errors here and there, but in the second, after a couple of games, I started getting nervous. She made fewer mistakes – it turned into a match of mentality and physicality,” Andreeva said.

Eighth seed Elina Svitolina was forced to withdraw before her match against Wang Xiyu with an ankle injury.

“I’ve been advised by the doctors to take a little bit of time to rest and recover completely,” the Ukrainian said in a statement.

Canada’s second-seeded Felix Auger-Aliassime eliminated Argentina’s Juan Manuel Cerundolo 7-5, 6-1 in 90 minutes.

“It was a tricky start, finding my rhythm,” the Canadian said. “Lefties are tricky, you don’t play them so often. You can prepare all you want, but until you step onto the court you can’t find your right adjustments. Then you feel comfortable.”

Washington winner and fifth seed Taylor Fritz fired eight aces in defeating Daniel Merida 6-3, 6-4 in 83 minutes. The Spaniard made 25 unforced errors as Fritz booked a fourth-round match against Australian Chris O’Connell, who is 0-3 against the American.

Last week’s Montreal finalist Nakashima came from the brink to upset fourth seed Medvedev 6-7 (3/7), 7-6 (7/4), 6-1.

Nakashima led 5-2 in the first set before falling in the tie-breaker, then saved three match points in the 10th game of the second set on the way to forcing a third, which he dominated.

Italian 10th seed Lorenzo Musetti defeated American Michael Zheng 6-1, 6-3 in 71 minutes.

Portugal’s Nuno Borges defeated 2021 runner-up Andrey Rublev 6-3, 6-4 in 72 minutes.

The 47th-ranked Borges ended a five-match loss streak in the rivalry, while Rublev will drop from the top 20 for the first time since January 2020.

“I played amazing,” Borges said. “It means a lot to be in the fourth round. It’s a big moment for me.”

articles.title: Kelsey Mitchell ties WNBA scoring record in Fever win over Tempo
articles.summary: The three-time All-Star made history when she registered 20 or more points in a WNBA game for the 20th straight time.
articles.body:
Kelsey Mitchell tied a Women’s National Basketball Association (WNBA) record when she finished with 29 points before sitting out the fourth, while Caitlin Clark added 24 points for the Indiana Fever to beat the Toronto Tempo 101-95 for their fifth straight victory.

Clark and Mitchell have each scored 20 or more in the same game 16 times this season, a WNBA record. Diana Taurasi and Cappie Pondexter did it 15 times with Phoenix in 2008.

list 2 of 4 Barcelona seal deal for World Cup winner Rodri from Manchester City

list 3 of 4 Premier League is back: All to know as the 2026-27 season kicks off

list 4 of 4 Arsenal preview: Five key questions heading into new Premier League season

Mitchell scored 20 or more for the 20th consecutive game on Tuesday, matching Las Vegas’ A’ja Wilson for the longest such streak in WNBA history. But after the Indiana combo guard scored eight points in the span of less than a minute late in the third quarter, she went to the locker room and did not return.

After the game, Fever coach Stephanie White said Mitchell appeared to get “overheated” while playing in a hot environment rather than suffering a serious injury.

Clark added seven assists for the Fever (24-12) and Aliyah Boston chipped in with 16 points. Sophie Cunningham scored 13 points off the bench.

The Tempo (10-24) were outshot 52.9% to 39.1% as they lost their 11th game in a row.

Marina Mabrey led the Tempo with 22 points. Brittney Sykes returned from a foot injury to score 15 points.

Toronto reserve Aneesah Morrow had 14 points and 16 rebounds. Temi Fagbenle added 13 points off the bench and Kiki Rice scored 10.

The Fever opened the fourth quarter with a 12-point lead that increased to 14 when Cunningham made three free throws with 6:45 to play.

But Indiana struggled shooting from the field and that allowed the Tempo to climb back within seven points with 2:55 to play. Makayla Timpson’s steal set up Cunningham for a 3-pointer that gave the Fever a 10-point lead with 1:25 to play.

Mabrey nailed two consecutive 3-pointers to trim the lead to 97-93 with 59 seconds left. After a Fever miss, the Tempo had possession with 21 seconds to play but Mabrey was called for a palming infraction and Rice was whistled for a foul.

The Fever led 33-23 on 61.9% (13-for-21) shooting after one quarter.

The energized Tempo cut the lead to six with 7:10 to play in the second quarter before the Fever surged to score the next 11 points. The Tempo battled back, and Morrow’s 3-pointer completed the first-half scoring and cut the halftime margin to 57-49.

Indiana shot 59% in the first half while Toronto made 42.2%.

Mabrey hit two 2-pointers in the first minute of the third quarter to trim the margin to four.

Mitchell reached 20 points on a driving layup with 6:03 remaining to give Indiana a 10-point lead. Fagbenle’s 3-pointer reduced the lead to five with 2:03 to play, but Indiana finished the third quarter on a 9-2 surge to lead 81-69.

articles.title: Nick Kyrgios provisionally suspended after positive test for cocaine
articles.summary: The Australian said he made no excuses but admitted to struggling with the twilight of his career.
articles.body:
Former Wimbledon finalist Nick Kyrgios was provisionally suspended from tennis after testing positive for cocaine, with the volatile Australian owning up to his “huge mistake” in a public apology.

The International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) on Wednesday announced the suspension of the 31-year-old following a positive test for benzoylecgonine, a cocaine metabolite, from a sample taken during an ATP 250 event in Mallorca in June.

Kyrgios, who reached a career-high rank of 13, has been provisionally suspended since August 4 after a World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) laboratory confirmed the presence of the banned stimulant on July 17.

“I recently failed a drug test in Mallorca after testing positive for cocaine. I made a huge mistake and I take full responsibility for it,” Kyrgios said on Instagram.

“I’m sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors and everyone close to me. Above all, I’m sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets and I’m deeply disappointed in myself.”

Cocaine is classified as a stimulant and substance of abuse on the WADA Prohibited List and is banned in competition under tennis anti-doping rules.

Kyrgios said he made no excuses but painted a picture of a player struggling with the twilight of his career, citing the mental toll of recent injuries.

“I do want to give some context about where I’ve been. The last couple of years of injuries have taken a huge toll on me, both physically and mentally,” he added.

“My body hasn’t been able to do what my mind expects it to do and coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined.

“I’ve always said I didn’t choose tennis – tennis chose me. But letting go of something that has been my whole life is one of the hardest things I’ve ever had to face. At times I’ve felt helpless and alone.”

While suspended, Kyrgios cannot play in, coach at or attend any events organised by World Tennis, WTA, ATP, the Grand Slams or any national association.

The Australian has not appealed the provisional suspension and said he would step away from social media and public life for 28 days to “focus on getting myself right”.

“I’m sorry. I’ll do the work and come back better,” he concluded.

articles.title: Manav Suthar takes 10-wicket haul as India beat Sri Lanka in 600th Test
articles.summary: India take a 1-0 lead with a 165-run win against the hosts in Galle to begin the two-Test series.
articles.body:
Left-arm spinner Manav Suthar finished with a haul of 10 wickets as India thrashed Sri Lanka by 165 runs in the first Test in Galle to take a 1-0 lead in the two-match series.

Suthar, playing only his second Test, impressed with his line and length to ensure India a memorable win on Wednesday in their 600th Test match.

list 2 of 4 Kelsey Mitchell ties WNBA scoring record in Fever win over Tempo

list 3 of 4 Senegal appoint Patrick Vieira as head coach with AFCON qualifiers looming

list 4 of 4 FIFA COO Lamour exits after criticism of Infantino’s World Cup plan

He took four wickets in the first innings and kept up the fine show to take 6-55, helping bowl out the hosts for 206 shortly after lunch on the final day.

Set a target of 372 runs, Sri Lanka’s batters failed to apply themselves, other than Sonal Dinusha, who top-scored in both innings.

Indian captain Shubman Gill called the victory “very satisfying”.

“We were in a comfortable position but were not sure if the match would go on [because of the weather], but the team responded well,” he said.

Gill also praised Suthar and the batsmen for their effort on a wicket that was not easy to score runs on.

“He has been bowling magnificently. Looks like a very promising guy and someone who can play for India for a long time,” he said.

India claimed two wickets in the morning session after Sri Lanka resumed from their overnight score of 84-4 and then quickly ran through the tail.

Captain Dhananjaya de Silva (59) and first-innings centurion Dinusha tried to fight back, batting for more than two hours to add 95 runs for the fifth wicket.

De Silva, who had been dismissed off a no-ball early in his innings, looked set to make the most of the reprieve, posting his 20th half-century.

But his knock ended after he attempted a sweep shot off Ravindra Jadeja and was caught at short fine leg by Suthar.

“It was not easy [batting fourth in Galle],” said de Silva.

“They won the toss, got the runs on the board, and with our batting, we lost wickets, and it went downhill from there.”

Wicketkeeper Niroshan Dickwella posted a half-century in the first innings but could not make an impact in the second.

Dickwella fell for 10 when he attempted to hit Prasidh Krishna over the slips but ended up edging one to the wicketkeeper.

Suthar triggered a late-order collapse with a triple-wicket maiden after lunch and then, in his next over, claimed the last wicket of Keshara Nuwantha as Sri Lanka folded 36 minutes after lunch.

The last four wickets fell for seven runs, with Suthar claiming them all.

The 25-year-old Dinusha (84) put up a solid effort despite little support from his teammates.

Playing his fourth Test, he showcased maturity beyond his age, taking on India’s spinners with nimble footwork.

He was dismissed when Dhruv Jurel at leg slip took a bat-pad catch. He faced 128 deliveries during his defiant knock and hit eight fours and one six.

Apart from Suthar, the other standout performer for India was top-order batter Devdutt Padikkal, who posted 167 and 44 in the game, having come in as a late injury replacement.

“The wicket had its natural wear and tear [but] it was a good Test wicket,” Padikkal said.

“Turned a lot more from the third day onwards. In the end, it was all about who came out on top with their skill-set.”

The teams now head to Colombo for the second Test match, starting on Sunday.

articles.title: 5 Potential Kenny Omega vs. Will Ospreay Outcomes at AEW All In 2026
articles.summary: The main event of All In on August 30 will see Will Ospreay challenge Kenny Omega for the AEW World Championship.
articles.body:
The main event of All In on August 30 will see Will Ospreay challenge Kenny Omega for the AEW World Championship.

For many fans, the outcome seems predictable, but there are several ways we could get to that outcome, and a few possible swerves that could turn things the other way.

This feud has been built up more than any other storyline on the card. Ospreay has been tied to Omega since he debuted with the company, and this feels like their years of history coming to a head.

The Billy Goat will have the home-crowd advantage at Wembley Stadium in London, but Omega seems determined to prove he is the better man.

Let's look at some of the possible outcomes for this match.

If you're a fan of Ospreay, the best possible outcome would be him defeating Omega clean in the middle of the ring to win the belt.

It would be the most satisfying conclusion for a lot of people because it would put all of the focus on Ospreay for his big moment in front of his countrymen in England.

However, some fans will also find this to be one of the most boring possible outcomes because it seems so predictable. It feels like all of this has been set up to put the belt on Ospreay, and if that is what happens, some people might think it was so obvious that AEW should have swerved us instead.

Sadly, you can't please everyone, but if you're a fan of The Billy Goat, you probably want this ending.

A lot of people think Ospreay winning is a foregone conclusion, but there is always the possibility that Tony Khan wants to go a different direction.

Omega winning cleanly would be the most surprising ending to this match, and that is one big reason why it might happen. As exciting as All Elite Wrestling's action can be, it can also be rather predictable with results, so shocking everyone is not out of the question.

AEW has generally favored longer world-title reigns, and with Omega having won the belt only on July 8 after the previous two champions had relatively short reigns, Khan may want to give him a longer run.

The Cleaner hitting the One-Winged Angel to score the win might not go over well in England, but it would make a lot of fans in the U.S. happy.

Part of Ospreay's story with The Death Riders was about Jon Moxley attempting to get him to cross lines he was unwilling to cross, and that eventually led to him cutting ties with Mox and his crew.

But what if Ospreay is willing to get his hands dirty in a different way? He has already said he is calling some of his United Empire buddies, so even if he doesn't try to end Omega's career, he might use his friends to win.

The biggest problem with this outcome is that it would negate a lot of the progress Ospreay made when choosing not to put the plastic bag over Kenny's head.

Turning him heel now wouldn't make a lot of sense, and it would taint his first world title victory for a lot of British fans who will be watching from the stands. That is why this outcome, while possible, is a lot less likely to happen.

The odds of a full heel turn for Omega seem slim, but there is one way this match might end that sees him win due to outside interference.

Ospreay turned on Moxley and The Death Riders leading up to this match, so if Mox wants a little payback, he might see costing Ospreay the title as his best option.

This would allow AEW to keep the belt on Omega for a bit while kicking off a full Moxley vs. Ospreay feud at the same time, which is going to happen eventually anyway.

A dirty finish to a main event is never ideal, but this is one of the times when it would make sense for storytelling purposes. Moxley might even succeed in making The Billy Goat cross his own boundaries by making him too angry to keep his cool after the loss.

An Ospreay who is at the end of his rope and wants revenge might even be more interesting than having him win the world title at this point.

The Death Riders getting involved not only creates the possibility of Omega retaining, but it could also lead to neither man actually winning.

Imagine this. Ospreay and Omega have a great back-and-forth match that feels like it's building to the finish, and then Moxley and his cohorts appear to destroy both men.

This would definitely be the least popular outcome proposed in this article, but this is pro wrestling, so all things are possible until a decision is made by management.

Having Mox take out both men and declare his intentions to regain the title would put Ospreay and Omega back on the same side temporarily. It could even lead to The Billy Goat teaming up with The Elite to battle The Death Riders in one of AEW's big stipulations like Stadium Stampede or Blood and Guts.

This wouldn't be a satisfying conclusion to All In, but we have to consider it as a possibility.

How do you think Ospreay vs. Omega will end at All In?

articles.title: Adam 'Edge' Copeland Reveals WWE Denied John Cena's Retirement Match Following Rumors amid AEW Run
articles.summary: During John Cena's retirement tour last year in which he stepped in the ring with many of his past WWE rivals, one name missing from the group was Edge in part because he had left to join AEW back in 2023.
articles.body:
During John Cena's retirement tour last year in which he stepped in the ring with many of his past WWE rivals, one name missing from the group was Edge in part because he had left to join AEW back in 2023.

Appearing on The Ariel Helwani Show , Adam Copeland was asked about the rumors he might have been the one to show up as Cena's final opponent last December.

The most interesting nugget is Copeland saying AEW president Tony Khan "absolutely" would have allowed him to do it, but he "never pursued" it knowing WWE would never consider it.

Copeland did note his original AEW contract might have expired in time for him to make a return appearance in WWE last year, but his time off due to injuries and film projects extended his tenure. He also made it clear he intends to spend the rest of his career with AEW.

"Yes. Yeah. That's where I want to," he said about ending his career in AEW. "I know that may disappoint a lot of people, but I love it there."

Appearing on Helwani's show last November (h/t Ethan Schlabaugh of SI.com), Khan confirmed WWE never reached out about letting Copeland wrestle Cena at some point during the latter's retirement run.

Even though one last Cena-Edge match never occurred, the two did pay tribute to each other in matches last year.

The onscreen rivalry between Edge and Cena throughout the mid-2000s was instrumental in elevating both men to superstardom. Cena was already on his way there, but Edge got a huge boost from the feud.

Edge won his first singles world title in WWE by defeating Cena at New Year's Revolution in January 2006 when he cashed in his Money in the Bank briefcase that he won the previous year at WrestleMania.

Cena and Copeland wrestled against each other 62 times , either in singles, tag or multi-person matches, in WWE.

The Rated R Superstar went on to become an 11-time WWE/world heavyweight champion before departing the company in 2023.

Since debuting in AEW, Copeland has primarily been paired with Christian Cage. The duo won the AEW tag team titles by defeating FTR in an I Quit match at Double or Nothing in May.

Copeland and Cage are next set to defend the championships against the Young Bucks at All In on Aug. 30.

articles.title: Panthers' Brad Marchand Trolls Maple Leafs' William Nylander Over Workout Photo
articles.summary: A potentially delayed start to the 2026-27 season hasn't stopped Florida Panthers star Brad Marchand from chirping his future opponents.
articles.body:
A potentially delayed start to the 2026-27 season hasn't stopped Florida Panthers star Brad Marchand from chirping his future opponents.

Marchand responded Tuesday to a photo shared on the NHL's Instagram of the Toronto Maple Leafs' William Nylander lifting.

"Don't hurt yourself with all that weight willy," Marchand wrote.

Marchand recently said in a video posted to social media he had undergone offseason surgery.

The forward was sidelined for the end of the 2025-26 season with something head coach Paul Maurice said he had been dealing with "for a couple of months."

Marchand said in a video posted earlier this month he had been trying to treat the issue without surgery but ultimately "had to kind of do it last minute."

It is not clear when Marchand will be able to rejoin the Panthers, which are set to open training camp within the next month prior to opening the regular season Sept. 29 against the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes.

The Panthers will hope to have him back in the lineup by the time the team faces Nylander and the Leafs on Dec. 3 in Toronto.

articles.title: NHL Announces 'Hometown Remix' Uniform Initiative for All Teams Ahead of 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: The NHL is introducing new special edition uniforms for each team during the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
The NHL is introducing new special edition uniforms for each team during the 2026-27 season.

"Hometown Remix" jerseys inspired by each team's local culture will be released during the upcoming season, the NHL announced Wednesday.

The initiative is part of the NHL's partnership with Fanatics, which has been producing the league's uniforms since the 2024-25 season.

The partnership made Fanatics the NHL's official uniform supplier through the 2034-35 season.

NHL EVP of marketing Brian Jennings told ESPN's Greg Wyshynski when the deal was first announced in 2023 that Fanatics would look at adding a new specialty jersey around the 2026-27 campaign.

The NHL previously produced apparel through a partnership with Adidas. That partnership featured specialty jerseys as part of the Reverse Retro collection .

That promotion, which featured jerseys inspired by each franchise's past, featured drops in 2020 and 2022, respectively.

Since the Fanatics partnership began in 2024, the NHL has only introduced specialty jerseys for single-game promotions such as the Winter Classic or Stadium Series.

Fanatics has previously been involved in manufacturing locally-inspired uniforms through the brand's partnership with Nike and MLB, which began its City Connect collection in 2021.

The NBA, which has its uniforms supplied by Nike, began its own collection of locally-inspired uniforms when the league launched the City Edition collection in 2017.

The NHL's specialty jerseys will be released alongside a general collection of Fanatics apparel inspired by the new design, the NHL reported.

More details about the uniforms will be released after the NHL opens the regular season on Tuesday, Sept. 29, according to the league.

articles.title: Supplements: what do athletes take and why?
articles.summary: There is a long list of supplements taken by elite athletes in the pursuit of marginal gains - what do they take and why?
articles.body:
It was at the 1992 Olympics in Barcelona when the mutterings about a new "secret weapon" started.

Dozens of Great Britain athletes had been taking a new product that increased muscle mass and improved athletic performance â a "wonder pill" that didn't fall foul of any doping rules.

Now found in tubs and bags on many supermarket shelves and tagged in your social feeds, it is the supplement of choice for millions of people and one of the most scientifically researched.

But back then, when it came on the scene at the very top of British elite sport, there were suspicions and stigma around the use of any substance described as 'performance enhancing' â even if it was legal.

From the minute an athlete wakes, to the moment they go to bed, they are thinking about how they can optimise their performance and recovery.

Today, creatine is just one of a long list of supplements taken by elite athletes in this pursuit of marginal gains. Some help with muscle size and strength, while others correct deficiencies in the diet.

"There are various reports in the literature of some studies that say maybe up to 90% of athletes take supplements. I often jokingly say that means 10% are lying," says Prof Graeme Close, professor of human physiology at Liverpool John Moores University.

"The sports teams that I've worked in, I think that's probably closer to 100% of athletes will be taking some form of supplementation."

So, what do supplements actually do and why do athletes take them? And in the world of strict liability, where elite athletes are solely responsible for what they put in their bodies, how do they make sure they stay clean?

While experts like Close advocate for seeking to meet nutritional needs through food in the first instance, it may not always be possible or practical to do this - and that is where supplements come in.

Take, for example, creatine, which is found naturally in meat and fish.

"You would need the best part of a kilogram of raw chicken a day to get the amount of creatine you need," says Close. But it is unsafe to eat raw poultry because of the food poisoning risk from harmful bacteria.

Creatine is a natural compound in the body produced in the kidneys, liver and pancreas. It is a quick source of energy for muscles, which is especially important for short-duration, high intensity activities such as sprinting.

Its big break as a supplement came in the 1990s when two scientists who had been researching it for two decades shared their findings with Steve Jennings, whose Maxim sports nutrition company supplied products to the British Olympic team.

During the 1992 Barcelona Games, investigative reporter Doug Gillon had learned of a 'secret trial' involving British athletes and seen a box of their Ergomax C150 â effervescent creatine tablets. He wrote that if the scientists' claims - that creatine could improve explosive athletic performance by 1-3% - were true, then "sport may never be the same again".

In terms of sport supplements and nutrition, he was right. By the time of the next Olympics in 1996, an estimated 80% of athletes were taking creatine, and since then it has become mainstream, with research suggesting there may be cognitive benefits as well as physical.

According to the Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition, the creatine breakthrough of the 1990s had "launched a new era in sports nutrition" and "sparked exploration into other supplements".

The global dietary supplements market size was valued at $209.5bn (Â£154bn) in 2025 and is projected to grow to $431.7bn (Â£317.4bn) by 2033, according to Grand View Research. , external

Close, who oversaw nutrition for last year's British and Irish Lions rugby union tour, sees supplements as the "final piece of the jigsaw" rather than a starting point.

"What we're talking about is small margins of benefit, where actually these athletes who focus on the food, I think what you often find is that they've got the big-ticket items right," he says.

"So they're seeing great performance benefits because their overall diet is immaculate.

"They might be missing out on the one per-centers, but they've really nailed the 99 per-centers. And they often do better than those who chase the one per-centers but have not given enough attention to the 99 per-centers."

Australian cyclist Nicole Frain agrees, adding: "I'm a pretty big believer that they are called sport supplements. They are there to supplement the things you already do right.

"I don't think supplements are the answer to fix my problems.

"You need to be eating a balanced diet, training well, sleeping right, recovering well, hydrating â all of those things â before we add in all of the extras."

Close puts protein powders top of the list of supplements taken by athletes he works with, followed by creatine and vitamin D.

Protein powders maximise muscle repair and contribute to muscle growth, while creatine is a quick source of energy for muscles and important in short-duration, high-intensity activities like sprinting. Vitamin D, meanwhile, is essential for bone health and supports muscle function.

Other popular supplements include carbohydrate gels, which Close says were key in the first sub-two hour marathon run earlier this year by Kenyan long-distance runner Sabastian Sawe.

"As sport nutritionists we were all fascinated at what the fuelling programme was, and it was the sports drinks and gels that played a huge part of that fuelling," Close says.

"There was a calculation done of what it would take to break the two-hour marathon, and that did involve making sure that over 100 grams of supplemental carbohydrate were ingested per hour.

"And the reports coming out of the recent sub-two-hour marathon was that it was 110 grams of carbohydrate per hour that was achieved."

Supplements can improve performance, but there is an uneasy ring to describing them as 'performance enhancing' because of the association with banned substances and anti-doping rule violations.

So what determines whether something is on the World Anti-Doping Agency's (Wada) banned list?

"For Wada to put anything on the list, it's got to hit two out of three criteria: dangerous to health, performance enhancing, and against the spirit of sport," Close explains.

"So just because something enhances performance, if it's not dangerous to health and not against the spirit of sport, Wada will not touch it.

"Though something like an anabolic steroid, where it's against the spirit of sport to be injecting yourself for a performance benefit, it's dangerous to health and it's performance enhancing - that hits all three."

But taking a supplement still carries anti-doping risks.

"No guarantee can be given that any particular supplement is free from prohibited substances," UK Anti-Doping advice states, urging athletes to "be vigilant" in using them.

And if you test positive for a prohibited substance, consuming it unintentionally can result in the same four-year ban as if you deliberately took it.

There are supplement-testing programmes which batch test products before they are sold to make sure they do not contain any Wada-prohibited substances.

One of those is Informed Sport, which says as many as one in 10 supplements is contaminated with ingredients and compounds prohibited in sport and points to a study carried out by the Anti-Doping Knowledge Centre that showed product contamination was responsible for 8% of all anti-doping violations between 2005 and 2022.

While Informed Sport is a very well used system among athletes, Wada makes it clear that quality assurance schemes can reduce but do not eliminate the risk of an anti-doping infringement.

If you do accept the risk, you need to be organised to keep track.

In the case of Great Britain rower Heidi Long, it takes a spreadsheet.

"I've recorded the batch number of every product that I've taken and its expiry date because if you take it after the expiry date the Informed Sport [certification] is no longer viable," she says.

Close says he has also done site visits to factories to see where the supplements are made to check the manufacturing processes because "the risk of failing a drugs test is huge".

There are risks to the general population too, he adds, saying: "You can be buying supplements off the internet that are made in somebody's garage and you've got no idea of the manufacturing processes."

He points to studies on creatine products which have found there is no creatine in them and so "you're completely wasting your money" and that in the worst case scenario it may contain substances that are dangerous to your health.

"So it is really important that the message is that while they can play a small role, the safety considerations are the key factor," he says.

There is, however, more than one way for an elite athlete to chase a competitive edge â and some are going back to basics.

For every trending supplement, there is an unprocessed, wholefood alternative â from the anti-inflammatory benefits of turmeric, staving off cramp with pickle juice or consumption of high-nitrate foods like beetroot before competition.

It is what Close calls a "food-first" or "food-only" approach and something he says every athlete should use as a starting point.

The latest to have its moment in the spotlight is an ancient Ethiopian grain called teff.

Used for thousands of years in traditional east African diets, teff is now making its mark globally in performance nutrition.

In comparison to other popular grains like wheat, rice and quinoa, teff has a high mineral content and is rich in calcium, iron and vitamin C. Naturally gluten-free and good for the gut, it is also unique for being a 'complete' protein, meaning it provides all nine essential amino acids required for human nutrition.

These superfood credentials have caught the attention of some of the world's best athletes over the years, from Olympic champion marathon runner Haile Gebrselassie to seven-time Grand Slam singles champion Venus Williams, and it is now becoming a more common sight on UK supermarket shelves.

British boxer Fran Hennessy was introduced to teff by her nutritionist and it is now part of her daily routine.

"I've never looked back," she says. "What I'm putting in my body is good fuel and energy and teff has so much. It energises you so much before a workout and it gives you the fibre you need."

As well as boosting her performances, Hennessy credits teff with being key to recovery.

She says: "Each meal I'm having there's a reason behind and everything that's in it there's a reason behind... I know what I'm putting in my body is fuelling me, recovering me, energising me."

Cost is another consideration when athletes are deciding on supplements.

"The supplement industry is really expensive," says Long. "And we're definitely not made of money. So I think it's really picking and choosing when you want to put that investment in."

She says it makes sense to have more supplements around racing time "when the performance is super critical and very time dependent".

"[But] on a daily basis if I can get the protein intake from my dinner and a glass of milk or yoghurt and breakfast then actually I was going to be eating that food anyway so it's not as expensive."

"I would much rather enjoy a coffee in the morning with friends or while I'm working rather than have one of the gels," she says. "Some of the gels ... you'll end up holding your nose when you take it.

"I guess it's just like the enjoyment of what you're taking, you know, it's nicer to eat food than it is to take supplements."

articles.title: Los datos más sorprendentes de Premier Padel: una promesa como el jugador con más ganadores
articles.standfirst: Aimar Goñi se cuela como uno de los grandes protagonistas de la primera mitad de año
articles.summary: Aimar Goñi se cuela como uno de los grandes protagonistas de la primera mitad de año
articles.body: El frenetismo de Premier Padel, con decenas de pruebas cada temporada, hace que muchas veces no quede tiempo para analizar lo que ocurre tras cada torneo. Sin embargo, las semanas de descanso que atraviesa el circuito profesional sirven como punto de inflexión para sacar a la luz algunas de las estadísticas más relevantes de lo que va de curso, con varias sorpresas en las categorías más cotizadas. El portal ‘Padel Intelligence’, referente en el análisis de datos, ha publicado el balance de su base de datos de la primera parte del año. Entre las métricas más destacadas figura la del jugador con más winners por partido en lo que va de 2026, un privilegio que se ha llevado una de las grandes revelaciones del circuito: Aimar Goñi. El navarro ha brillado con su pegada y envergadura, liderando la tabla con 30,3 golpes ganadores por encuentro. Le siguen, a bastante distancia, Ale Galán con 24,4 y Javi Garrido con 23,3. Aimar empezó la campaña junto a Enri Goenaga, pero ha sido al lado de Edu Alonso con quien ha logrado explotar en los últimos meses. Su compañero es un drive clásico, sin tanto poderío aéreo, lo que permite al joven revés asumir galones y maximizar sus cualidades ofensivas. Esos espectaculares 30,3 winners nacen principalmente de su smash, faceta donde también lidera el circuito con 13,6 remates ganadores por partido. En esta estadística le sigue de nuevo Galán (11,9), mientras que Javi Leal cierra el podio con 11,4. Sin embargo, el recurso de Goñi no se limita al remate. El navarro también ocupa el primer puesto en ganadores de volea, con 8,75 por choque, situándose por encima de Arturo Coello (7,10) y de Ale Galán (7,02), a quien el consenso general señala como el mejor voleador del planeta. El volumen de winners exige asumir riesgos, y las cifras de Aimar se entienden mejor al observar sus errores no forzados. Jon Sanz es el jugador que más fallos ha acumulado en estos meses, con 16,35 por encuentro. Justo por detrás aparece el propio Goñi, con 15,21 errores no forzados por partido. Es ahí donde reside el gran margen de mejora del revés navarro: si logra sostener su producción ofensiva reduciendo el número de concesiones, se consolidará entre los mejores del planeta. El espejo donde mirarse en términos de consistencia es Coki Nieto, quien lidera la clasificación de los jugadores más fiables. El madrileño comete apenas 5,8 errores no forzados por duelo. Le siguen Martín Di Nenno con 6,8 y Lucas Bergamini con 6,9. En el pádel de élite, la fiabilidad para forzar el fallo ajeno resulta tan determinante como la capacidad para definir. Estas métricas ofrecen además un reflejo fiel de las dinámicas de pareja. Jon Sanz, el jugador que más falla, asume mayores riesgos al estar respaldado por la solidez de Nieto, el que menos concede. Por su parte, Bergamini sostiene el esquema de una dupla cuyo compañero figura entre los principales rematadores. En esa lista de pegadores ya no aparece Leo Augsburger, líder el año pasado, ya que la presencia de Juan Lebrón a su lado equilibra el reparto de tareas ofensivas. Ocurre lo contrario con Goñi o Galán, acompañados por perfiles de contención que exigen un mayor volumen de resolución por su parte. El caso más ilustrativo es el de los número uno. Ni Arturo Coello ni Agustín Tapia encabezan de forma aislada estas clasificaciones individuales, pero su equilibrio entre un volumen altísimo de definición repartido entre ambos y una tasa de error reducida —sin llegar a los mínimos de Nieto o Di Nenno debido a su estilo agresivo— los consolida en lo más alto del ranking de Premier Padel.

articles.title: Top seeds Sabalenka, Zverev knocked out of Cincinnati Open
articles.summary: World No 1 Aryna Sabalenka stunned by Sara Bejlek, while French Open champion Alexander Zverev exits after fourth round.
articles.body:
Top seeds Aryna Sabalenka and Alexander Zverev crashed out of the Cincinnati Open in a matter of hours on a rainy fourth-round day of action.

American Tommy Paul saved a match point on the way to a 4-6, 7-6 (8/6), 6-4 upset of Germany’s Zverev on Wednesday.

list 2 of 4 Premier League form guide: Ranking the title contenders for 2026-27 season

list 3 of 4 Mourinho fires Real Madrid shot at Barcelona saying he ‘didn’t need’ Rodri

list 4 of 4 Arsenal preview: Five key questions heading into new Premier League season

But the biggest shock came on the women’s side, where Czech Sara Bejlek, ranked 35th, stunned world number one Sabalenka 7-6 (9/7), 6-4 in a gritty match that finished up shortly after the clock ticked past midnight into Thursday morning.

Former champion Sabalenka led by a break in the opening set and was up 5-1 in the tiebreaker before Bejlek roared back to pocket the set in 65 minutes.

Bejlek broke the Belarusian three times in the second set, rallying from 4-1 down and securing the win with a love game capped by an ace.

“I lost my words – it feels incredible,” Bejlek said after her first win over a top 10 player.

“I was playing what I was feeling and not really thinking. I was trying not to be nervous and just play. I believed in myself no matter what.”

Bejlek, who won the Abu Dhabi hard court title in February as a qualifier, booked a quarterfinal clash with American Madison Keys.

It was yet another setback for Sabalenka as the start of the US Open looms on August 30.

The four-time Grand Slam champion was ousted in the fourth round of the Toronto Masters last week, having lost in the same round at Wimbledon and in the quarterfinals at Roland Garros.

Zverev’s match was interrupted by rain for 90 minutes in the seventh game of the second set and had two more five-minute pauses as drops were dried from the court.

French Open champion Zverev had a chance to close it out at 6-5 in the second-set tiebreaker but stuffed a volley into the net.

The German again gained an edge in the deciding set with a break for 4-2, but Paul broke back in the next game and again for a 5-4 lead on the way to his third win over Zverev in their last four meetings.

“I’m not sure how I did it,” Paul said. “I put some returns in, he gave me some looks at second serves and he threw in a few doubles (faults). That always helps a tonne.

“I went after the ball a bit more, I was having fun out there.”

Second seed Felix Auger-Aliassime of Canada was another casualty, falling 6-3, 6-4 to American Frances Tiafoe.

Zverev’s conqueror Paul next faces Roland Garros runner-up Flavio Cobolli, who laboured two and a half hours to engineer a turnaround against red-hot Spaniard Rafael Jodar 4-6, 7-6 (7/3), 6-3.

American sixth seed Taylor Fritz dispatched Australian Chris O’Connell 6-4, 6-3.

Thiago Tirante, who upset Novak Djokovic in the second round, continued his surprise run, reaching his first Masters quarterfinal with a 5-7, 6-4, 6-4 victory over Jakub Mensik.

Australian Alex de Minaur was no match for Frenchman Arthur Fils, who cruised to a 6-3, 6-4 victory over the fifth seed.

The women’s 2023 champion Coco Gauff saved all eight break points she faced in a 6-3, 6-2 win over Czech Marie Bouzkova.

The fourth seed double-faulted on her first match point but leapt up to smash an overhead winner on her second chance.

“I played well the whole match, going for my shots, coming forward and not letting her counter-punch,” Gauff said. “I’m happy with how I played.”

Defending women’s champion Iga Swiatek needed four match points to get past Diane Parry of France 6-3, 6-3.

The seventh-seeded Pole now faces a rerun of last week’s Toronto final against Elena Rybakina, who beat Diana Shnaider 6-4, 6-4.

Six-time Grand Slam champion Swiatek captured her first title of 2026 with her victory over reigning Australian Open champion Rybakina in Toronto.

Two other current Grand Slam champions bowed out.

Ukraine’s Marta Kostyuk rallied from a set down to beat French Open winner Mirra Andreeva 4-6, 6-0, 6-2.

Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova fell to Amanda Anisimova 6-1, 6-4 in another weather-disrupted match.

articles.title: Max Verstappen signs new F1 contract with Red Bull until 2030
articles.summary: Four-time F1 World Drivers’ Champion’s new deal puts to rest rumours that he would exit the team at the end of 2028.
articles.body:
Multiple Formula One world champion Max Verstappen has signed a new contract with Red Bull Racing until the end of 2030, the team announced, ending speculation over his future in the sport.

“Four more years of full send. We are delighted to announce that Max has signed a contract extension with the team until the end of 2030,” Red Bull said on X on Thursday.

list 1 of 3 Messi scores emotional first goal since father’s death in draw versus Union

list 2 of 3 Tennis: Top seeds Sabalenka, Zverev knocked out of Cincinnati Open

list 3 of 3 Premier League form guide: Ranking the title contenders for 2026-27 season

The news came with preparations in full swing for Verstappen’s home race this Sunday, the Dutch Grand Prix in Zandvoort, and will delight his thousands of orange-clad fans.

Verstappen is one of the most successful Formula One drivers of all time, dominating the sport with four consecutive world championships from 2021.

But results have been harder to come by this season, with the 28-year-old failing to see a chequered flag in the first half of the year and sitting sixth in the drivers’ championship.

“This commitment is about more than continuing an already extraordinary alliance,” the team said in its statement.

“It is a powerful statement of mutual trust and ambition – and a shared decision to shape the future together.”

The uncompetitive nature of the Red Bull car this year has led many to speculate that the mercurial Dutchman could switch to another team or even leave Formula One entirely.

But Verstappen said he was keen to get the team back to winning ways.

“We have the best people and I’m excited to keep working together with everyone to get back to the top again,” he was quoted as saying.

The news adds even more spice to the last-ever edition of the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort.

Verstappen was unbeatable on his home track, winning the first three editions since it was reintroduced to the circuit in 2021.

But he has since been chasing McLaren in his own back yard, with Papaya drivers Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri claiming the last two races.

Verstappen is expected to don a special helmet for the occasion, inspired by the famous blue Delft pottery.

The promoters decided not to continue racing at Zandvoort, partly due to uncertainty over Verstappen’s future given his importance for the popularity of the event.

“I have always said it: The team is like a second family for me and I feel very at home,” said Verstappen.

“I came to the team hoping to be able to win races. What we went on to achieve together has been simply lovely,” added Verstappen, using his trademark phrase.

articles.title: Revolución en Hyundai: su superventas Tucson cambia tanto que no lo reconocerás
articles.standfirst: La quinta generación del superventas coreano estrena un diseño mucho más contundente, gana espacio y recupera algo que muchos conductores echaban de menos: los botones físicos
articles.summary: La quinta generación del superventas coreano estrena un diseño mucho más contundente, gana espacio y recupera algo que muchos conductores echaban de menos: los botones físicos
articles.body: El Tucson es la joya de la corona de Hyundai: el modelo más vendido de la marca coreana en Europa en el último lustro de forma constante... y el SUV compacto preferido por el público del continente. Por eso ha puesto toda la carne en el asador para su renovación. Salta a la vista que es una renovación/revolución en lo estético la que Hyundai ha aplicado para la quinta generación, que se presentará mundialmente en el próximo Salón del Automóvil de París (a mediados de octubre). El nuevo Tucson no se parecerá a otros modelos de la marca coreana... siguiendo una estrategia de diseño muy particular, en la que casi cada modelo tiene identidad propia. Sí que vemos rasgos familiares en el concepto de iluminación frontal, con una tira horizontal que cruza todo el morro como ya sucede en el Kona, pero reinterpretado. Pero el resto de sus líneas son más dramáticas, lejos de la redondez del modelo actual.  Es un Tucson más cuadrado y rectilineo, adoptando un estilo más parecido a sus primos de Kia y a su hermano mayor, el Santa Fe, pero con una personalidad distinta.  En cuanto a dimensiones, el nuevo Tucson crece seis centímetros hasta los 4,7 metros y también es más ancho (+4 cm) y con más distancia entre ejes (+3 cm). Con estas cifras cabe esperar una mejor habitabilidad interior, aparte de una presencia más contundente sobre la carretera. Eso sí, su nueva talla es más de SUV grande que de compacto, por lo que quizá sus rivales cambien y el Tucson 2027 mire hacia modelos como el Toyota RAV4, el Skoda Kodiaq El interior también da un vuelco total... donde lo más destacado no es el nuevo concepto de cuadro de relojes (minimalista) o la gran pantalla central. Lo que más destaca es la vuelta de los botones físicos Sobre las mecánicas, de momento sólo se ha confirmado que habrá versiones híbridas y enchufables, aunque es probable que se mantengan versiones térmicas como complemento. Más difícil será ver un Tucson eléctrico, algo que de momento Hyundai reserva para su gama Ioniq. En las fotos que Hyundai ha ofrecido para el lanzamiento también aparece una versión XRT con una estética off road aún más extrema, algo que ya había mostrado en el Santa Fe.

articles.title: WWE's Growing Problem with Oba Femi
articles.summary: Oba Femi has had a breakout year for WWE, enjoying a magical run through the main roster that has seen him dominate the competition, defeat Brock Lesnar in two of their three wars and win the King of the Ring tournament.
articles.body:
Oba Femi has had a breakout year for WWE, enjoying a magical run through the main roster that has seen him dominate the competition, defeat Brock Lesnar in two of their three wars and win the King of the Ring tournament.

Femi is incredibly popular with fans and looks every bit the future star that Lesnar labeled him at the conclusion of their Hell in a Cell Match at SummerSlam.

However, The Ruler's meteoric rise and early career triumphs are not without a significant growing problem for WWE.

Femi exploded onto the scene in WWE and within three months of his main roster call-up, defeated Lesnar clean and in the center of the ring.

He lost the next matchup, but put an end to The Beast Incarnate's Hall of Fame-worthy career inside the unforgiving confines of Hell in a Cell at SummerSlam in their third encounter.

There is no better way for WWE to have introduced Femi to the fans and announced him as the next big thing than the way he has been booked.

However, when a star arrives in WWE and immediately conquers the seemingly unconquerable, there are only so many directions they can go and still maintain their momentum.

For Femi, beating and retiring Lesnar was a blessing and a curse in that the only logical next step for him is vanquishing Roman Reigns or CM Punk and claiming one of the company's top two titles.

WWE, however, appears content to deliver the slow build, with Femi likely winning the men's Royal Rumble match in January 2027 and challenging for one of those titles at WrestleMania 43.

The Show of Shows is still nearly nine months away.

The only thing that can possibly happen between now and then is that Femi loses momentum. Even his rivalry with Bron Breakker, a showdown between two men expected to carry WWE well into the future, feels like a step down for The Ruler.

That is not an indictment of Breakker. There are levels to this, though, and to suggest he has not been adversely affected by baffling creative would be an understatement.

A match with Femi clearly means more to Breakker than it does to The Ruler.

That there is unlikely to be a clean finish means the two will keep each other busy for a few months. That will benefit one half of the pairing while leaving fans to speculate when Femi will step up to Reigns.

WWE Creative has not had the best track record over the last two years, with head-scratching decisions hurting story progression, leading to nonsensical developments and stunting the growth of some of its top young stars.

Case in point, Breakker, who returned at WrestleMania 42, defeated Seth Rollins at Backlash, but ultimately lost that feud and has been saddled in a tag team with Austin Theory ever since.

It would be fair to question whether WWE can effectively push Femi in a way that does not undo everything it has accomplished with him to this point.

One loss here, or a bad segment of TV there, could do considerable damage and threaten it all. Lesnar put Femi in a prime position to go out and succeed as the new smashing badass in WWE.

If someone in the room overthinks a single match or moment, it could unravel, and Femi's aura and popularity will be adversely affected. Again, nine months is a long time, with plenty of opportunities for someone to make a call that sabotages the biggest slam dunk the company has had in decades.

Yes, WWE has carefully booked Femi to this point, except for the guaranteed title shot he willingly gave up to battle Lesnar at SummerSlam. But that was a momentary lapse with little ill-effect.

The company will not be that lucky if it fails him on the road to what feels like an inevitable and appropriate coronation as soon as WrestleMania next spring.

Holding off on crowning Femi champion at that event would only deepen WWE's growing problem.

articles.title: Max Verstappen, Red Bull F1 Agree to 4-Year Contract Extension amid Mercedes Rumors
articles.summary: Red Bull Racing announced Thursday that Max Verstappen has signed an extension through the 2030 Formula One season.
articles.body:
Red Bull Racing announced Thursday that Max Verstappen has signed an extension through the 2030 Formula One season.

"I am really pleased with the contract extension," the four-time F1 champion said . "We have the best people and I'm excited to keep working together with everyone to get back to the top again. This remains the ultimate goal that all of us have been working towards and will continue to pursue. I want to thank Red Bull, (team principal Laurent Mekies) and everyone at Oracle Red Bull Racing for the trust they put in me."

York Responded to Ad on Prostitution Site Before Arrest

Verstappen was runner-up to Lando Norris in the 2025 drivers' standings. He had a sluggish start to the year and mounted a comeback attempt in the second half.

Back in March, the 28-year-old suggested he could walk away from Formula One altogether at the end of the current season.

Verstappen's performance on the track added some more uncertainty , with Mercedes having been linked with a blockbuster move in the past. More recently, McLaren emerged as a possible option .

Alas, Verstappen continues to believe in Red Bull's direction, and this is a significant show of faith in Mekies, who replaced Christian Horner as team principal last July.

Verstappen sits sixth in the standings and has yet to notch a victory. At the very least, any title challenge is likely out of the question, and remaining in sixth would be his worst finish since 2017.

The Dutchman's new contract ties him to Red Bull for the remainder of the decade. In theory, that should provide further doubt as to his status for the foreseeable future.

Should Verstappen's malaise extend into 2027 and beyond, the same concerns could once again emerge.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz confirms US Open return after four-month injury layoff
articles.summary: Spanish tennis star had missed the French Open, ‌Wimbledon and the hard-court events in Toronto and Cincinnati.
articles.body:
Carlos ‌Alcaraz will return to competitive tennis at ⁠the US ⁠Open, ending a more than four-month absence caused by a wrist injury , in ⁠a bid to defend his title in New York.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion confirmed ⁠on Thursday that he will play the August 30-September 13 tournament after withdrawing from the Barcelona Open in April and missing the French Open, ‌Wimbledon and the North American hard-court events in Toronto and Cincinnati.

list 1 of 4 Tennis star Kyrgios provisionally suspended after positive test for cocaine

list 2 of 4 Tennis: Top seeds Sabalenka, Zverev knocked out of Cincinnati Open

list 3 of 4 Sabalenka cruises through as Medvedev falls to Nakashima at Cincinnati Open

list 4 of 4 Tennis: Williams sisters fall in doubles return at Cincinnati Open

Alcaraz had initially targeted Cincinnati, where he won last year, for his comeback. But he opted to give his wrist more time to recover.

He has gradually ⁠increased his workload in recent ⁠weeks and trained with Denmark’s Holger Rune in Murcia as he tested the injury at higher intensity.

His return was also ⁠given a football-style announcement on Instagram by transfer reporter Fabrizio Romano, who posted “Here we go!” ⁠alongside confirmation that Alcaraz would be back at the US Open.

New York holds particular significance for Alcaraz. He won ‌his first Grand Slam title at Flushing Meadows in 2022, becoming the youngest player to reach ‌world ‌number one in the Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) rankings.

Alcaraz became the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam in January with his triumph, at age 22, at the Australian Open.

He added the ATP hard court title in Doha in February.

But after withdrawing in Barcelona he pulled out of tournaments in Madrid and Rome before withdrawing from Roland Garros, where he was the two-time reigning champion.

articles.summary: Harden previously declined $42.3m player ⁠option on his contract in bid to secure a multi-year basketball deal.
articles.body:
Former NBA MVP ‌and 11-time All-Star guard James ⁠Harden ⁠has agreed to a new three-year, $97m contract to return to the Cleveland ⁠Cavaliers, his agents told ESPN on Thursday.

Per his agents at Equity Sports, ⁠the deal includes a player option for the 2028-29 US basketball season and a trade kicker.
