articles.title: Super League: St Helens keep play-off hopes alive with victory against Castleford as Toulouse and Hull both win
articles.summary: St Helens keep their play-off hopes alive with victory over Castleford, despite finishing with 10 men; Hull KR slump to a second home Super League defeat of the week and Jake Arthur lands a late drop goal to seal a thrilling fightback for Hull
articles.body:
St Helens called on six different try-scorers to beat Castleford 36-12 and keep their play-off hopes alive, despite finishing the match at the Brewdog Stadium with only 10 men.

It has been a dramatic week for Castleford, whose former head coach Ryan Carr announced he was leaving the club for "personal reasons" on Friday.

Saints also announced a coaching change this week, with Kevin Walters due to join from next season.

  • Super League's Final Charge: Seven teams in contention
  • Super League fixtures & results | Super League table
  • Get Sky Sports or stream contract-free on NOW
  • Choose the Sky Sports notifications you want

The Australian's new side took an early lead, and tries from Jack Welsby, Shane Wright, Jacob Douglas, Tom Humphreys and Tristan Sailor made it 30-0 before the break.

Captain Jackson Hastings had added five goals, but lost his cool and was sent off after an altercation with Tyler Dupree for violent conduct.

Dupree was sin-binned for the same incident, and tempers continued to flare as the teams disappeared down the tunnel for the break.

Nene McDonald added a sixth try for the hosts after the break, making a Castleford comeback look increasingly unlikely.

Louis Senior and Laulu-Togaga'e finally got them on the board, before Saints finished the game with 10 men after Alex Walmsley and Chris Matagi were both sent to the sin bin.

St Helens interim boss Eamon O'Carroll told BBC Radio Merseyside: "I said I wanted to see the attitude of the players, and what better way to display that than when you go down to 10 men for 45 minutes?

"The players were fantastic. We simplified a few things, which probably helped, because everyone knew what the role was and their position."

Commenting on Hastings' dismissal, Castleford director of rugby Chris Chester told Sky Sports: "Scott Murrell just jumped (in the way of Dupree). We all know the rules, you can't punch people in the face.

"We'll let the disciplinary (match review panel) deal with those kinds of things. That's what they're there for."

Hull KR slump to another home defeat

Hull KR slumped to a second home defeat of the week as Toulouse ran out deserved 32-12 winners following a ruthless second half at Craven Park.

The Robins were beaten at home by play-off rivals Warrington on Tuesday night, and head coach Willie Peters dropped both Tevita Pangai Junior and Mikey Lewis following their upcoming bans which were handed out in the wake of the 34-28 defeat against the Wolves.

It was a scrappy start - much to the frustration of the expectant Hull KR fans - as Toulouse dug in during the opening 20 minutes and then exerted some control before Mathieu Jussaume scored the opening try on the half-hour when he broke through down the right.

The defending champions, chasing a home play-off berth, finally sparked into life when substitute Elliot Minchella went over in the 35th minute after a surging run by Peta Hiku, with Rhyse Martin adding the extras to make it 6-6 heading into half-time.

Toulouse opted to kick for a penalty early in the second half after a late tackle from Tom Amone, but Cesar Rouge saw his 35-metre attempt bounce off the crossbar.

Hull KR continued to be pushed back and Toulouse deservedly did get themselves in front again after 57 minutes when Benjamin Laguerre burst down the left and fed Romeo Tropis to go on to touch down under the sticks.

Toulouse further extended their advantage when Anthony Marion got on the end of a kick through and barged over, with the try given following a lengthy video review which showed the ball had been grounded after Hull KR initially had looked to have held him up.

Hull KR, who face leaders Wigan next week, crumbled again when Paul Ulberg was played into space down the left corner after 65 minutes before Tropis burst clear through down the other channel. Luke Polselli added another late scrappy Toulouse try after a kick bounced off the post and Louix Gorman got a consolation score for the home side in the closing stages with a fast break down the left.

Arthur's late drop goal seals Hull fightback

Hull half-back Jake Arthur landed a late drop goal to seal his side's thrilling fightback as they beat Catalans Dragons 27-26 at the Gilbert Brutus Stadium.

Arthur coolly slotted over a match-winning one-pointer with six minutes left to clinch Hull victory over former boss John Cartwright's Catalans and just their second win in 10 Super League games.

Hull trailed 26-14 early in the second half, but came storming back through converted tries from Harvie Hill and Aidan Sezer to tie the scores before Arthur's match-winning effort.

The visitors led through early tries from Logan Moy and Lewis Martin and led 14-12 at half-time after Catalans had hit back through touchdowns from Charlie Staines and Kruise Leeming.

Catalans appeared to take control of the match when Edenn Rogers-Smith and Leo Darrelatour both went over early in the second period, either side of Guillermo Aispuro-Bichet's penalty, to put them 26-14 ahead.

But Hull launched their fightback as Hill and Sezer both went over for converted scores in the space of six minutes and Arthur had the final word.

Hull have climbed up one place to 11th in the table, while Catalans sit ninth after their 15th defeat of the season.

Hull interim head coach Andy Last said: "It was a nail-biting game, it went right down to the wire. I'm just really proud of the playing group.

"I spoke all week about showing our personality and our performance when it gets tough and to make sure you answer those questions with your effort and your actions."

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

articles.title: Pegula dethrones Swiatek to book Cincinnati final against Gauff
articles.summary: The women’s all-American final will be followed by a men’s title clash between Frances Tiafoe and Arthur Fils of France.
articles.body:
Jessica Pegula rallied in the third set to topple defending champion Iga Swiatek and book a title showdown with Coco Gauff at the Cincinnati Masters tennis tournament.

World number three Pegula won a “crazy” match against Swiatek 7-5, 4-6, 6-4 on Saturday in the US city.

list 1 of 4 CONCACAF asks Infantino to skip youth event amid FIFA governance crisis

list 2 of 4 Former world champion boxer Zolani Tete shot and killed in South Africa

list 3 of 4 Arsenal rout Coventry 3-0 to begin Premier League title defence in style

list 4 of 4 Argentina’s Paredes gets 10-game ban for World Cup final scuffle with Spain

Gauff powered past giant-killer Sara Bejlek 6-4, 6-1, ending the unseeded Czech’s dream run that included a fourth-round victory over world number one Aryna Sabalenka.

Their all-American Sunday night final will be followed by a men’s title clash between American Frances Tiafoe and Arthur Fils of France.

Fils charged into his first Masters 1000 final with a 6-3, 6-4 victory over French Open runner-up Flavio Cobolli in a match delayed for 45 minutes by rain and lightning.

Swiatek and Pegula then waited out another rain delay before their match, which was also briefly interrupted two games in.

“Crazy match today,” Pegula said after needing nearly three hours to subdue Swiatek, who was coming off her first title of 2026 in Toronto last week.

“A lot of back and forth, a lot of breaks,” she said. “Really windy, kind of odd conditions. I felt like we were playing well and then not playing well.

“It was really tough to kind of get a gauge on the match.”

The pair rode a rollercoaster of breaks and re-breaks before Pegula took a 5-4 lead in the final set, Swiatek saving three break points before double-faulting on a fourth.

Pegula quickly closed it out, firing a service winner on match point.

“I was just really happy with the way I was able to kind of handle just a lot that was going on today,” the 31-year-old American said. “I did a good job no matter what was happening.”

The first five games of what evolved into an epic went against the server as Pegula and Swiatek struggled to adjust to the conditions.

Swiatek blinked first as Pegula held at love for a 4-2 lead, but Swiatek won the next three games before Pegula broke again, finally taking the set when Swiatek smacked a volley into the net on set point.

They had exchanged two breaks in the second when Swiatek broke in the final game to square the match.

Tiafoe feeling ‘damn good’ on return to final

Tiafoe, runner-up to Jannik Sinner in Cincinnati in 2024, returned to the final with a 7-5, 6-3 victory over fellow American Brandon Nakashima.

Tiafoe saved three set points in the opening set, breaking Nakashima five times in all to earn the win in less than two hours.

The American predicted a “h*** of a show” against Fils, whose 68-minute win over seventh-seeded Cobolli made him the youngest French Masters finalist since a 20-year-old Richard Gasquet in Toronto two decades ago.

Fils admitted he had been unsettled by the weather delay.

“You come on court more nervous because it’s a semi-final. The rain arrives, you wait and when you come back conditions are completely different,” he said.

“It was tough, but I’m happy with how I dealt with it.”

articles.title: Starc takes 10 as Australia hand Bangladesh innings defeat in second Test
articles.summary: Australia bounce back after losing first Test, bowling out the visitors for 64 and 95 to win by an innings and 51 runs.
articles.body:
An irrepressible Mitchell Starc bagged four wickets in the second innings and 10 for the match as he ripped through Bangladesh’s batting lineup to ensure a commanding victory by an innings and 51 runs in the second Test for Australia in just two days.

The statement win on Sunday ensured the hosts ended the two-match series in a draw.

The visitors headed into the Mackay showdown on a high after shocking the world’s top-ranked team by nine wickets in the first Test at Darwin.

But they were brought crashing back to earth by some scintillating fast bowling, led by man of the match Starc, who finished with 10-51 for the match to level the series.

After 18 wickets fell on a frenetic first day of the five-day match, the hosts were all out for 210 in the second day’s morning session, securing a lead of 146 on the back of Cameron Green’s 67.

Paceman Shoriful Islam claimed 7-48 — the best figures by a Bangladeshi bowler in an away Test.

The visitors collapsed for just 64 in their first innings , when Starc took 6-12, and he was the chief tormentor again, claiming 4-39 as Bangladesh crumbled to be 95 all out.

Skipper Pat Cummins chipped in with 3-10 and Nathan Lyon 3-25.

“A lot of things went right these couple [of] days and a lot of things went wrong last week,” said Cummins.

“But yeah, we needed to bounce back, and it was a great few days from the lads. I thought everyone was sharp. It was a great start, and we didn’t really let up after that.”

Bangladesh had a horror start, with Shadman Islam lasting just three balls, playing a meaningless stroke to a moving Starc delivery and edging to Marnus Labuschagne at point.

Mominul Haque was equally clueless next ball, failing to offer a shot, with Starc removing his off stump and setting up a hat-trick opportunity.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto, who was out for a golden duck in the first innings, this time survived to deny Starc.

But their woes deepened when Tanzid Hasan departed soon after for nine. Starc was again involved, taking a catch in the deep after Tanzid pulled Cummins.

Shanto did well to soak up the pressure after lunch for 46 deliveries, but he eventually lost focus against the off-spin of Lyon, holing out to the safe hands of Starc at long off on 31.

And when Starc was brought back into the attack, he was front and centre again, enticing a loose shot from Litton Das, who was caught without scoring by Beau Webster at third slip.

Mehidy Hasan Miraz struggled to get going and departed to an equally poor shot, lashing at a Cummins bouncer and being collected by wicketkeeper Alex Carey.

The Australian captain then removed Hasan Mahmud (2) before Starc took his 10th for the match — the fourth time he has achieved the feat — when he bowled Taijul Islam for 7 runs.

Lyon quickly wrapped up the tail in the first over after tea.

“We know how good Australia are. They showed their character,” said Shanto.

“We were not up to the mark with the bat. It was challenging conditions here with extra bounce and swing; we would like to learn from this.”

Australia resumed at 165-8, with Green on 51 and Lyon on 10.

Green, who scored a century during the first Test in Darwin, kept the scoreboard moving early with quick singles.

But he was undone by an inswinging yorker from the impressive Shoriful that hit him on the toe, with a review declaring him out lbw.

A valiant Lyon brought up the 200 for Australia with a towering six off Taskin, and with Josh Hazlewood adding 24 crucial runs for the last wicket.

The innings ended when Hazlewood skied Taijul to Shadman on six, leaving Lyon not out on 32.

articles.title: Serena Williams teams up with Carlos Alcaraz in US Open mixed doubles
articles.summary: The 23-time Grand Slam champion will not be playing singles, but could team up with her older sister Venus for doubles.
articles.body:
Serena Williams will team up with Carlos Alcaraz to create a powerhouse mixed doubles pair on her return to the US Open.

The US Tennis Association announced on Saturday that Williams and Alcaraz had been given a wild card into the tournament. The mixed doubles main draw begins on Tuesday, with the winning team sharing $1 million.

list 2 of 4 Arsenal rout Coventry 3-0 to begin Premier League title defence in style

list 3 of 4 Arsenal sign Konsa from Villa as Premier League holders bolster defence

list 4 of 4 What to know about the Freedom 250 Grand Prix, Trump’s capital car race

It will be Williams’s first time playing at the US Open since 2022. The 23-time Grand Slam singles champion returned to tennis this summer.

“Let’s gooooo!” Alcaraz posted on X, with a fire emoji and tagging Williams.

Williams is not planning to play singles in New York. The USTA had been holding one women’s wild card, presumably in case Williams wanted it. However, the tournament announced on Saturday that it had been given to American Sofia Kenin, the 2020 Australian Open champion.

Williams played singles at Wimbledon but sustained a knee injury in her first-round loss. She played doubles with older sister Venus at the Cincinnati Open, and they could still opt to play together at the US Open.

Alcaraz announced this week he would return to defend his US Open singles title after being sidelined since April with a right wrist injury.

Serena Williams won a mixed doubles title at the US Open even before winning any of her six singles titles there. She teamed for the 1998 championship with Max Mirnyi, who now works with top-ranked woman Aryna Sabalenka.

The mixed doubles tournament is far different now, as the USTA revamped it last year to make it a two-day, 16-team event it hoped would draw top singles players.

Few are bigger than Williams and Alcaraz, the two-time US Open men’s champion who is ranked number two.

The USTA also announced a number of updates to the field after some players withdrew from the competition.

Americans Jessica Pegula and Taylor Fritz will team up, after their previous partners, Jack Draper and Elena Rybakina, pulled out with injuries. The teams of Emma Navarro and Tommy Paul, along with Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik, were given the remaining two wild cards into the main draw.

Diana Shnaider remains in the field and will be given a chance to find a new partner after Daniil Medvedev withdrew.

US Open mixed doubles teams: Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic, Pegula and Fritz, Iga Swiatek and Casper Ruud, Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli, Amanda Anisimova and Learner Tien, two-time defending champions Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori, Alex Eala and Felix Auger-Aliassime, Leylah Fernandez and Frances Tiafoe, Taylor Townsend and Alexander Zverev, Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils, Williams and Alcaraz, Muchova and Mensik, and Navarro and Paul.

The remaining two spots will be determined through an eight-team qualifying tournament on Monday.

The USTA gave wild cards to the teams of Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev, and Peyton Stearns and Christian Harrison, to be part of that field.

It is otherwise largely made up of the traditional doubles specialists who lost out on the chance to play in the US Open last year, with direct entry based on the players’ combined singles ranking.

articles.title: Wild Ideas to Keep WWE Interesting Until WrestleMania 43 Season
articles.summary: After the failures associated with SummerSlam 2026, the WWE Universe is growing tired of the lack of storyline continuity and character development across the Raw and SmackDown brands.
articles.body:
After the failures associated with SummerSlam 2026, the WWE Universe is growing tired of the lack of storyline continuity and character development across the Raw and SmackDown brands.

As it's currently constructed, WWE has an enormous roster and plenty of championships, but needs structural changes to make the weekly shows feel important.

With wrestling fans already looking toward WrestleMania 43, here are three ideas that could shake things up without requiring the company to completely reinvent itself.

While WWE has technically maintained Raw and SmackDown as separate brands, the separation feels meaningless, and Superstars regularly appear on both shows. A true brand split would make Raw and SmackDown feel important, as WWE Creative could be judged based on the performance of one show against the other.

Instead of letting storylines die on the vine or failing to follow through on a character arc pivotal to a freshly debuted NXT performer's success, each brand would be forced to focus on continuity and maximizing the growth of its smaller roster.

To ensure the brand split is a success this time, WWE must hold a massive draft of the entire main roster and make the results permanent for the foreseeable future. Once drafted, wrestlers belong exclusively to that brand.

Each brand would get its own men's and women's championships, with only their Superstars able to challenge for the respective titles. This move gives WWE more room to elevate younger stars and allows for longer stories with more depth and development.

To get people to care about Raw and SmackDown again, WWE Creative needs to give them storylines and characters worth investing their emotions. With more time and fewer people on each show, the stage would be set for the deepest two-day WrestleMania card in history.

Championships are supposed to represent WWE's best wrestlers, but sometimes titles disappear from television for weeks. Whether an injury keeps them off television or their contract calls for a certain number of days off, no champion should go more than 30 days without defending their title.

Rhea Ripley and Liv Morgan can go months without defending their belts, but Chelsea Green is given a 30-day mandate due to injury? The policy should be uniform across all divisions and brands, creating excitement around every championship again.

This rule would ensure the titles are defended more often to satisfy the WWE Universe, but the 30-day limit could also be a major storyline factor. A champion might deliberately avoid dangerous challengers to preserve their reign, so the general manager of Raw or Smackdown could be forced to find legitimate contenders.

By adding and enforcing the rule, every championship becomes a weekly storytelling device: contenders have a reason to fight, champions can't disappear after a major win, and, most importantly, WWE has a reason to create unexpected title matches on TV.

Add the drama of someone being stripped of a title or a heel champion using loopholes to exploit it, and you have a major storyline driver that wrestling fans could embrace.

While a vocal minority of wrestling fans would hate the concept, one key to WWE's success over the next six months would be to bring back the Raw Underground concept and make it a competitive division rather than simply a presentation style.

With both a men's and women's championship, the WWE Underground fights would be the only platform to allow cross-promotional bouts in the entire company, making the fights feel special. Add a combat-sports-inspired element to the matches, and it becomes a unique selling point that could air on Raw or SmackDown week to week.

Each bout would take place inside the WWE Underground setting, away from the arena, possibly filmed at the Performance Center each week. The segments would feature no traditional entrances, faster match times, minimal interference, and an emphasis on raw physicality.

To add an element of sport, there should be a season-long points system with every match counting towards the overall standings. The highest-ranked wrestlers would receive championship opportunities, which creates opportunities for storylines to be crafted over time and characters to be built through winning streaks or redemption arcs.

In addition to nodding to parent company TKO's UFC style, it would give WWE Creative something visually and competitively different, while also creating meaningful matches that don't require weeks of buildup.

articles.title: Chelsea preview: Five key talking points for 2026-27 Premier League season
articles.summary: Chelsea have had their worst Premier League run in 30 years. Can new manager Xabi Alonso succeed and is Cole Palmer key?
articles.body:
Chelsea’s story has rarely been one of plain sailing. The Blues first won the English top flight in 1955, and by 1971 had won three FA Cups and the old UEFA Cup Winners’ Cup.

Fortunes soon turned, and in 1983, the west Londoners avoided relegation to the English third tier by the skin of their teeth. Within a decade, the good times were rolling again, and a 26-year wait for a trophy ended with their fourth FA Cup.

list 1 of 4 La Liga: The key talking points for Real Madrid before the 2026-27 season

list 2 of 4 La Liga: Five key talking points heading into Barcelona’s 2026-27 season

list 3 of 4 Real Madrid officially present Mourinho in bizarre closed-door ceremony

list 4 of 4 Top 10 players to watch in the 2026-27 European football season

Enter a new owner, Roman Abramovich, and the rest – of their modern era – is history.

The latest wait for a trophy is only five seasons, but in the past four seasons, the Stamford Bridge club has witnessed its choppiest waters in 30 years and now faces a campaign without any European football.

Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at the club’s prospects in advance of the new season.

What have been Chelsea’s biggest problems in recent seasons?

A run of 12th, sixth, fourth and 10th-placed finishes in the Premier League marks the worst run since the Blues finished 11th in 1996. Since then, they have only finished outside the top six once, that being one of only five finishes outside the top five in that period.

The arrival of Xabi Alonso marks the seventh permanent manager since Thomas Tuchel’s side lifted their second Champions League title in May 2021.

That statistic, in itself, points to the answer: instability.

The chopping and changing behind the scenes, including the sale of the club by their billionaire backer Abramovich in 2022, have left the team in turmoil on the field.

Under Enzo Maresca, who is now Manchester City manager, the Blues enjoyed a great deal of possession last season. That did not, however, translate into results.

Opponents sat deep and found Maresca’s team to be predictable.

When the Italian left his role, amid internal tensions, his team had won only one of their last seven matches.

What system will Xabi Alonso play at Chelsea?

Ironically, in the face of the chopping and changing off the field, the biggest problem under Maresca was his rigid tactics.

Alonso, who lost his job at Real Madrid in January, was heavily criticised for his formations and tactical changes.

Los Blancos were renowned for their 4-3-3 formation for years, but Alonso used a mix of 4-2-2-2, 3-4-3 and 4-4-2. It led to unhappiness among the players and a serious downturn in results.

The most likely formation at Chelsea will be 3-4-3, and that is what was deployed in the final preseason friendly against Real Sociedad last Saturday, as it was in the two games before that.

It is a formation often seen as a weakness in the Premier League given the pace and power that teams have on the flanks, but it is also the formation that was used the last time Chelsea won the league, under Antonio Conte during the 2016-17 season.

Can Cole Palmer rediscover his form at Chelsea?

Above all else, the biggest question heading into the new campaign surrounds Palmer.

The Manchester City academy graduate was let go by Pep Guardiola in 2023, but the attacking midfielder quickly became a hero at Stamford Bridge.

Two seasons ago, his form saw him push Mohamed Salah close for the league’s Player of the Year award with 29 Premier League goal involvements. Salah admittedly recorded 47 goals, but in a high-flying Premier League winning side.

Palmer helped a still disjointed Chelsea to fourth that season, and his dip in form last season can also be attributed to his side’s 10th-place finish.

It is hard to imagine the Blues firing on all cylinders this season unless Palmer does likewise. Much like Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, the 24-year-old is a player capable of dragging a struggling side to a greater level.

Where will Morgan Rogers fit into Alonso’s Chelsea plans?

The arrival of England forward Rogers from Aston Villa could actually ease the burden on Palmer, especially as the pair are likely to line up behind a lone striker.

Therefore, some of the attention from opponents’ defences and midfields will be drawn away from the latter. The danger is that Rogers, a reported 117 million pounds ($158m) record signing for a British player, might occupy the same spaces that Palmer will try to play in.

Palmer is the type of forward that likes to pull the strings as well as make forward runs, which Rogers is more associated with.

So the chemistry between this pair will be one of the main puzzles for Alonso to solve. Theoretically, the runs of Rogers to support the likes of Joao Pedro or Estevao – as they plough a lone furrow in the striker role – should drag players out of position, as should the overload from the wingbacks.

Does the booing of Enzo Fernandez suggest unrest at Chelsea?

One of the most protracted sagas of the season has been the “will he or won’t he” transfer of Fernandez.

Chelsea were understood to have set a deadline of last Friday for offers for the Argentinian midfielder.

With that passing, Fernandez lined up in the 3-1 friendly win against Real Sociedad the following day and was roundly jeered by sections of the home support.

The 25-year-old is understood to have made known his desire to leave Chelsea and has reportedly had an asking price of 120 million pounds ($162m) placed on his head.

Both Manchester United and City were interested, but only the latter now appear an option.

Those who booed Fernandez were met by those who showed their support for the midfielder with applause when he came on as a 62nd-minute substitute, so a future at the Bridge remains a possibility.

The discontent among the fans is perhaps a small insight into what has simmered since Abramovich sold the club to the US consortium.

Will the Chelsea ownership change again?

Chelsea chairman Todd Boehly and director Mark Walter are thought to be considering selling their stakes in the Premier League side to the club’s majority owner Clearlake Capital.

American billionaires Boehly and Walter were two of the investors who partnered with Clearlake to buy Chelsea from Abramovich for 2.5 billion pounds (approximately $3.1bn) in May 2022.

Private equity company Clearlake currently owns 62 percent of Chelsea, with Boehly and Walter holding the remaining shares alongside fellow investor Hansjorg Wyss.

Boehly, Walter and Wyss control 38 percent through Blueco Holdings.

Boehly has reportedly been dissatisfied with the direction of Chelsea, notably regarding recruitment, managers and a potential new stadium plan.

There have been reports that Boehly and Clearlake had attempted to buy each other out of Chelsea several times over the last two years.

Boehly and Walter reportedly believe Chelsea are worth 5 billion pounds ($6.8bn) if they do sell their stake.

The pair are friends and business partners, having also invested together in baseball’s Los Angeles Dodgers and women’s basketball franchise LA Sparks.

What will be unthinkable for whoever is in charge is that the tide will not turn under Alonso.

articles.title: Nordic nations ‘have lost confidence in Infantino’, demand FIFA reforms
articles.summary: Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden and the Faroe Islands back calls for Infantino’s resignation amid FIFA crisis.
articles.body:
Six Nordic football associations have delivered a united blow to FIFA President Gianni Infantino, declaring they have lost confidence in his leadership while demanding sweeping governance reforms at world football’s governing body.

The six Nordic FIFA members – Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden and the Faroe Islands – met in Helsinki and issued a rare joint statement on Sunday, backing calls for Infantino’s resignation from three major regional confederations.

They also supported demands for an independent investigation into his proposal to sell a stake in events like the World Cup to private equity investors, a plan that was quickly abandoned in the face of a global backlash.

“The six Nordic football associations have lost confidence in FIFA’s president and are concerned about the organisation’s governance and decision-making at the highest level,” they said in a statement.

“The Nordic football associations stand united with UEFA and support the measures that the organisation and its national member associations have jointly proposed.

“We expect FIFA to provide binding guarantees that the organisation’s governance or competitions will never again be opened up to private ownership.”

FIFA did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

On Friday, Denmark’s football association pledged to find a credible alternative to Infantino in March’s presidential election.

Infantino is under pressure from three confederations to resign: UEFA, the AFC and CONCACAF.

The sport’s regional powerhouses in Europe, Asia, and North and Central America and the Caribbean have also discussed a potential vote of no confidence against the FIFA chief.

“We also support the demand made by AFC, CONCACAF and UEFA that a fully independent external investigation into the events surrounding the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal be established,” the Nordic associations added.

“We also call on FIFA to initiate a comprehensive and independent review of its governance framework to determine whether it ensures the independence, checks and balances, transparency and accountability that were intended when FIFA adopted its reform programme in 2016.”

Infantino, who is seeking a fourth term until 2031 in next year’s election, is in the Dominican Republic this weekend , where he has met with officials of the Caribbean Football Union (CFU).

CONCACAF President Victor Montagliani had asked Infantino to stay away from a youth football tournament in the country, saying his presence would overshadow the event.

“This meeting of the presidents of CFU takes place in the environment of [an] under-14 youth tournament in the region, which actually is one of those tournaments that can take place thanks to the FIFA Forward programme,” Infantino said.

“So even more so a reason to be proud to be here and happy as well because it’s important to engage, to have a dialogue, to express views and opinions.”

articles.title: Matt Cardona Reveals Torn Triceps Injury in New Photo After WWE Main Event Match
articles.summary: WWE Superstar Matt Cardona announced Sunday that he recently tore his triceps.
articles.body:
WWE Superstar Matt Cardona announced Sunday that he recently tore his triceps.

In a post on X, Cardona shared a photo of his swollen and bandaged arm, and revealed that he suffered the injury during a match that was taped for Main Event prior to Friday night's episode of SmackDown:

Per Fightful's Ishaan Sharma , the Main Event bout pitted Cardona against Kit Wilson.

Formerly known as Zack Ryder during his first stint with WWE, Cardona established himself as a top star on the independent scene following his WWE release in 2020.

Cardona re-signed with WWE in January, and he has been part of the SmackDown roster ever since.

The 41-year-old Cardona is married to reigning WWE women's champion Chelsea Green, who has been nursing an orbital injury since shortly after her title win at SummerSlam.

On the Aug. 14 episode of SmackDown, Gunther interrupted Green and disrespected her, prompting Cardona to run down to the ring and stand up for his wife.

In a subsequent match between Gunther and Cardona, Gunther won by submission.

Despite the loss, Cardona seemed to be building some momentum based on his involvement in such a significant segment, but now he will have to work his way back from injury.
paragraphs: WWE Superstar Matt Cardona announced Sunday that he recently tore his triceps.

In a post on X, Cardona shared a photo of his swollen and bandaged arm, and revealed that he suffered the injury during a match that was taped for Main Event prior to Friday night's episode of SmackDown:
Per Fightful's Ishaan Sharma , the Main Event bout pitted Cardona against Kit Wilson.
Formerly known as Zack Ryder during his first stint with WWE, Cardona established himself as a top star on the independent scene following his WWE release in 2020.
Cardona re-signed with WWE in January, and he has been part of the SmackDown roster ever since.
The 41-year-old Cardona is married to reigning WWE women's champion Chelsea Green, who has been nursing an orbital injury since shortly after her title win at SummerSlam.
On the Aug. 14 episode of SmackDown, Gunther interrupted Green and disrespected her, prompting Cardona to run down to the ring and stand up for his wife.
In a subsequent match between Gunther and Cardona, Gunther won by submission.
Despite the loss, Cardona seemed to be building some momentum based on his involvement in such a significant segment, but now he will have to work his way back from injury.

articles.title: Raphinha and Lopez score braces as Barcelona trounce Elche 5-0
articles.summary: Barcelona ‌begin their La Liga title ⁠defence ⁠and bid for a third successive crown with a 5-0 ⁠victory at Elche.
articles.body:
Spanish champions Barcelona have cruised to a 5-0 win over Elche in their La Liga opener, with Raphinha and Fermin Lopez scoring twice each and Anthony Gordon setting up two goals on his debut.

After watching Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid defeat Espanyol 2-1 on Saturday with a late winner, Barca’s display on Sunday warned the Portuguese coach that the Catalans will not relinquish the title easily.

list 1 of 4 Squad, formation, unrest: Key talking points ahead of Chelsea’s new season

list 2 of 4 Man Utd humiliated at Hull to open Premier League account

list 3 of 4 Fans and police injured in pitch invasion during ‘high risk’ German Cup tie

list 4 of 4 Arsenal rout Coventry 3-0 to begin Premier League title defence in style

Karim Adeyemi also found the net on his debut as Barca made light work of a vulnerable Elche side at Martinez Valero Stadium.

Hansi Flick started with several regular starters on the bench as they continue to get up to speed following the World Cup.

Teenage winger Lamine Yamal, a key part of the triumphant World Cup Spain squad, did start on the right but was far from his best, though it did not matter given Barca’s otherwise sparkling display.

Raphinha was cut down in the box by Victor Chust and stroked home the resulting penalty after 14 minutes to get Flick’s team on their way.

Eric Garcia was sharp at the back to ward off a threatening Elche attack, while Barca’s Gavi caught the eye in midfield – admittedly more for his pink haircut to celebrate Spain’s triumph than for his performance.

Rapid winger Adeyemi, playing on the left, started shakily but grew into the game and doubled Barca’s lead before the break after Raphinha unselfishly set him up.

In the second half, former Newcastle United winger Gordon, on as a substitute, teed up Raphinha for his second, and then supplied Lopez for Barca’s fourth in an electric and impressive cameo.

Youngster Xavi Espart played in Lopez, who endured a difficult summer after missing Spain’s World Cup triumph through injury, for his second to seal Barcelona’s comfortable triumph.

Flick’s high-line defence showed the occasional sign of its usual frailty, but goalkeeper Joan Garcia did well when called on to keep a clean sheet.

Raphinha told reporters after the game that “whether a game is easy or hard depends on us.

“If we start playing at the maximum level, we’re likely to win. It was a very tough game, but we did our job.”

articles.title: Gauff, Fils win Cincinnati tennis titles in run-up to US Open
articles.summary: Gauff beat Pegula for her second Cincinnati Open trophy and Fils overcame Tiafoe for his first Masters 1000 title.
articles.body:
Coco Gauff has defeated fellow American Jessica Pegula, 6-2, 6-4, to capture her second women’s Cincinnati Open title as she looks ahead to the US Open starting in New York next week.

Arthur Fils of France overcame American Frances Tiafoe 6-3, 1-6, 6-0, in the men’s final for his first Masters 1000 title, with Sunday’s decider marking the first time two Black players competed in an ATP Masters 1000 final.

list 1 of 4 Nordic nations ‘have lost confidence in Infantino’, demand FIFA reforms

list 2 of 4 Real Madrid’s Mourinho condemns bullying of Vinicius after La Liga win

list 3 of 4 Squad, formation, unrest: Key talking points ahead of Chelsea’s new season

list 4 of 4 Raphinha and Lopez score braces as Barcelona trounce Elche 5-0

Gauff, who won the 2023 title beating Karolina Muchova and then went on to win her first Grand Slam at the US Open, stormed to a 5-0 lead in the first set before winning it 6-2. Pegula battled back to 5-4 in the second before Gauff closed out the win. Gauff won five of six break points.

The last time two American women played in the Cincinnati final was in 1970, when Rosie Casals beat Nancy Richey.

Pegula’s best finish in Cincinnati came in 2024, when she lost to Aryna Sabalenka in the final.

In Saturday’s semifinals , Pegula beat defending champion Iga Swiatek and Gauff defeated Sara Bejlek to set up the first all-American women’s final at the Cincinnati Open in 56 years.

“I think it was a long journey, but I’m happy,” Gauff said after the match. “I think it’s night and day, the player I was last year to now. I don’t think that this is an indicator that I’m going to do well in New York. Just knowing the quality ones that I had this week, hopefully I can use that experience.”

Gauff had five wins in straight sets in Cincinnati.

“I thought she just played at a really high level and didn’t really have many dips,” Pegula said.

“I didn’t really think I played badly. The more you construct the point [against her], the worse it is because she almost likes to run. It was tough today. A dangerous, confident Coco is going to New York.”

The head-to-head series between Gauff and Pegula is now tied at five apiece. Sunday was their second meeting in a final, with Gauff winning in Wuhan last year.

Meanwhile, Fils became the third Black man to win a Masters 1000 title, joining Ben Shelton, who won twice in Canada, and Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, who won in Paris in 2008 and Canada in 2014.

At 22 years old, Fils is the youngest French champion in Masters 1000 history. He became the second French player to win a Cincinnati final, joining Guy Forget in 1991.

“Very happy with that,” Fils said. “It’s been a tough last year. I didn’t play the French Open [due to a hip injury]. I lost early in Washington. People think that I’m done. But here we are. I got the title.”

It was the second time Tiafoe has appeared in the Cincinnati Open final, losing to Jannik Sinner in 2024. He was looking to become the first American man to win in Cincinnati since Andy Roddick in 2006.

Tiafoe saved three championship points in the final game before Fils closed out the victory.

The Frenchman had 11 aces and won 71 percent of his points on first serve. He improved to 10-0 in deciding sets this year and 8-0 against American opponents.

Fils also won his only previous meeting with Tiafoe in Miami last year, also in three sets.

“It feels very good to have a trophy next to me, especially Masters 1000,” Fils said. “Never won one before. You just have to stay positive and find a way to make it work. Being positive is going to help me in the next weeks in the US Open.”

articles.title: Ceferin won’t challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency but tells him to quit
articles.summary: European football chief doesn’t want to lose credibility over FIFA job but says Infantino will face a challenger.
articles.body:
European football chief Aleksander Ceferin says he is “not interested” in replacing Gianni Infantino but warned the under-fire FIFA president must quit or face a leadership challenge.

Ceferin has been vocal in his criticism since Infantino revealed his controversial plans to seek private investment in a company to run FIFA tournaments. However, ruling himself out of a bid to take Infantino’s place, the 58-year-old Slovenian told The Rest is Politics podcast on Monday that he is “not interested because of two reasons”.

“One reason is that I love UEFA and I love working here, and I think that at a certain point … it’s time to also enjoy life a bit,” he said.

“And the second point is, my credibility is much, much higher if I’m not interested in the position.”

Infantino has come under increasing pressure to step down as head of world football’s governing body over his now-abandoned plan to secure private investment in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup.

UEFA, which oversees European football, has threatened a boycott of FIFA competitions, with several continental and national federations also withdrawing their support for Infantino.

Ceferin now believes Infantino’s previously impregnable position is under threat, with him forecasting the Swiss will have to stand down or face a leadership challenge if he seeks re-election at the next FIFA Congress in Morocco in March.

Infantino, a former UEFA secretary-general, had the broad backing of European nations when he succeeded Sepp Blatter as FIFA president in 2016.

But Ceferin, who revealed he has not spoken to Infantino since the controversy started, insisted the current situation was very different.

“One option is that he [Infantino] realises that he doesn’t have the support, and that’s not only a political support of the ones who vote, but the political support of the football community, the political support of fans, the political support of the players, former players, coaches.

“And the second option, that he goes to the elections in March, but in that case I think he will have a candidate against him. I don’t know yet who.”

UEFA has been backed by the regional blocs for Asia (AFC) and North and Central America and the Caribbean (CONCACAF).

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani and AFC boss Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa are considered two of the most likely challengers for Infantino’s position.

Infantino seeks support in the Caribbean

Infantino was in the Dominican Republic over the weekend for meetings with local and regional football officials, despite Montagliani reportedly asking him to stay away from a youth tournament there.

In video remarks released by FIFA on Sunday, the 56-year-old Infantino appeared to reference the furore surrounding him.

“It’s important to engage, to have a dialogue, to express views and opinions,” he said.

“A lot has been happening the last few weeks, and it’s important that you hear, you listen, and you’re able to also express what your feelings are.

“So I think overall positive, very, very happy with all the support I get here.”

Infantino ⁠⁠laid out his manifesto for re-election as ⁠⁠the champion of poorer football nations.

FIFA has not responded to Al Jazeera’s request for a comment on Ceferin’s criticism of Infantino and FIFA.

Infantino has shown no signs of walking away from the position he has held since 2016 and made it clear that he was banking on ⁠⁠his appeal to the less well-off national associations to win re-election until 2031.

He has support from the African and South American regional blocs and ⁠⁠has looked to sideline the confederations and appeal directly to individual members throughout the crisis.

articles.title: Salah scores two goals, has two disallowed in first start for Trabzonspor
articles.summary: Salah started his first game for the Turkish Super Lig side, whom he joined on a free transfer earlier this month.
articles.body:
Mohamed Salah ‌‌opened his account in the Turkish ⁠⁠Super Lig ⁠⁠with a double as Trabzonspor beat Istanbul Basaksehir 2-1 to clinch their first win ⁠⁠of the season.

Salah, who joined Trabzonspor on a free transfer after leaving Liverpool ⁠⁠following a trophy-laden nine-year spell, also had two goals disallowed in a standout performance on Sunday.

Making his first league start after appearing as a substitute in Trabzonspor’s ‌‌season opener, Salah put his side ahead in the eighth minute, capitalising after Basaksehir goalkeeper Muhammed Sengezer failed to hold on to the ball.

Basaksehir’s Eldor Shomurodov equalised from the penalty spot in the 19th minute, but Salah restored ⁠⁠Trabzonspor’s lead three minutes into the ⁠⁠second half, bursting down the right, exchanging passes with Ernest Muci and slotting the ball into the far corner.

The 34-year-old ⁠⁠winger had a stoppage-time effort chalked off for a foul in ⁠⁠the build-up and another ruled ⁠⁠out for offside when he found the empty net from long range with the goalkeeper upfield for a corner.

He will ‌‌now turn his attention to Thursday’s Europa League playoff second leg away to Ferencvaros after his ‌‌side ‌‌suffered a 1-0 home defeat in the first leg.

articles.title: Mercedes no longer have the fastest car in F1, says leader Antonelli
articles.summary: McLaren’s reigning champion Lando Norris celebrates his second win in a row from pole position at Zandvoort.
articles.body:
McLaren have taken a big step forward and Mercedes no longer have the quickest car in Formula One, championship leader Kimi Antonelli said after the Dutch Grand Prix.

McLaren’s reigning champion Lando Norris celebrated his second win in a row from pole position at Zandvoort on Sunday, with Antonelli and Mercedes teammate George Russell finishing second and third, ahead of Ferrari pair Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.

list 1 of 4 ‘Simply lovely’: Verstappen extends with F1 Red Bull Racing until 2030

list 2 of 4 Norris finally wins a race in 2026 with Hungarian Grand Prix triumph

list 3 of 4 Formula One returns to Malaysia as Sepang circuit hosts Bahrain Grand Prix

list 4 of 4 F1 needs better balance between business and sport, says Norris

“We’re clearly not the fastest car any more on the grid,” said Antonelli, who won five races in a row earlier in the season.

“We’re probably second or third, at least in today’s race, and McLaren has taken a huge step, especially since Hungary, since the big upgrade package they brought.”

However, Norris, who lost out to Antonelli at the race restart and then had to overtake him on track, questioned that assertion.

“I don’t think it’s true. I think if I didn’t get Kimi when I overtook him, I don’t think I would have won the race,” he said.

“For once, I would give myself a little bit of credit that I feel like I’m doing a better job than everyone, and I think that can also make a difference.

“We certainly have a car now capable of beating them … but I think they have a better all-round performing car than what we do.”

Zandvoort, and Budapest’s Hungaroring before that, played to McLaren’s strengths but some of the tracks coming up may be less favourable.

Ferrari can be expected to go well at their home Grand Prix at Monza early next month, with upgrades in the pipeline, while Antonelli faces hefty grid penalties for an engine change.

Mercedes are still way ahead of Ferrari and McLaren in the constructors’ championship and scored more points – 46 to McLaren’s 43 and Ferrari’s 31 – than anyone else over the weekend.

“We have a strong car in certain areas. It’s not like last year where we were pretty good everywhere,” said Norris.

“We’re very, very strong in high speed, and that’s the place we’ve improved the car the most, is high-speed performance. No one matches us in high speed, and that’s a good thing.

“But the advantage that they [Mercedes] have to us in slow speed is also crazy. And therefore, I don’t have the confidence to say ‘yeah, I can easily fight for a championship for the rest of the season’.”

“I know I’ve just won two races in a row and had two poles in a row, but at the minute I don’t have the car I need to fight for a championship,” added the Briton, who is 83 points behind Antonelli, with 11 rounds remaining unless the situation in the Middle East forces a calendar change.

Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said cost cap restrictions meant Mercedes did not have the money to implement developments on the car as quickly as they might want.

“We are trying to evenly split that through the season based on our calculations of when we can bring the biggest updates and optimising the championship points,” he told reporters.

“So the ride has been a bit tougher than at the beginning of the year.”

McLaren principal Andrea Stella said he expected Mercedes to accelerate their car’s development regardless.

“I’m sure their car in the wind tunnel is quite a bit faster than the car they have on track,” said the Italian.

“And they will want to now convert some of this potential into upgrades that make it to the real car. I’m just pretty sure that they will have upgrades.”

Antonelli will take grid penalty at home race

Antonelli, who turns 20 on Tuesday, faces another obstacle in his quest to become F1’s youngest-ever champion.

He will need to take a hefty grid penalty at his home Italian Grand Prix in two weeks as Mercedes plan to swap his car’s power unit to head off potential reliability problems in the second half of the season. That will put Antonelli over his allowance of key components for the year.

“Our theory, our calculations say that that’s the best track to take it. Obviously, our algorithms don’t take the nationality into consideration,” Wolff said. “We’re here to fight for a championship and not the most PR, so that’s what we’re going to do.”

Monza is a high-speed track where the Mercedes engine is likely to be strong, and overtaking is relatively easy, giving Antonelli a chance to make up places. He has accepted the decision.

“I think it still will give me a chance to do a great result and bring home good points,” he said.

“I know I’ve just won two races in a row and had two poles in a row, but at the minute I don’t have the car I need to fight for a championship,” added the Briton, who is 83 points behind Antonelli, with 11 rounds remaining unless the situation in the Middle East forces a calendar change.
Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said cost cap restrictions meant Mercedes did not have the money to implement developments on the car as quickly as they might want.
“We are trying to evenly split that through the season based on our calculations of when we can bring the biggest updates and optimising the championship points,” he told reporters.
“So the ride has been a bit tougher than at the beginning of the year.”
McLaren principal Andrea Stella said he expected Mercedes to accelerate their car’s development regardless.
“I’m sure their car in the wind tunnel is quite a bit faster than the car they have on track,” said the Italian.
“And they will want to now convert some of this potential into upgrades that make it to the real car. I’m just pretty sure that they will have upgrades.”
Antonelli will take grid penalty at home race
Antonelli, who turns 20 on Tuesday, faces another obstacle in his quest to become F1’s youngest-ever champion.

He will need to take a hefty grid penalty at his home Italian Grand Prix in two weeks as Mercedes plan to swap his car’s power unit to head off potential reliability problems in the second half of the season. That will put Antonelli over his allowance of key components for the year.

“Our theory, our calculations say that that’s the best track to take it. Obviously, our algorithms don’t take the nationality into consideration,” Wolff said. “We’re here to fight for a championship and not the most PR, so that’s what we’re going to do.”
Monza is a high-speed track where the Mercedes engine is likely to be strong, and overtaking is relatively easy, giving Antonelli a chance to make up places. He has accepted the decision.
“I think it still will give me a chance to do a great result and bring home good points,” he said.

articles.title: Transfer target Julian Alvarez booed by fans in Atletico Madrid draw
articles.summary: Argentinian striker was targeted by fans while warming up and jeered again after coming on in the 66th minute.
articles.body:
Giuliano Simeone delivered a family rescue act in the dying moments, earning Atletico Madrid a dramatic 2-2 draw with Villarreal after his father Diego’s side had been reduced to 10 men on a scorching afternoon of fan anger towards European transfer target Julian Alvarez.

The hosts appeared ready to collapse after Robin Le Normand was sent off in the 76th minute for bringing down Georges Mikautadze, who converted the resulting penalty to put Villarreal ahead in the Spanish league on Sunday.

list 1 of 4 Salah scores two goals, has two disallowed in first start for Trabzonspor

list 2 of 4 Ceferin won’t challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency but tells him to quit

list 3 of 4 Gauff, Fils win Cincinnati tennis titles in run-up to US Open

list 4 of 4 Maradona’s ‘Hand of God’ ball from Mexico sells for $3.35m

But Atletico found one last burst on the counterattack as Alex Baena released Giuliano down the right and the manager’s son kept his cool, sliding a delicate finish beyond goalkeeper Luiz Junior.

The match had been simmering with tension long before the late drama, with Atletico supporters turning their frustration on Alvarez.

The striker was booed while warming up, jeered again when his name was announced among the substitutes, and met with louder whistles when he came on in the 66th minute.

A section of the crowd chanted: “Let him leave once and for all, let him leave” after Alvarez had revealed at the World Cup that he had spoken to the club about a possible transfer to “fulfil my dream”, with Barcelona heavily linked in Spanish media reports.

The hostility followed him beyond the final whistle as he headed straight to the changing room while teammates saluted the fans, drawing another heavy round of boos.

Atletico manager Diego Simeone confirmed that Alvarez had been advised by the club to leave the pitch after the match.

“The club decided he should not go near the stands or the fans,” the Argentinian said in a news conference.

“It was the club’s decision to keep him away and separate him, so he could go to the locker room.”

Asked what advice he would give the under-fire Alvarez, Simeone responded: “I’m not here to give advice.”

“I have to focus on my job, which is to give my best for Atletico Madrid. If we want to win a title, we need to stick together, have forwards, and have key forwards. We all need to work accordingly on what we need.”

A day earlier, Simeone confirmed that Alvarez would return to the squad despite reports linking him to English champions Arsenal.

Alvarez, still finding fitness after his post-World Cup holiday, was not involved in Atletico’s opening victory over Malaga on Wednesday.

“Yes, he’s going to be included in the squad list tomorrow, and he’s doing better,” Simeone told reporters on Saturday.

“Obviously, he’s still getting up to speed, like all his teammates.”

Simeone said the fans should be respected when asked about it previously, but reiterated that he still views Alvarez as a key player and does not agree with the criticism himself.

“Obviously, I don’t share in any insults or slights. Let that be absolutely clear,” said the coach.

“Julian is a hugely important player for achieving the goals we have as a team. We need him, we’re going to look after him.

“That’s from a sporting standpoint, and we’re going to stand by him. Why? Because he’s our player, and as long as there are players at Atletico Madrid who are mine, I’m going to look after them.”

Barcelona coach Hansi Flick, asked repeatedly on Saturday about whether the Spanish champions had given up their pursuit of Alvarez, said he would not speak about players from other clubs.

articles.title: Give Imran Khan proper medical care, cricket legends urge Pakistani gov’t
articles.summary: Twenty-one cricket captains request PM Sharif’s government to ensure Khan is given timely and independent medical care.
articles.body:
Pakistan’s imprisoned former prime minister and cricket captain, Imran Khan, must be given “humane treatment and proper medical care”, urge a group of cricket greats in a letter seen by Al Jazeera and addressed to Pakistan’s current Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

Twenty-one former captains from around the world have appealed to Sharif’s government to allow an independent assessment of Khan’s health, reinstate his weekly family visits and provide him with the required medical treatment without delay, four signatories of the letter confirmed to Al Jazeera late on Sunday.

Khan, 73, has been imprisoned for the past three years on a range of charges.

On Tuesday , Pakistan’s Supreme Court ordered local authorities to transfer Khan from Adiala jail to the privately run Shifa International Hospital by midnight on Thursday. However on Saturday, Khan’s party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), filed a contempt petition against the government after he was sent to a state-run hospital instead of the private facility ordered by the top court, party officials said.

Khan is widely regarded as one of the world’s greatest-ever all-rounders and arguably Pakistan’s greatest cricketer, who led his nation to its first World Cup win in 1992 and holds the record for most international wins for a Pakistani captain.

Khan’s former cricket adversaries turned friends said the recent events prompted them to pen a letter to Sharif, who replaced the PTI founder as prime minister in April 2022 and again after Pakistan’s last general election in February 2024.

The letter, dated August 23, follows similar outreach in February by 14 former international cricket captains who raised concerns over Khan’s deteriorating health and alleged mistreatment during his imprisonment.

“We wrote then not as politicians, but as former colleagues and rivals who share a bond forged on the cricket field — one that transcends the borders and disputes that too often divide countries,” said the letter.

“We write again now — joined by seven further former captains — because of what has reportedly just occurred,” read the letter, whose signatories include cricket Hall of Famers Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev, Clive Lloyd, Allan Border, Greg Chappell, Ian Chappell, John Wright and David Gower.

Greg Chappell, who shared a friendly bond with Khan following their retirement from cricket, initiated the letter on both occasions.

Lloyd told Al Jazeera on Sunday that he contributed to the letter. Former England captains David Gower, Nasser Hussain and Michael Atherton also confirmed signing it.

Notably, no former Pakistani cricketers were among the signatories of both letters, although several star players have publicly voiced concerns over Khan’s health in the past.

Gavaskar, Dev and Dilip Vengsarkar are the three Indian players among the 21, while former Sri Lanka captain, Arjuna Ranatunga, is the other South Asian name.

Former Australian women’s team captains Alex Blackwell and Belinda Clark are also on the list of signatories.

The letter praised the “welcome steps” of the Supreme Court ordering Khan’s transfer to a private hospital for medical examination by a board that included personal physicians and his sister, Dr Uzma Khan.

The signatories requested the government that:

The medical board directed by the Supreme Court — including Khan’s own doctors — be permitted to complete a full and independent assessment of his health, particularly the reported loss of vision in his right eye.

The weekly family visits reinstated by the court be honoured without interruption or administrative delay.

Whatever the outcome of that medical assessment, the treatment recommended by it be provided without delay.

The former cricketers lamented Khan’s short-lived hospital visit. They reiterated the concerns raised by his family, who said the examination by a state-appointed team and swift return after being declared “medically fit” fell short of what the Supreme Court ordered.

“Whatever the legal and political arguments surrounding his case, the basic decency of ensuring a court-ordered medical process is actually completed is not, in our view, a controversial request,” the letter said.

“It is one we believe every nation that plays this game would recognise as fair.”

The Pakistan government did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for a comment.

Full list of signatories: Michael Atherton, Alex Blackwell, Allan Border, Michael Brearley, Greg Chappell, Ian Chappell, Belinda Clark, Alastair Cook, Sunil Gavaskar, Lee Germon, Adam Gilchrist, David Gower, Kim Hughes, Nasser Hussain, Clive Lloyd, Kapil Dev Nikhanj, Deshamanya Arjuna Ranatunga, Sir Andrew Strauss, Dilip Vengsarkar, Stephen Waugh, John Wright.

Chappell praises Khan’s charisma and power

Following the first appeal made to the Pakistani government in February, Greg Chappell wrote and spoke about his bond with Khan and what prompted him to take the lead in writing the letter.

He said that the letter was meant to highlight a human rights issue rather than be a political intervention and admitted being pleasantly surprised at how quickly it came together since everyone was in the same boat.

“This seems to have had some real impact,” Chappell said as he emphasised the need for the first letter to have “long-lasting impact” rather than fizzle out in the next news cycle.

The former Australian captain praised the charisma Khan wielded both on the field as a cricketer and later when he entered politics.

“People were threatened by someone like Imran because of his aura, personal power and charm,” he told the Cricket Et Al podcast in February.

“They were threatened by him and obviously that’s played its part in this.”

articles.title: Cambuur fans suffer burns as fireworks set off during Dutch league match
articles.summary: Game resumed despite injuries to home fans, but it would have been abandoned if a player or match official had been hit.
articles.body:
Dutch side SC Cambuur has said fans suffered burns, hearing damage and eye injuries after visiting Feyenoord supporters threw fireworks during a league match in Leeuwarden in the Netherlands province of Friesland.

The match on Sunday was halted for about 20 minutes in the first half when fans in the away section lit large numbers of red flares and threw fireworks.

list 1 of 4 Ceferin won’t challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency but tells him to quit

list 2 of 4 Argentina’s Paredes gets 10-game ban for World Cup final scuffle with Spain

list 3 of 4 Mourinho begins second Real reign in Barca but not against old rivals

list 4 of 4 Maresca faces daunting task to succeed Guardiola at Man City

Some were aimed towards sections of the ground containing Cambuur supporters, while one exploded on the pitch just a few metres from Feyenoord goalkeeper Tjark Ernst.

“Our own goalkeeper had a flare fired at him and only just managed to avoid it,” said Feyenoord general manager Robert Eenhoorn, describing the incident as “simply terrible”.

Cambuur said in a statement on Monday that five fans were confirmed to have been injured and that the club would work with the authorities to make sure those responsible were caught.

“It should be clear that setting off and firing fireworks is completely unacceptable and has no place in a football stadium whatsoever,” the club added.

Leeuwarden Mayor Foort van Oosten also condemned the incident and promised an investigation, while the Dutch football association said it would revisit its protocols for incidents of disorder.

The game resumed despite the injuries to the supporters, but it would have been abandoned if a player or match official had been hit.

“That doesn’t feel right,” Jan Bluyssen, KNVB manager of professional football competition affairs, told Dutch news agency ANP.

“We need to examine whether the protocol is still appropriate and how we might want to adjust it.”

Feyenoord won the match 5-2 to maintain their unbeaten start to the new league season, while newly promoted Cambuur have lost all three of their opening matches.

articles.title: Former NBA player Enes Kanter ejected after confrontation with WNBA’s Cloud
articles.summary: Kanter was ejected from the Indiana-Chicago WNBA game after he was confronted by Sky guard Natasha Cloud on court.
articles.body:
Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected after a ‌verbal altercation with WNBA player Natasha Cloud of the Chicago Sky during the third quarter of Chicago’s loss to the visiting Indiana Fever.

Kanter Freedom, sitting ⁠courtside, stood up and took ⁠a few steps towards the court with his arms outstretched after Cloud began pointing and yelling at him at the start of an Indiana timeout on Sunday.

A game official and security personnel got between them, and her teammates pulled Cloud away. The official ⁠gestured for Kanter Freedom to be ejected, and he was escorted from his seat by team and arena security.

Kanter Freedom, 34, wore a black T-shirt that read: “WOMAN noun. Adult human female.”

Cloud, 34, spoke with team and league security after the Sky’s 113-90 loss but did not address the media. ⁠She did post a statement on social media, per CBS Sports.

“To every trans kid/person, You are a part of MY community & tribe. You belong. You’re loved. You’re seen. You’re perfect as you are. & you will always be protected by me,” Cloud wrote.

Kanter Freedom, who had a conversation with police officers before exiting Wintrust Arena, later wrote on his X account, “I just got kicked out of a @WNBA game for supporting WOMEN! Let that sink in, America.”

Sky coach Tyler ‌Marsh said at his postgame news conference that Cloud did not want to be a distraction.

“I told her she wasn’t,” Marsh said. “I told her we all embrace her as someone who protects our team and people who need to be protected. Tash is always gonna stand on that, and we stand for Tash.”

Marsh also had a message for spectators, apparently with Kanter Freedom in mind.

“There’s so many good things about this league and so many good things about the play of these players, that if you come to a game, you should probably come to enjoy the basketball,” Marsh said.

“That seems pretty simple to me. I think these players deserve that and have earned that. Being a ⁠former basketball player, you should probably understand and feel that, too.”

Kanter Freedom, formerly known as Enes Kanter, played ⁠centre for 11 years in the NBA for five teams from 2011-12 to 2021-22 and averaged 11.2 points, 7.8 rebounds and 21.5 minutes in 748 regular-season games (259 starts).

He also has spoken out on social issues, including the debate about transgender athletes. The WNBA, which has never had a known transgender player, has been ensnared in the issue, only heightened ⁠when the Fever’s Sophie Cunningham came out strongly in favour of women’s sports being solely for women.

Cunningham emphasised in her remarks last month in an ESPN profile that “girls should never have to compete with biological men”.

Cunningham later ⁠said on July 22 that she does not “dislike anyone” and that there is “room to love everyone”. She continued, “I’m ⁠also there to love biological women, and I think that there are rights that need to be protected. And, like I said, I’m gonna stand true to that. I’ll never falter in my beliefs in that. But I have never once stated that I hated the trans community.”

There have been rallies outside WNBA arenas involving people who are both pro-Cunningham and ‌anti-Cunningham.

Kanter Freedom and another former NBA player, Royce White, have talked about being eligible for the 2027 WNBA Draft, and both claim to now identify as women, according to media reports.

The league does not have a public policy about transgender participation. The collective bargaining agreement, signed in March, states ‌that “only ‌players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA”.

Cloud is in her 11th season in the WNBA and first in Chicago. She entered Sunday averaging 11.4 points, 5.0 assists, 3.6 rebounds and 29.1 minutes in 36 games (23 starts).

She has also played for the Washington Mystics (2015-19, 2021-23), the Phoenix Mercury (2024) and the New York Liberty (2025).

The league does not have a public policy about transgender participation. The collective bargaining agreement, signed in March, states ‌that “only ‌players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA”.
Cloud is in her 11th season in the WNBA and first in Chicago. She entered Sunday averaging 11.4 points, 5.0 assists, 3.6 rebounds and 29.1 minutes in 36 games (23 starts).
She has also played for the Washington Mystics (2015-19, 2021-23), the Phoenix Mercury (2024) and the New York Liberty (2025).

articles.title: WWE Contracts, '90-Day No-Compete Clause' Finally Explained by Former Champion in New Video
articles.summary: WWE is rumored to be going through roster cuts sometime soon, and one wrestler who went through that experience shined some light on how things play out.
articles.body:
WWE is rumored to be going through roster cuts sometime soon, and one wrestler who went through that experience shined some light on how things play out.

Raj Dhesi, formerly known as one-time WWE Champion Jinder Mahal, resurfaced his video explaining why wrestlers are required to sit out for 90 days after being cut, even though "there is no such thing as a no-compete clause in WWE."

"When you sign a WWE contract, in the writing it states, 'WWE can terminate your contract with 90 days' notice.' So when you receive the phone call, it's them letting you know that in 90 days, your contract is cut," Dhesi explained. "They will pay you for the 90 days. That distinction is very important, because if it was a no-compete clause, you would not get paid for 90 days. For 90 days, you are still under WWE contract."

ESPN Addresses 'Completely False' Rumors About Future WWE Contract

Dhesi went on to add that wrestlers who are cut are pulled from live events and shows to protect both themselves and the company from future liabilities such as injuries or misrepresenting the brand in any way.

"In my opinion, WWE paying you for 90 days is an incredible gesture," Dhesi said. "It gives you time to reorganize your life. You're not making moves out of desperation or anger, and it actually protects both parties."

articles.title: Texans Reportedly Acquire WR Kayshon Boutte From Patriots For S Jaylen Reed
articles.summary: The Houston Texans reportedly acquired wide receiver Kayshon Boutte from the New England Patriots on Monday in exchange for safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round draft pick.
articles.body: The Houston Texans are adding much-needed depth at wide receiver.  Houston has agreed to a deal to acquire wide receiver Kayshon Boutte from the New England Patriots in exchange for safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round draft pick, The Ringer reported on Monday.  The draft selection sent to New England originally belonged to the New Orleans Saints, according to NFL Network. The trade addresses an immediate roster need for Houston following a season-ending knee injury to wide receiver Jayden Higgins during last week's joint practice session with the Las Vegas Raiders. Higgins was expected to hold a starting role in the Houston offense before suffering a torn ACL. Boutte spent his first three seasons with New England after being selected in the 2023 draft. Last season, the receiver recorded 33 receptions for 551 yards and six touchdowns in a bit of a breakout year. However, Boutte became expendable this offseason following the Patriots' moves at wide receiver. They made a big trade for A.J. Brown and signed Romeo Doubs to a pricey contract. Brown and Doubs joined a wide receiver room that also features DeMario "Pop" Douglas, Kyle Williams and Mack Hollins.  So, Boutte's name emerged in trade rumors over the offseason and into training camp. He addressed the trade speculation during training camp last week. "I'm just blocking out the noise. That's the main thing. We all hear the stuff that's going on," Boutte told reporters. "But like I always said, I'm where I'm at. My feet are here, so I'm not worried about what's next or what's behind me. Just being present." In return, New England acquires Reed to bolster their secondary along with future draft compensation. Boutte now joins a Houston receiving group that features Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel, and Tank Dell.
