articles.title: WWE Raw Live Updates, Results and Highlights From Aug. 24
articles.summary: Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of WWE Raw on August 24. Scroll down for updates of all the action from Ottawa, Ontario, Canada.
articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of WWE Raw on August 24. Scroll down for updates of all the action from Ottawa, Ontario, Canada.

OTM put Jimmy through the announce table while Keys held Jey and forced him to watch. The show ended with Knight, Solo and The Usos all down around the ring as OTM and Keys stood tall in the ring.

The Usos still had the upper hand all through the break into the next segment. They kept Sikoa isolated with quick tags and double-team moves.

The Street Champ hit a desperate clothesline to give himself some breathing room. Knight and Jimmy both tagged in at the same time. The Megastar unloaded on the elder Uso with jabs and a clothesline.

As Jey and Solo were fighting at ringside, Royce Keys put both of them through the barricade with a huge Spear. In the ring, OTM from NXT attacked Knight and Big Jim.

Bronco Nima and Lucien Price helped Keys destroy all four men. It looks like we officially have a new trio on Raw to compete with The Bloodline.

The Usos vs. LA Knight and Solo Sikoa Part 1

Jimmy and LA came out of the gate hot as soon as the bell rang. Knight hit a clothesline to get the first takedown before tagging in Solo for a double back elbow.

The Usos were able to take control with some combined attacks. They took Solo out of the ring and drilled him with a double superkick.

After a video hyping Zilla Fatu in NXT, Chad Gable was talking to Pearce backstage, and the GM said he is going to go find a new challenger for him. Ethan Page walked up and congratulated him on winning the IC title from Rey Mysterio.

All Ego said Gable is intimidated by him, but Gable reminded him that he beat him to earn the title shot in the first place. He said he would have given Page a title shot, but the way he is acting has made him change his mind.

Back in the arena, The Usos came out for their match against Sikoa and Knight.

Penta had control through the break, but the living skeleton started to regain his footing. He took Penta down with a few high-flying moves and scored a two-count with a powerslam.

La Parka drilled the former IC champion with a DDT for a close two-count. Penta caught him with a Penta Driver, but he couldn't keep him down for the pin.

A Spanish Fly got La Parka another near-fall before Penta wrenched his arm behind his back. He hit the Mexican Destroyer to seal the victory and advance to the finals.

This was a solid match, but the most intriguing part of this is that we will see Penta and Fenix fight in the finals next week to determine who gets to face Roman Reigns for the world title in Mexico City.

Lyra Valkyria had a brief exchange with Sol Ruca and Iyo Sky before Penta made his way out first to take on La Parka in the other semifinal match in the ongoing No. 1 Contender's tournament.

The luchadores started with a fast-paced exchange, but Penta took control. He sent La Parka out of the ring so he could take him down with a dive through the ropes.

La Parka recovered and hit a moonsault from the middle rope to the floor. Penta caught him with a superkick as he was coming off the top rope, but it only got him a two-count.

We returned to see Cass missing a corner splash. Evans tried to build a little momentum, but he couldn't take Cass off his feet. The big man caught him, but Evans sent him over the top rope before hitting a suicide dive.

The Young OG put Cass in the timekeeper's area so he could hit a running dive over the barricade. Evans started unloading on him with punches and kicks.

He brought Cass back in the ring and hit the Red Dot kick and a springboard clothesline. He went for the OG Cutter, but Cass shoved him off the top turnbuckle.

He nailed Je'Von with a big boot for the win. This seemed like a pretty abrupt ending, and an odd choice for a finishing move.

Judgment Day attacked Evans after Cass left the ring and left him down and out.

Big Cass has been making Evans' life hard recently, so they met in what was the first match Cass has had in WWE since returning. The way they shot the entrance for Cass was designed to make him look as big as possible, and it worked.

Evans tried to stick and move to avoid the big man. He brought the powerhouse out of the ring with a hurricanrana, but when he went for a slingshot crossbody, Cass caught him. Je'Von got back in the ring and Cass leveled him with a clothesline over the top rope.

Michael Cole talked about the journey Cass has been on since he was fired by WWE eight years ago as we saw him throw Evans into the barricade. He said Cass has taken no accountability for his actions.

Paul Heyman and Adam Pearce were in the ring for a contract signing between Oba Femi and Bron Breakker. The Ruler made his entrance first as the crowd chanted his name.

Breakker asked Femi who he thinks he is, claiming to be the future. He asked what Femi has done to earn the title of being the future of WWE. He diminished Femi's King of the Ring win and victory over Brock Lesnar.

He talked a lot of trash about how Femi wouldn't even be where he is if Breakker hadn't been out with an injury for months. The Ruler called him an angry, orange man and said he can't understand that his chances of being the face of WWE are gone.

Breakker signed the contract and said Femi is going to realize he is the one guy he can't beat. He taunted Oba by saying Heyman should sign it for him since they are so close now.

Bron and Oba ended up brawling after Breakker threatened Heyman. Austin Theory showed up to help his partner, but Femi fought them off and put Theory through the table.

We returned to see both men trading chops. Lee hit a few kicks to take Fenix off his feet. He hit a beautiful float over into a powerbomb, but it couldn't get him the win.

They continued to trade fast-paced offense until they ended up fighting near the announce table. Fenix was tripped on the table, which gave Lee an opening to hit a massive cannonball through the second rope that hit Fenix off the top of the table.

That spot was wild! The crowd chanted "This is awesome" as Lee brought Fenix in for a tornado DDT to get a two-count. Rey hit a brainbuster as he began regaining momentum.

He got Lee up for the Mexican Muscle Buster, but Lee countered into the Styles Clash for a near-fall. They kept going back and forth until Fenix finally hit his finisher to get the win.

This match was incredible. If you are not watching the show live, make sure you check this one out. Both guys worked their butts off to make this awesome.

The No. 1 Contender's tournament continued this week with Rey Fenix taking on Dragon Lee in the semifinals. Before the match, Je'Von Evans attacked Dom Mysterio and JD McDonagh backstage, which Rey Mysterio seemed to love.

They started with a quick exchange of holds and counters. Neither man could get an advantage as they went move for move. They came to a stalemate before they began trading strikes.

Lee was the first one to take control with a nice dropkick in the corner for a two-count, but Fenix wasn't down for long. He hit the running kick across the top rope he is known for, and he followed it with a diving crossbody for a near-fall.

The AAA cruiserweight champion hit a moonsault on the floor, but when they got back into the ring, Lee hit a German suplex. He took Fenix down with a huge dive over the top rope that sent us into the break.

Perez had control through the break, but Vaquer was starting to make a comeback when we returned. Roxy had to pull her hair to escape an abdominal stretch, but the former world champion maintained control.

She used the Devil's Kiss to slam Roxanne's head into the mat 10 times. She used a brutal dragon screw leg whip in the corner before hitting a running double knee against the turnbuckle.

Perez recovered and hit a nice shining wizard for a two-count. Stephanie countered a crossface into a package backbreaker. Morgan interfered while Rodriguez distracted the ref. This brought out Becky Lynch.

Roxy tried to take advantage of all the mayhem, but Vaquer was able to hit her with her finisher to score the win.

Lynch took Morgan out at ringside before getting into the ring. She and Vaquer exchanged a few words before The Man made her exit.

Stephanie Vaquer vs. Roxanne Perez Part 1

Stephanie Vaquer returned to action for the first time since WrestleMania to take on Roxanne Perez. La Primera made her way to the ring right before the break. Liv Morgan and Raquel Rodriguez were at ringside.

Perez played some mind games by avoiding Vaquer a few times before slapping her and then hiding in the ropes. Once Vaquer got her hands on her, she wrestled her to the mat and stomped on her elbow.

Roxy fooled her into chasing her back into the ring. They traded stiff slaps before Stephanie almost locked her in an armbar. Vaquer hit a running kick in the corner, but a distraction from Raquel allowed Perez to shove her off the top rope.

LA Knight came to the ring to kick things off with a promo. He said he needs to talk about the coward, Roman Reigns.

He talked about Reigns refusing to defend the belt against him and how he wasn't able to compete in the current tournament going on with AAA.

Solo Sikoa appeared in the crowd and used Knight's own catchphrase before thanking him for helping out last week with The Bloodline. A moment later, The Usos started making their way to the ring.

When Jey sent him a warning shot, Solo pretended like he was in The Matrix to avoid it. They ended up agreeing to a tag match with the four of them for later in the show.

Knight and Sikoa are so great together. They are always funny whenever they interact.

Monday Night Raw is officially on the air. This week's episode had an early start time due to a double taping alongside SmackDown.

Shots of various Superstars backstage were shown before we went to a video recapping what happened last week with The Bloodline.

articles.title: Browns Making Another QB Error? 7 Takeaways From Week 2 Of The Preseason
articles.summary: Here's what we learned from this week's preseason games.
articles.body: Two weeks of preseason games are in the books, and we're starting to see the light at the end of the tunnel.  This past week's slate of preseason games, plus joint practices, brought us more glimpses of what we could expect to see in the regular season. But it brought some drama, too. Deshaun Watson was named the Cleveland Browns' starting quarterback on Monday after making pointed remarks to the team's fans following his lackluster performance on Saturday. There's also an unusual storyline developing with players who might wind up playing college football in the next couple of weeks.  So, with only one more preseason week to go, here are our takeaways from the latest slate of preseason games.  1. Deshaun Watson Didn’t Deserve The Starting Job In Cleveland. He Got It Anyway. Ralph Vacchiano: Deshaun Watson showed everyone on Saturday why he shouldn’t be the Cleveland Browns' starting quarterback, with a terrible on-field performance and an even worse one off the field. Then, Todd Monken gave him the job anyway.  Maybe that’s a sign that the new Browns coach had nothing but bad options in his quarterback competition, but his choice still couldn’t have been any worse. He went with a 30-year-old who’ll surely be an ex-Brown next season over a somewhat promising young quarterback, Shedeur Sanders. And he did it two days after Watson was terrible in a preseason game against the Bills (5 of 12 for 36 yards and an interception) and then showed an incredible lack of self-awareness (and an abundance of immaturity) when he whined about being booed. "I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do with the performance," Watson said. "It’s a little more personal than that. So, I think that’s a disrespectful thing." OK, that’s a little rich and a lot outrageous, coming from the man who got the biggest fully-guaranteed contract in NFL history from the Browns in 2022 (five years, $230 million) even though he hadn’t played in two years and was accused of sexual misconduct by 27 women. He then rewarded that startling generosity by only being healthy enough to play in 19 games over the last four seasons — and not particularly well, either. Even without that bad moment, though, Monken still made the wrong choice. The coach had been leaning this way, multiple team sources told me, in part because the Browns’ early schedule is overloaded with road games (their first two and six of their first nine), and Monken thought Watson’s veteran presence would help his young team. But Watson’s play didn’t warrant that faith. He was just 16 of 27 for 162 yards and an interception in two preseason games. His passer rating of 61.0 was even a notch below Sanders’ 65.2. So while it’s true that there was no good option here, it’s also true that really is no upside to Watson, who is understandably reviled by what seems to be a majority of the Browns’ fan base. Starting Sanders at least would’ve given them hope that he can get better, something to look forward to other than the QB-rich 2027 draft. Instead, Monken latched on to the anchor that has been scraping the Browns along rock bottom for the last five years. Sanders will surely get a shot later this season. But as usual in Cleveland, any hope for the future is delayed. 2. Yes, The Pipeline To The Pros Goes Both Ways Greg Auman: The most backwards trend of the NFL preseason? Marginal players testing the waters of playing in NFL preseason games and  … going back to college. It seems impossible, but these days, if you can get a judge to rule the right way, traditional lines of amateurism and eligibility can disappear. The NCAA’s shift to a five-year eligibility model wasn’t intended to be backdated for athletes who had exhausted their window – and signed a pro contract, gotten paid and even played for NFL teams. But that’s really happening, leaving general managers to wonder if they’ll lose players off their roster to the allure of NIL money from colleges. Tight end Dae’Quan Wright, an undrafted rookie with the Browns, put his name in the transfer portal. Cleveland has since waived him, setting him up to play for LSU this fall. "Man, ain’t this s--- crazy?" Browns coach Todd Monken said. "I mean, I don’t even know what to say … I wondered why Lane Kiffin reached out a week ago. Now I know. I didn’t call him back, guess I should have." Speaking of LSU, consider Tampa Bay Buccaneers undrafted rookie linebacker Jack Pyburn, who had two sacks in Tampa Bay’s preseason opener. He’s also one of the players granted a temporary restraining order that could allow him to return to college football. He played at LSU last year, and that sets up the man-bites-dog possibility of an NFL player leaving early for college. The fall semester at LSU started on Monday, and NFL rosters will be cut from 90 players to 53 by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday. It’s unlikely the Bucs will keep Pyburn for their 53, but he has (had?) a good shot at their practice squad. That pays $247,500 for a full season, and Pyburn could make three or four times that much on the Van Wilder go-back-to-college route. Pyburn said after Saturday’s preseason game that his agents had told the Bucs that college was a potential "backup plan," but when pressed as to what he might decide if choosing between an NFL practice squad and going back to college, he was noncommittal. "Ultimately, that’s a decision I’m going to have to make with my family, talk to my agents and see what’s the best business decision and what’s the best option for me and my future career," he said. Yes, it’s NFL "respect my decision" season. Players would have to repay their NFL employers to regain college eligibility. Pyburn got a $15,000 bonus and $100,000 in guaranteed salary, but it’s possible that college NIL payments could also be covered by "offset" language standard in such contracts, normally intended so if NFL Team B pays a player to be on their practice squad, that subtracts from the money NFL Team A was on the hook for by their guarantee. The league will have to sort out the ramifications. Can a player already passed over once in the draft get another shot, like baseball players do? This was already happening with basketball and G League players showing up on college rosters, but for NFL teams, it’s made roster-building even more complicated by the idea that players can make more money playing football at a lower level. 3. Stetson Bennett Commands Offense, Cements Role As Rams' Backup QB Eric D. Williams: With Jimmy Garoppolo no longer on the roster, Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay’s search for someone to fill that void, should reigning MVP Matthew Stafford suffer an injury during the regular season, appears to be over. In the battle between Ty Simpson and Stetson Bennett, the Alabama product cracked the door open with a sparkling performance in a Week 1 preseason win over the Kansas City Chiefs. But Bennett may have closed the door by playing well in a 34-0 victory over the New Orleans Saints at SoFi Stadium. The Georgia product finished with two rushing touchdowns in the first half, leading the Rams to scoring drives on four of his five possessions. Bennett finished 19 of 31 for 181 yards, with no touchdown passes and no interceptions for a 77.5 passer rating.  Ty Simpson also played solidly, finishing 8 of 12 for 73 yards in the second half. Simpson led the offense on one scoring drive. However, Bennett impressed McVay by the way he led the offense, with quarterbacks coach and associated offensive coordinator Dave Ragone calling the plays – although he didn’t like Bennett reaching for the pylon with the ball on his first rushing touchdown. "I loved the fact that he used his legs," McVay said. "We’ll learn from reaching the ball into the end zone, even though I challenged that and we were successful. We don’t want to leave ourselves susceptible to losing the ball out of the end zone where it goes for a touchback. "But he did a great job. I thought he got an opportunity to really showcase a lot of his skills." 4. Daniel Jones Primed To Pick Up From Where He Left Off Last Season Ben Arthur: Watching the Indianapolis Colts quarterback at Wednesday’s joint practice with the Atlanta Falcons, it was impossible for me to tell that he tore his Achilles just eight months ago. Everything you want your passer to do — drop back, scramble, throw on the move, evade pressure — Jones looked normal in doing so. Oh, and he was carving up the Falcons’ secondary as well. With Indianapolis’ rushing attack struggling, Jones was near perfect in the pass game, targeting various receivers.  We still need to see Jones move and perform in games. But all the early signs suggest that he can pick up from last season, when he was playing the best ball of his career before a broken leg slowed him down and the Achilles injury ended his season.  "I think with any major rehab process, you're always kind of progressing and getting back and getting used to doing everything, building up the reps on it, building up just your conditioning level," Jones said Wednesday. "I feel really good and there's nothing I don't feel good doing." The Colts’ pass-catching situation around Jones is a bit shaky at the moment, given star tight end Tyler Warren (groin) and wide receiver Alec Pierce (offseason ankle surgery) are currently sidelined. But when they return, they’ll add to a group that features one of the league’s best slot receivers in Josh Downs and recent signee Keenan Allen, who’s been a dominant force on third down.  That’s a cast of receivers Jones can find success with.  "I think it could be really special, to be honest," Colts coach Shane Steichen said of the pass-catching group. "Alec (Pierce) obviously is a hell of a football player, which you guys know. [Josh] Downs, Tyler [Warren], and then adding Keenan [Allen] to the fold. I think we can do a lot with those guys and move bodies around and find matchups."  5. Let’s Have A Conversation About Chiefs Breakout Rookie WR Cyrus Allen Henry McKenna: If you’ve been following training camp for Kansas City, you’ve heard of Allen. If you’re the type who combs X for potential breakout stars in fantasy football, you’ve heard of Allen. If you’re obsessed with NFL rookies and the draft, you’ve heard of Allen.  His training camp highlights have been crazy. And Andy Reid didn’t slow the hype’s momentum. "He's done a nice job," Reid said of Allen. "The quarterback trusts him." This was the first week of training camp. Allen was a sixth-round pick out of Louisiana Tech. It felt like a big proclamation, particularly given that Rashee Rice has a history of missing time due to injuries and suspensions and Xavier Worthy has failed to live up to his first-round hype.  Since then, Allen has played well — steadily doing what he could to move up the depth chart. That included scoring touchdowns with the first-team when paired with Patrick Mahomes. That also included beating first-round cornerback Mansoor Delane in 1-on-1s and team drills (7x7 and 11x11), per reporters on the scene. But here’s the truth for anyone expecting the second coming of Tyreek Hill. The folks at Arrowhead Pride broke it down with depth. But it’s likely — perhaps even overly optimistic — to project 60 for Allen. And only six receivers converted 60 targets into 500+ receiving yards in 2025. But before he wows in the box score, he’ll need to land in the WR3 spot. Given that he was playing behind Tyquan Thornton and Jaylen Royals in the second preseason game, Allen appears to be WR5. For what it’s worth, Hill had 83 targets, 61 catches, 593 yards and six touchdowns in his rookie season. That would be a great year for Allen. So keep an eye on him. He’s a real playmaker. But let’s stay reasonable for a rookie in a Chiefs' offense that has a lot of mouths to feed. 6. De’Zhaun Stribling Shows Kyle Shanahan Knows How To Evaluate WRs Williams: NFL draft analysts were up in arms over the San Francisco 49ers taking Ole Miss product De’Zhaun Stribling in the second round, believing the organization had reached for a player that some consensus draft boards had going later in the draft. However, through two weeks of preseason play, Stribling has acquitted himself nicely. Stribling is tied for the league lead with 11 catches for 109 yards, with a long of 32 yards. He finished with four catches for 46 yards in a win over the Los Angeles Chargers this week.  I had a chance to watch Stribling in a joint practice at the Chargers’ facility. At 6-2 and 210 pounds, Stribling is an easy mover with suction-cup hands that can make contested catches in congested areas. Along with that, Stribling has the potential for explosive playmaking ability to do something after the catch, a key attribute in Shanahan’s offense. With Ricky Pearsall out for the year and Brandon Ayiuk no longer on the roster, Stribling should find a significant role in San Francisco’s offense this season. "I love how he handles himself," Shanahan said about Stribling. "He takes coaching well and never seems to take anything personally. He’s been a real fun guy to coach so far." 7. Bills’ Thin WR Corps May Be More Of A Problem Than Ever Vacchiano: One great NFL mystery of this generation will surely be why the Buffalo Bills, with arguably the best quarterback in the league in Josh Allen, keep failing to surround him with top-end receivers. And once again, heading towards a season they hope will end in a Super Bowl, that failure is being exposed. Though they are getting a solid performance this summer from D.J. Moore, the veteran "No. 1" wideout they acquired from the Chicago Bears, the rest of the corps is falling apart. Keon Coleman, their second-best receiver last season (38 receptions for 404 yards and four touchdowns), is nursing a concerning sprained toe. Khalil Shakir, last season’s top wideout (72 receptions for 719 yards and four touchdowns), missed the joint practices and preseason game against the Browns last week with an undisclosed injury. And rookie Skyler Bell, their fourth-round pick, has missed two weeks with a groin injury. That leaves Allen right now with Moore, who cost the Bills a second-round pick in March, Joshua Palmer (22 receptions for 303 yards and zero touchdowns) last season, and … not much else. That, of course, is not how the Bills see it. One team source told me their belief is that Allen can win with almost anyone around him, and that he can take what looks like a below-average group and make them much better. They are also convinced that Moore, at age 29, can reverse his steep, two-year decline simply by playing with an elite quarterback. It’s a gamble, of course, because otherwise all the pieces are in place in Buffalo: A powerful running game led by James Cook, a top offensive line, a top-10 defense that gets a boost from the addition of edge rusher Bradley Chubb. And of course, the brilliance of Allen will always give them a shot. Still, it’s hard not to imagine what this team would look like with just one elite receiver by Allen’s side. It would make their path to Buffalo’s first Super Bowl in 33 years look a lot easier than it currently is.

articles.title: Why 49ers Appear To Be Driving Off The Cliff Entering 2026 Season
articles.summary: During Monday's edition of The Herd, Colin Cowherd evaluated the overall state of the 49ers, questioning whether San Francisco can maintain their position among the elite teams in the NFC.
articles.body: The San Francisco 49ers enter the upcoming regular season with expectations to remain competitive within arguably the best division in football while battling early injuries, older franchise mainstays returning from surgeries, and, most recently, off-field news involving the team's owner.  That doesn't seem to be a recipe for success, and Colin Cowherd agrees. During Monday's edition of The Herd, Cowherd questioned whether San Francisco can maintain its position among the elite teams in the conference. "I tend to think the Niners are very close to pulling a Thelma and Louise and driving off the cliff here," Cowherd said, comparing the 49ers to the hit '90s movie. On paper, the 49ers have reloaded with talent. They signed star wide receiver Mike Evans to beef up their wide receiver room and brought back Dre Greenlaw to solidify what they have at linebacker.  However, tight end George Kittle continues working back from Achilles surgery with a chance to play in Week 1, and running back Christian McCaffrey remains on a planned load management schedule during practice reps.  With that in mind, Cowherd pointed out that age and recovery timelines across essential positions present distinct hurdles for San Francisco when compared to younger rosters across the league. The roster remains heavily reliant on a core group of established veterans, several of which are returning from surgical procedures. "This is an old, old team, oldest roster in the NFL, and almost all their old guys are coming off serious surgeries," Cowherd said. "They are really dependent on five older players: Trent Williams, left tackle, he's 38. Kittle, going to be a hall of farmer, coming off surgery. Nick Bosa, coming off his second surgery. Christian McCaffrey led the NFL in touches. Mike Evans, who is often banged up, though I love him and Fred Warner off a surgery as well." San Francisco's depth issues have been compounded by injuries to recent high draft selections. "Don't forget their last two first-round picks: Ricky Pearsall, out for the year, injured. … Mykel Williams, who is a great young talent, he's banged up and won't be there for Week 1," Cowherd added. "They are hanging on by peptides and a prayer." Compared to the recent success NFC West rivals the Seahawks and Rams have had in the draft, the Niners will have their work cut out for them. "The Seahawks and the Rams have drafted so brilliantly over the last three years, very few misses. … Those are four games the Niners go in as an underdog," Cowherd said. San Francisco receives early scheduling relief to begin the regular season. Following their trip to Australia, the team returns home for consecutive games against the Miami Dolphins and Arizona Cardinals before entering a more challenging stretch that includes matchups against the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos. Despite the favorable early home slate, Cowherd expressed skepticism regarding San Francisco's postseason prospects over a full 17-game schedule. "I don't think they're a playoff team," Cowherd said. "I love the coach. I love McCaffrey. I love the organization. I think they're heading right for a cliff." paragraphs: The San Francisco 49ers enter the upcoming regular season with expectations to remain competitive within arguably the best division in football while battling early injuries, older franchise mainstays returning from surgeries, and, most recently, off-field news involving the team's owner.  That doesn't seem to be a recipe for success, and Colin Cowherd agrees. During Monday's edition of The Herd, Cowherd questioned whether San Francisco can maintain its position among the elite teams in the conference. "I tend to think the Niners are very close to pulling a Thelma and Louise and driving off the cliff here," Cowherd said, comparing the 49ers to the hit '90s movie. On paper, the 49ers have reloaded with talent. They signed star wide receiver Mike Evans to beef up their wide receiver room and brought back Dre Greenlaw to solidify what they have at linebacker.  However, tight end George Kittle continues working back from Achilles surgery with a chance to play in Week 1, and running back Christian McCaffrey remains on a planned load management schedule during practice reps.  With that in mind, Cowherd pointed out that age and recovery timelines across essential positions present distinct hurdles for San Francisco when compared to younger rosters across the league. The roster remains heavily reliant on a core group of established veterans, several of which are returning from surgical procedures. "This is an old, old team, oldest roster in the NFL, and almost all their old guys are coming off serious surgeries," Cowherd said. "They are really dependent on five older players: Trent Williams, left tackle, he's 38. Kittle, going to be a hall of farmer, coming off surgery. Nick Bosa, coming off his second surgery. Christian McCaffrey led the NFL in touches. Mike Evans, who is often banged up, though I love him and Fred Warner off a surgery as well." San Francisco's depth issues have been compounded by injuries to recent high draft selections. "Don't forget their last two first-round picks: Ricky Pearsall, out for the year, injured. … Mykel Williams, who is a great young talent, he's banged up and won't be there for Week 1," Cowherd added. "They are hanging on by peptides and a prayer." Compared to the recent success NFC West rivals the Seahawks and Rams have had in the draft, the Niners will have their work cut out for them. "The Seahawks and the Rams have drafted so brilliantly over the last three years, very few misses. … Those are four games the Niners go in as an underdog," Cowherd said. San Francisco receives early scheduling relief to begin the regular season. Following their trip to Australia, the team returns home for consecutive games against the Miami Dolphins and Arizona Cardinals before entering a more challenging stretch that includes matchups against the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos. Despite the favorable early home slate, Cowherd expressed skepticism regarding San Francisco's postseason prospects over a full 17-game schedule. "I don't think they're a playoff team," Cowherd said. "I love the coach. I love McCaffrey. I love the organization. I think they're heading right for a cliff." articles.title: Ex-Oregon State RB Anthony Hankerson Set For College Return After Being Waived By Seahawks
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks have waived running back Anthony Hankerson, who could try to play in college again.
articles.body: The Seattle Seahawks have waived running back Anthony Hankerson, who could try to play in college again. Hankerson signed with the Seahawks last week and rushed for 10 yards on five carries in their 19-16 preseason loss at Tennessee on Sunday night. He also caught two passes for nine yards. He is among 16 players who graduated high school in 2022 and became eligible to play a fifth collegiate season thanks to a Louisiana court order last week. Once he clears waivers, he could enter the transfer portal. Running back T.J. Harden, who played for the Seahawks in their preseason game against Dallas, was also among those granted a temporary restraining order by the Louisiana judge. Harden, who played last year at SMU and went undrafted, was waived by the Seahawks and entered the portal last week. Hankerson was an undrafted rookie out of Oregon State who signed with Miami in April, then was waived earlier this month. He ran for 1,086 yards and nine touchdowns last season, his second in Corvallis. He also had 22 catches for 123 yards. Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: Cal Raleigh Hits Career-High 3 Homers For Mariners Amid Season-Long Slump
articles.summary: Cal Raleigh busted out of a season-long slump with the first three-homer game of his career.
articles.body: Cal Raleigh busted out of a season-long slump with the first three-homer game of his career Monday night. The switch-hitting catcher capped a five-run first inning with a two-run shot off struggling Philadelphia Phillies ace Zack Wheeler. Raleigh added a leadoff homer against Wheeler in the fifth and a solo drive off reliever Chase Shugart in the seventh to give him 17 home runs this season. It was the first multihomer game of the year for Raleigh, who finished 3 for 3 with a walk in a 9-2 victory and raised his batting average from .159 to .167. Raleigh was runner-up for the AL MVP award last year, when he led the majors with 60 home runs and added 125 RBIs. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.summary: Chess News: Indian Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa secured his place in the final of the last leg of the Grand Chess Tour with a commanding 19-9 victory over Germany.
articles.body: Indian Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa secured his place in the final of the last leg of the Grand Chess Tour with a commanding 19-9 victory over Germanyâs Vincent Keymer.Praggnanandhaa will now face pre-event favourite and defending champion Fabiano Caruana of the USA in the title clash.The Indian entered the final day with a six-point advantage after winning the second Classical game against Keymer. With the competition moving to shorter formats, Praggnanandhaa wasted little time in strengthening his position.He won both Rapid games against Keymer to establish an unassailable 17-3 lead. Another victory in the opening Blitz game took Praggnanandhaa to 19 points and confirmed his place in the final.The remaining Blitz games still had to be completed under the tournament rules, and Keymer managed to finish strongly by winning the final three Blitz encounters. However, the Germanâs late surge could not alter the outcome as Praggnanandhaa had already secured a decisive advantage.Caruana also booked his place in the final after defeating fellow American Wesley So 18-9. The defending championâs performance in the faster formats proved decisive, particularly during the Blitz games.Caruana had not traditionally been regarded as a dominant player in faster formats, but his performance on Monday showed that he could challenge that perception when it mattered.The Grand Chess Tour finale carries a total prize purse of USD 450,000, with USD 200,000 going to the winner and USD 125,000 to the losing finalist.Although Caruana enters the final as the favourite, Praggnanandhaa has already shown he can thrive under pressure and will look to produce another strong performance against the defending champion.In the third-place play-off, Keymer will meet another American, Wesley So. articles.title: Sir Billy Boston: 'A world-class athlete, whose story deserved to be told'
articles.summary: Rugby league commentator Matt Newsum says Sir Billy Boston was a "world-class athlete, whose story deserved to be told".
articles.body:
When Sir Billy Boston was knighted in 2025, it was a unique moment for rugby league.

For the first time, this rebel sport from the north of England had been recognised in such a manner; one of its heroes had been acknowledged for their contribution to history through the game.

Sir Billy was a fitting recipient of the honour and a world-class athlete, whose story deserved to be told.

You can tell the importance of someone by how many statues have been erected in tribute, and Sir Billy Boston wasn't lacking.

His name was chosen as one of just five to grace Wembley's monument to rugby league's Challenge Cup, while years after his departure north, his home city of Cardiff also ensured his legacy remained cast-iron strong as he formed part of a three-man tribute along with Clive Sullivan and Gus Risman.

Unsurprisingly, Boston is also captured in bronze in his adopted home of Wigan; the place where his legend really came to life.

Born and brought up in Cardiff's ethnically-eclectic Tiger Bay district, he learned his rugby skills on the streets and with the talent factory-esque Cardiff International Athletic Club.

Like all Welsh lads he harboured dreams of playing for his local club Cardiff RFC and hopefully the national team.

Like others before and after for a time, Boston found those routes blocked, having to travel to Neath and Pontypridd to trial before his military service took him north.

It was here where the league scouts came calling, and Wigan persuaded Boston to turn professional in 1953, forever ending his union dreams in the time of 'sine die' penalties for liaising with league personnel.

Â£3,000 could easily buy a house at that stage, while it proved money well spent as he took to the new code like a duck to water, scoring with his first touch in a Wigan A team game.

This prime specimen of Welsh breezeblock had everything; he was quick, he could step and as former player and BBC commentator Ray French put it - his fend was like "being hit in the face with shovel".

The sepia footage and slow shutter speeds of the cameras that captured his magic during his playing days simply cannot dull his brilliance.

Whether it was bustling over for another try in cherry and white hoops at Wembley or crushing the Aussies at Sydney Cricket Ground, Boston was a blur of speed, footwork and power.

Having swiftly progressed to the first team at Central Park, he would go on to score 478 tries in 488 games for Wigan, and tales of his feats would be passed down through generations. There are very few down at the Brick Community Stadium these days who don't know of Sir Billy, young or old, his name carried a cache right until his last.

Great Britain gave him the international recognition denied to him by Wales, and he rewarded the selectors by racking up the tries, particularly against the Australians who would bear the brunt of his scoring ability.

He scored 36 tries alone on his maiden Great Britain tour, dazzling both Australia and New Zealand in 1954 under captain and fellow Welshman Dickie Williams.

Boston was a phenomenal rugby league player, but there is also a powerful message in how in post-war Britain a black athlete could become a hugely popular figure by communities adjusting to a new, more diverse world.

Others like Roy Francis beforehand, Johnny Freeman, and Colin Dixon, also became established names, but never quite sprinkled the same stardust as Sir Billy.

It paved the way for players such as Ellery Hanley and Martin Offiah to charm the public with their talents, while modern day talent such as Junior Nsemba and Kai Pearce-Paul continues to stand out in a sport which has broken down barriers for years.

Sir Billy had a unique unifying effect on a normally partisan and tribal rugby league community.

He was revered naturally in Wigan, his adopted home, but you won't hear a boo or jeer at mention of Boston anywhere - not even at sworn rivals St Helens where they appreciate a good footballer when they see one.

Still a regular visitor to Wigan games right up to his passing, it was always a beautiful moment when the cameras found him, the crowd spotting him on the screen bursting into cheer, and the realisation creeping over his face in the shape of a smile.

There was a photo of him and his wife Lady Joan, who had died just a few weeks previously, on her seat with flowers at Wigan's game with Wakefield last week. There is a poignancy that Sir Billy departed soon after her.

His seat will always be reserved at Wigan, and he will be dearly missed but certainly not forgotten.

articles.title: How did Washington Capitals captain Alex Ovechkin reportedly collect 33 traffic fines in Russia
articles.summary: NHL News: Washington Capitals captain Alex Ovechkin reportedly collected 33 traffic fines in Russia during his offseason, totaling around 82,000 rubles. The fines were for various offenses and have sparked interest due to Ovechkin's celebrity status.
articles.body: Alex Ovechkin reportedly had an unusually high number of traffic violations in his native Russia during a portion of his NHL offseason. According to reports from Russian outlet Mash Sport, the Washington Capitals captain has been fined 33 times over the course of roughly four months. The total reported was 82,000 rubles, or about $1,000 at current media conversions.The alleged violations occurred during Ovechkin's absence from the NHL over the summer. They allegedly included speeding, toll-road violations, unpaid parking fines and stopping or parking in restricted areas. The attention around the story hasnât been on the financial value of the penalties, but rather on the sheer quantity of citations.Why did Alex Ovechkin reportedly receive traffic fines in Russia?During the NHL offseason, Alex Ovechkin was reportedly fined for multiple traffic violations in Russia. The 33 citations were connected to his Aurus Arsenal, a luxury Russian minivan tied to the Washington Capitals star, reports said.The citations reported were for multiple offences, not one repeated offence. One of the infractions was speeding, while other reports also mentioned toll road fines, parking tickets and stopping or parking in restricted areas. All in all, it came to 82 thousand rubles.That means the headline figure of 33 fines does not necessarily equate to 33 separate police stops. Available reports indicate the infractions were traffic-related citations tied to Ovechkinâs vehicle while in Russia for an extended period.Why did Alex Ovechkin reportedly receive traffic fines in Russia?According to reports, Ovechkin has already paid most of the reported fines. One citation was still reported outstanding, worth 4,500 rubles.The number of violations makes the incident unusual, though itâs a relatively small financial penalty in relation to the scale of Ovechkinâs NHL earnings. The 40-year-old forward is still one of the NHLâs most recognisable players, so an off-season stat that included 33 traffic tickets was bound to get some attention.Traffic reports donât mention an NHL suspension, hockey-related discipline, injury or roster issue with the Washington Capitals. Instead, the incident happened away from NHL competition during Ovechkinâs off-season in Russia.Ovechkin will return to Washington for his 22nd NHL season after signing a new one-year contract with the Capitals. He comes into the campaign after scoring 32 goals and 32 assists in 82 games in 2025-26.The timing is odd because Ovechkin has otherwise been spending his offseason preparing for another NHL season. When the new season begins, he will again be a center of attention for the Washington Capitals, who made him the NHLâs all-time regular-season goals leader.For now, the 33 traffic tickets reported are an unusual offseason footnote for a player whose career stats usually center on goals, records and championships.The reports also make it clear that this is about traffic violations, not a legal issue related to his NHL career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Crystal Palace: Why is Premier League club's home kit white?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains why Crystal Palace are wearing a white home shirt during the 2026-27 season
articles.body:
For the first time in almost two decades, Crystal Palace will wear a white home shirt for the duration of the 2026-27 Premier League season.

Traditionally, the Eagles have worn a blue and red strip. White is also a colour associated with the club, and while it is often a secondary tone in home shirts across the past 40 years, it has frequently featured as the primary shade on away and alternate jerseys.

But Palace have this year opted to wear a white home strip. It includes a blue and a red sash diagonally across the chest, in keeping with the club's traditional colours.

Palace say that the kit is a nod to their shirt worn 50 years ago. Having featured a sash during their run to the semi-finals of the FA Cup in 1976, the following season saw the club implement the shirt for the duration of the campaign.

Following that initial use, the white strip with a blue and red sash was worn frequently by the club during the early 1980s.

The strip also contains the use of Palace's former circular badge, worn by the club between 1973 and 1987.

Palace wore the shirt for the first time competitively in their 2-0 away defeat to Everton on the opening fixture of the season.

Pierre Sage's side will wear the shirt at Selhurst Park for the first time on Friday night when they host Manchester City in their first home match of the campaign.

The last time Palace wore a white shirt as their home kit was during the 2008-09 season, which the club spent in the Championship.

articles.title: Islam Makhachev makes bold Alexander Volkanovski prediction as Movsar Evloev prepares for UFC 333 title fight
articles.summary: International Sports News: Islam Makhachev has made a clear pick for the Alexander Volkanovski vs. Movsar Evloev title fight, and it may surprise some UFC fans. The UFC welterwe.
articles.body: Islam Makhachev has made a clear pick for the Alexander Volkanovski vs. Movsar Evloev title fight, and it may surprise some UFC fans. The UFC welterweight champion believes Evloevâs youth could help him beat Volkanovski at UFC 333. Makhachev also feels the Australian is no longer at the same peak he reached a few years ago, even though he still sees him as one of the best fighters in the sport.Islam Makhachev predicts Movsar Evloev can beat Alexander VolkanovskiVolkanovski and Evloev will meet for the UFC featherweight title on October 24 at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. The UFC has officially confirmed the fight as the main event of UFC 333. Volkanovski enters the bout as champion, while Evloev is still unbeaten with a 20-0 record.Makhachev knows what Volkanovski brings because the two have already fought twice. Their first meeting came at UFC 284, where Makhachev won a close decision. He then stopped Volkanovski with a head kick in the first round of their rematch at UFC 294.Now, despite those wins, Makhachev is not picking his former opponent to keep the featherweight belt.Speaking to reporters in Russia, Makhachev backed Evloev and pointed to the age gap between the two fighters.âItâs no secret and he himself knows that the fight wonât be easy, that Volkanovski is a tough opponent for anyone. But I think Movsar will manage with his youth. Volkanovski, honestly speaking, is not at the same peak he was a couple of years ago. Even though he is still one of the best fighters. I think itâll be a very competitive fight but I hope Movsar will do his job.âSherdog reported Makhachevâs prediction on August 25.The prediction is interesting because Makhachev did not dismiss Volkanovski. Instead, he pointed to something that could matter over five rounds: whether the 37-year-old champion can still perform at the level he showed during his best years.Evloev, meanwhile, has built an unbeaten record and earned his first UFC title shot. The UFCâs official event listing identifies him as the No. 1-ranked contender going into the fight.Alexander Volkanovski reveals what could happen after Movsar Evloev fightThere is another reason this title fight has extra weight for Volkanovski. The champion recently admitted that a very bad performance against Evloev could make him think about retirement.Volkanovski told 10 News that he has no plans to retire right now. However, he said the result and the damage from the fight could affect what he decides next.âIf things go terribly wrong, alright, weâre done. If things go very well, like the last one, no damage, go through, alright, weâll keep it rolling. Taking each fight as it goes, just trying to be real with it. But I donât have plans on retiring right now. Moneyâs always good.â MMA Fighting reported his comments.That puts more focus on what happens when Volkanovski faces the undefeated Evloev. Makhachev expects the younger challenger to take advantage, while Volkanovski is preparing to show that he still has enough to stay on top.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Luke Littler suffers Players Championship 27 quarter-final exit with loss to eventual winner Jermaine Wattimena
articles.summary: Luke Littler has won every major on PDC circuit so far in 2026 in bid for historic clean sweep; world No 1 must finish in top 64 of Players Championship Order of Merit in order to qualify for Finals in November; 19-year-old lost 6-5 to eventual PC27 winner Jermaine Wattimena in last eight
articles.body:
Luke Littler's bid to qualify for the Players Championship Finals, and keep alive his hopes of claiming a historic clean sweep of PDC major titles in 2026, suffered a blow with a quarter-final exit at PC27.

Littler was beaten 6-5 by Jermaine Wattimena in a final-leg decider, with the Dutchman going on to take the title in Leicester, overcoming countryman Kevin Doets 8-6 in the final.

Littler beat Archie Self 6-2, Arno Merk 6-3 and then William O'Connor 6-3 to set up a last-16 tie with Chris Dobey, who he thrashed 6-0, before losing out to eventual champion Wattimena.

  • Darts in 2026: Key dates, calendar, results 📅
  • Got Sky? Watch on the Sky Sports app📱
  • Not got Sky? Get instant access with NOW 📺

The world No 1 has won every major title on the PDC circuit so far in 2026 - the World Championship, Masters, UK Open, Premier League, World Cup of Darts and World Matchplay.

He still needs to win the World Series, World Grand Prix, European Championship, Grand Slam of Darts and Players Championship Finals this season in order to achieve something no-one has ever managed in the sport.

Can Littler still qualify for Players Championship Finals?

The major obstacle standing in the way of a Littler clean sweep is that only the top 64 in the Players Championship Order of Merit make it through to the finals in Minehead in November, with the projected cut-off expected to be over £30,000 in earnings.

The winner of each Players Championship event scoops up £15,000 but Littler was able to secure only £4,000 by reaching the quarter-finals on his season-debut outing.

The 19-year-old opted out of the first 26 events before entering PC27 and 28 in Leicester, meaning he needs to have strong showings in the final seven scheduled floor events to stand a chance of qualifying.

PC28 on Wednesday, also being held at the Mattioli Arena in Leicester, gives him another opportunity to claim a tournament win and boost his finals hopes.

How Wattimena stormed to PC27 title

Wattimena fended off a late fightback Doets to clinch his third PDC ranking title with victory in the Players Championship 27 showpiece on Tuesday.

Following his dramatic, first career win against Littler, sealed with a clutch 115 checkout on tops in a last-leg decider, Wattimena produced further heroics in his semi-final against Luke Woodhouse, reeling off six straight legs from 4-1 down, aided by an astonishing flurry of five ton-plus finishes.

Wattimena converted 136, 135, 115, 127 and 128 outshots to complete the comeback, before winning six straight legs against Doets to power into a commanding 6-2 lead.

Doets responded by winning four of the next five to threaten an improbable turnaround, only for Wattimena to fire in a brilliant 11-darter en route to victory.

"I played really well today but some games I made difficult for myself," conceded Wattimena, who reclaims a place in the world's top 16 at the expense of Ross Smith.

"I always play really well against Luke to be honest. Even when I lose I play well, and that 115 finish against Luke gave me big confidence.

"I didn't realise I hit five ton-plus finishes in the semi-final because you're busy with the game, but I'm very happy with this win."

Nathan Aspinall was another high-profile name in action, and the Stockport star struck perfection during his opening round tie against Thibault Tricole, before succumbing to Mickey Mansell in round three.

articles.title: Luke Littler's Players Championships finals dented by Jermaine Wattimena defeat
articles.summary: Luke Littler loses to Jermaine Wattimena in the quarter-finals of the 27th Players Championship contest of the year.
articles.body:
Luke Littler's hopes of qualifying for the Players Championship finals in November took a hit as he was defeated by Jermaine Wattimena in the quarter-finals of PC27 in Leicester.

Littler, playing in his first Pro Tour event in 2026, was forced into a last-leg decider, and the Dutchman hit a 115 checkout to claim his first victory in six meetings against Littler on the PDC tour.

The 19-year-old was in a positive mood afterwards though, posting "on the move" on Instagram.

Qualification for November's finals is important for Littler as he aims to complete the calendar sweep of ranking events in 2026.

The top 64 players in the Players Championship qualify for Minehead in November and Littler, who skipped the first 26 events on the circuit, sits in 141st place after claiming Â£4,000 on Tuesday.

There are seven Players Championship events remaining for The Nuke to get in to the top 64 - including one on Wednesday at the same venue.

However, he has previously stated his intention to only feature in the UK events, meaning he would only have three more opportunities to climb up the order of merit.

Littler is currently Â£22,250 behind 64th-placed Mario Vandenbogaerde. Victory at one of the events earns you Â£15,000, while runners-up receive Â£10,000.

He subsequently made his first successful defense against WWE Hall of Famer Rey Mysterio, establishing himself as a fighting champion. Iâm not just talking about âoh, letâs have respectful matches every week and show what we can do and bring value to this title.âHe further stated, âThere are a million ways to bring value to the title, and one of the ways is being a fighting champion against guys who are considered dastardly.
